description: When seawater gets cold, it gets viscous. This fact could explain how single-celled ocean creatures became multicellular when the planet was frozen during “Snowball Earth,” according to experiments.

title: Vacuum of Space to Decay Sooner Than Expected (but Still Not Soon)
description: One of the quantum fields that fills the universe is special because its default value seems poised to eventually change, changing everything.

title: Monumental Proof Settles Geometric Langlands Conjecture
description: In work that has been 30 years in the making, mathematicians have proved a major part of a profound mathematical vision called the Langlands program.

title: What Are Sheaves?
description: These metaphorical gardens have become central objects in modern mathematics.

title: Will AI Ever Have Common Sense?
description: Common sense has been viewed as one of the hardest challenges in AI. That said, ChatGPT4 has acquired what some believe is an impressive sense of humanity. How is this possible? Listen to this week’s “The Joy of Why” with co-host Steven Strogatz.

title: Tight-Knit Microbes Live Together to Make a Vital Nutrient
description: At sea, biologists discovered microbial partners that together produce nitrogen, a nutrient essential for life. The pair are in the process of merging into a single organism.

title: ‘Sensational’ Proof Delivers New Insights Into Prime Numbers
description: The proof creates stricter limits on potential exceptions to the famous Riemann hypothesis.

title: What Could Explain the Gallium Anomaly?
description: Physicists have ruled out a mundane explanation for the strange findings of an old Soviet experiment, leaving open the possibility that the results point to a new fundamental particle.

title: How America’s Fastest Swimmers Use Math to Win Gold
description: Number theorist Ken Ono is teaching Olympians to swim more efficiently.

title: What Is Machine Learning?
description: Neural networks and other forms of machine learning ultimately learn by trial and error, one improvement at a time.

title: What Can Tiling Patterns Teach Us?
description: If you cover a surface with tiles, repetitive patterns always emerge — or do they? In this week’s episode, mathematician Natalie Priebe Frank and co-host Janna Levin discuss how recent breakthroughs in tiling can unlock structural secrets in the natural world.

title: With Fifth Busy Beaver, Researchers Approach Computation’s Limits
description: After decades of uncertainty, a motley team of programmers has proved precisely how complicated simple computer programs can get.

title: Tracing the Hidden Hand of Magnetism in the Galaxy
description: Susan Clark is helping to unravel the mysterious workings of the Milky Way’s magnetic field, a critical missing piece of the galactic puzzle.

title: Why Is This Shape So Terrible to Pack?
description: Two mathematicians have proved a long-standing conjecture that is a step on the way toward finding the worst shape for packing the plane.

title: How AI Revolutionized Protein Science, but Didn’t End It
description: Three years ago, Google’s AlphaFold pulled off the biggest artificial intelligence breakthrough in science to date, accelerating molecular research and kindling deep questions about why we do science.

title: The Question of What’s Fair Illuminates the Question of What’s Hard
description: Computational complexity theorists have discovered a surprising new way to understand what makes certain problems hard.

title: How the Square Root of 2 Became a Number
description: Useful mathematical concepts, like the number line, can linger for millennia before they are rigorously defined.

title: How Is Science Even Possible?
description: How are scientists able to crack fundamental questions about nature and life? How does math make the complex cosmos understandable? In this episode, the physicist Nigel Goldenfeld and co-host Steven Strogatz explore the deep foundations of the scientific process.

title: Across a Continent, Trees Sync Their Fruiting to the Sun
description: European beech trees more than 1,500 kilometers apart all drop their fruit at the same time in a grand synchronization event now linked to the summer solstice.

title: The Enduring Mystery of How Water Freezes
description: Making ice requires more than subzero temperatures. The unpredictable process takes microscopic scaffolding, random jiggling and often a little bit of bacteria.

title: The Brainstem Fine-Tunes Inflammation Throughout the Body
description: The evolutionarily ancient part of the brain that controls breathing and heart rate also regulates the immune system — a discovery about the brain-body axis made by experts on taste.

title: Computation Is All Around Us, and You Can See It if You Try
description: Computer scientist Lance Fortnow writes that by embracing the computations that surround us, we can begin to understand and tame our seemingly random world.

title: The New Math of How Large-Scale Order Emerges
description: The puzzle of emergence asks how regularities emerge on macro scales out of uncountable constituent parts. A new framework has researchers hopeful that a solution is near.

title: In Highly Connected Networks, There’s Always a Loop
description: Mathematicians show that graphs of a certain common type must contain a route that visits each point exactly once.

title: Can Psychedelics Improve Mental Health?
description: Research suggests that psychedelic drugs can reopen critical periods of brain development to create opportunities for re-learning and psychological healing. In this episode, co-host Janna Levin speaks with Gül Dölen, a neuroscientist studying the therapeutic potential of psychedelic substances.

title: Most Life on Earth Is Dormant, After Pulling an ‘Emergency Brake’
description: Many microbes and cells are in deep sleep, waiting for the right moment to activate. Biologists discovered a widespread protein that abruptly shuts down a cell’s activity — and turns it back on just as fast.

title: Cryptographers Discover a New Foundation for Quantum Secrecy
description: Researchers have proved that secure quantum encryption is possible in a world without hard problems.

title: Mathematicians Attempt to Glimpse Past the Big Bang
description: By studying the geometry of model space-times, researchers offer alternative views of the universe’s first moments.

title: Physicists Puzzle Over Emergence of Strange Electron Aggregates
description: Electrons have been seen uniting into entities with fractions of electric charge, this time without a magnetic field coaxing them into it.

title: Simple Equation Predicts the Shapes of Carbon-Capturing Wetlands
description: To calculate the amount of carbon stored inside peatlands, researchers developed a unified theory of “bog physics” applicable around the world.

title: The S-Matrix Is the Oracle Physicists Turn To in Times of Crisis
description: Particle physicists in search of the next theory of reality are consulting a mathematical structure that they know will never fail: a table of possibilities known as the S-matrix.

title: What Happens in the Brain to Cause Depression?
description: Drugs that target the neurotransmitter serotonin have long been prescribed to treat depression. Now the spotlight is turning to other aspects of brain chemistry. In this episode, the neuropharmacologist John Krystal shares findings that are overturning our understanding of depression.

title: How Failure Has Made Mathematics Stronger
description: The topologist Danny Calegari discusses the inevitability of disappointment in math, and how to learn from it.

title: Electric ‘Ripples’ in the Resting Brain Tag Memories for Storage
description: New experiments reveal how the brain chooses which memories to save and add credence to advice about the importance of rest.

title: AI Needs Enormous Computing Power. Could Light-Based Chips Help?
description: Optical neural networks, which use photons instead of electrons, have advantages over traditional systems. They also face major obstacles.

title: He Seeks Mystery Magnetic Fields With His Quantum Compass
description: Alex Sushkov is updating an old technology with new quantum tricks in hopes of sensing the magnetic influence of dark matter.

title: Computer Scientists Invent an Efficient New Way to Count
description: By making use of randomness, a team has created a simple algorithm for estimating large numbers of distinct objects in a stream of data.

title: Strangely Curved Shapes Break 50-Year-Old Geometry Conjecture
description: Mathematicians have disproved a major conjecture about the relationship between curvature and shape.

title: How ‘Idle’ Egg Cells Defend Their DNA From Damage
description: How do immature egg cells maintain genetic quality for decades before they mature? Scientists find unusual safeguards in this quiescent cell that may inform research into fertility.

title: Game Theory Can Make AI More Correct and Efficient
description: Researchers are drawing on ideas from game theory to improve large language models and make them more consistent.

title: Will Better Superconductors Transform the World?
description: Scientists are pursuing materials that can conduct electricity with perfect efficiency under ambient conditions. In this episode, the physicist Siddharth Shanker Saxena tells co-host Janna Levin about what makes this hunt so difficult and consequential.

title: New AI Tools Predict How Life’s Building Blocks Assemble
description: Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold3 and other deep learning algorithms can now predict the shapes of interacting complexes of protein, DNA, RNA and other molecules, better capturing cells’ biological landscapes.

title: Dogged Dark Matter Hunters Find New Hiding Places to Check
description: Perhaps dark matter is made of an entirely different kind of particle than the ones physicists have been searching for. New experiments are springing up to look for these ultra-lightweight phantoms.

title: A Rosetta Stone for Mathematics
description: In 1940 André Weil wrote a letter to his sister, Simone, outlining his vision for translating between three distinct areas of mathematics. Eighty years later, it still animates many of the most exciting developments in the field.

title: The Mystery of the Missing Multicellular Prokaryotes
description: Why have bacteria never evolved complex multicellularity? A new hypothesis suggests that it could come down to how prokaryotic genomes respond to a small population size.

title: Scientists Find a Fast Way to Describe Quantum Systems
description: After years of false starts, a team of computer scientists has found a way to efficiently deduce the Hamiltonian of a physical system at any constant temperature.

title: To Pack Spheres Tightly, Mathematicians Throw Them at Random
description: Four mathematicians broke a 75-year-old record by finding a denser way to pack high-dimensional spheres.

title: How a NASA Probe Solved a Scorching Solar Mystery
description: The outer layers of the sun’s atmosphere are a blistering million degrees hotter than its surface. The hidden culprit? Magnetic activity.

title: Does AI Know What an Apple Is? She Aims to Find Out.
description: The computer scientist Ellie Pavlick is translating philosophical concepts such as “meaning” into concrete, testable ideas.

title: What Does Milk Do for Babies?
description: Human nutrition begins with milk, but the wondrous biofluid does much more than feed babies. In this episode, co-host Steven Strogatz speaks with molecular nutritionist Elizabeth Johnson about her research into the impact of human milk on a healthy microbiome.

title: Ecologists Struggle to Get a Grip on ‘Keystone Species’
description: More than 50 years after Bob Paine’s experiment with starfish, hundreds of species have been pronounced “keystones” in their ecosystems. Has the powerful metaphor lost its mathematical meaning?

title: AI Starts to Sift Through String Theory’s Near-Endless Possibilities
description: Using machine learning, string theorists are finally showing how microscopic configurations of extra dimensions translate into sets of elementary particles — though not yet those of our universe.

title: Mathematicians Marvel at ‘Crazy’ Cuts Through Four Dimensions
description: Topologists prove two new results that bring some order to the confoundingly difficult study of four-dimensional shapes.

title: Insects and Other Animals Have Consciousness, Experts Declare
description: A group of prominent biologists and philosophers announced a new consensus: There’s “a realistic possibility” that insects, octopuses, crustaceans, fish and other overlooked animals experience consciousness.

title: Cryptography Tricks Make a Hard Problem a Little Easier
description: Researchers have shown how to find the simplest description of a data set faster than by simply checking every possibility.

title: Hopes of Big Bang Discoveries Ride on a Future Spacecraft
description: Physicists and cosmologists will have a new probe of primordial processes when Europe launches the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) next decade.

title: Pleasure or Pain? He Maps the Neural Circuits That Decide.
description: The work of the neuroscientist Ishmail Abdus-Saboor has opened up a world of insights into precisely how much pleasure and pain animals experience during different forms of touch.

title: Geometers Engineer New Tools to Wrangle Spacecraft Orbits
description: Mathematicians think abstract tools from a field called symplectic geometry might help with planning missions to far-off moons and planets.

title: How Do Machines ‘Grok’ Data?
description: By apparently overtraining them, researchers have seen neural networks discover novel solutions to problems.

title: My Fantastic Voyage at Quanta Magazine
description: Founding editor-in-chief Thomas Lin looks back at a decade of Quanta journalism and forward to what’s next for the magazine.

title: Viruses Finally Reveal Their Complex Social Life
description: New research has uncovered a social world of viruses full of cheating, cooperation and other intrigues, suggesting that viruses make sense only as members of a community.

title: Can Information Escape a Black Hole?
description: Black holes are inescapable traps for most of what falls into them — but there can be exceptions. The theoretical physicist Leonard Susskind speaks with co-host Janna Levin about the black hole information paradox and how it has propelled modern physics.

title: Avi Wigderson, Complexity Theory Pioneer, Wins Turing Award
description: The prolific researcher found deep connections between randomness and computation and spent a career influencing cryptographers, complexity researchers and more.

title: Number of Distances Separating Points Has a New Bound
description: Mathematicians have struggled to prove Falconer’s Conjecture, a simple, but far-reaching, hypothesis about the distances between points. They’re finally getting close.

title: How the Ancient Art of Eclipse Prediction Became an Exact Science
description: The timing of the total eclipse on April 8, 2024, will be known to within a second, thousands of years after fearful humans first started trying to anticipate these cosmic events.

title: Dark Energy May Be Weakening, Major Astrophysics Study Finds
description: A generation of physicists has referred to the dark energy that permeates the universe as “the cosmological constant.” Now the largest map of the cosmos to date hints that this mysterious energy has been changing over billions of years.

title: Overexposure Distorted the Science of Mirror Neurons
description: After a decade out of the spotlight, the brain cells once alleged to explain empathy, autism and theory of mind are being refined and redefined.

title: Merging Fields, Mathematicians Go the Distance on Old Problem
description: Mathematicians have illuminated what sets of points can look like if the distances between them are all whole numbers.

title: The Social Benefits of Getting Our Brains in Sync
description: Our brain waves can align when we work and play closely together. The phenomenon, known as interbrain synchrony, suggests that collaboration is biological.

title: How Is Flocking Like Computing?
description: Birds flock. Locusts swarm. Fish school. From chaotic assemblies of life, order somehow emerges. In this episode, co-host Steven Strogatz interviews the evolutionary ecologist Iain Couzin about how and why collective behaviors arise.

title: The Researcher Who Explores Computation by Conjuring New Worlds
description: Russell Impagliazzo studies hard problems, the limits of cryptography, the nature of randomness and more.

title: Topologists Tackle the Trouble With Poll Placement
description: Mathematicians are using topological abstractions to find places where it’s hard to vote.

title: The Best Qubits for Quantum Computing Might Just Be Atoms
description: In the search for the most scalable hardware to use for quantum computers, qubits made of individual atoms are having a breakout moment.

title: Math That Connects Where We’re Going to Where We’ve Been
description: Recursion builds bridges between ideas from across different math classes and illustrates the power of creative mathematical thinking.

title: How Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Helps Neural Networks Compute
description: Large language models do better at solving problems when they show their work. Researchers are beginning to understand why.

title: Michel Talagrand Wins Abel Prize for Work Wrangling Randomness
description: The French mathematician spent decades developing a set of tools now widely used for taming random processes.

title: Doubts Grow About the Biosignature Approach to Alien-Hunting
description: Recent controversies bode ill for the effort to detect life on other planets by analyzing the gases in their atmospheres.

title: Brain’s ‘Background Noise’ May Explain Value of Shock Therapy
description: Electroconvulsive therapy is highly effective in treating major depressive disorder, but no one knows why it works. New research suggests it may restore balance between excitation and inhibition in the brain.

title: Swirling Forces, Crushing Pressures Measured in the Proton
description: Long-anticipated experiments that use light to mimic gravity are revealing the distribution of energies, forces and pressures inside a subatomic particle for the first time.

title: What Is Quantum Teleportation?
description: Teleporting people through space is still science fiction. But quantum teleportation is dramatically different and entirely real. In this episode, Janna Levin interviews the theoretical physicist John Preskill about teleporting bits and the promise of quantum technology.

title: ‘The Rest of the World Disappears’: Claire Voisin on Mathematical Creativity
description: The recipient of the 2024 Crafoord Prize in Mathematics discusses math as art, math as language, and math as abstract thought.

title: Physicists Finally Find a Problem That Only Quantum Computers Can Do
description: Researchers have shown that a problem relating to the energy of a quantum system is easy for quantum computers but hard for classical ones.

title: Tiny Tweaks to Neurons Can Rewire Animal Motion
description: Altering a protein in the neurons that coordinate a rattlesnake’s movement made a slow slither neuron more like a speedy rattle neuron, showing one way evolution can generate new ways of moving.

title: New Breakthrough Brings Matrix Multiplication Closer to Ideal
description: By eliminating a hidden inefficiency, computer scientists have come up with a new way to multiply large matrices that’s faster than ever.

title: Cellular Self-Destruction May Be Ancient. But Why?
description: How did cells evolve a process to end their own lives? Recent research suggests that apoptosis, a form of programmed cell death, first arose billions of years ago in bacteria with a primitive sociality.

title: Elliptic Curve ‘Murmurations’ Found With AI Take Flight
description: Mathematicians are working to fully explain unusual behaviors uncovered using artificial intelligence.

title: Fresh X-Rays Reveal a Universe as Clumpy as Cosmology Predicts
description: By mapping the largest structures in the universe in X-rays, cosmologists have found striking agreement with their standard theoretical model of how the universe evolves.

title: Mollusk Eyes Reveal How Future Evolution Depends on the Past
description: The visual systems of an obscure group of mollusks provide a rare natural example of path-dependent evolution, in which a critical fork in the creatures’ past determined their evolutionary futures.

title: What Is the Nature of Time?
description: Time is all around us: in the language we use, in the memories we revisit and in our predictions of the future. But what exactly is it? The physicist and Nobel laureate Frank Wilczek joins Steve Strogatz to discuss the fundamental hallmarks of time.

title: How Selective Forgetting Can Help AI Learn Better
description: Erasing key information during training results in machine learning models that can learn new languages faster and more easily.

title: ‘Entropy Bagels’ and Other Complex Structures Emerge From Simple Rules
description: Simple rules in simple settings continue to puzzle mathematicians, even as they devise intricate tools to analyze them.

title: A Quantum Trick Implied Eternal Stability. Now the Idea May Be Falling Apart.
description: A series of advances seemed to promise the impossible: the existence of quantum states that would never, ever fall into disarray. But physicists are now discovering that the pull of disorder may not be so easily overcome.

title: Never-Repeating Tiles Can Safeguard Quantum Information
description: Two researchers have proved that Penrose tilings, famous patterns that never repeat, are mathematically equivalent to a kind of quantum error correction.

title: A New Agenda for Low-Dimensional Topology
description: This past October, dozens of mathematicians gathered in Pasadena to create the third version of “Kirby’s list” — a compendium of the most important unsolved problems in the field.

title: A Multitalented Scientist Seeks the Origins of Multicellularity
description: The pathbreaking geneticist Cassandra Extavour pursues the secrets of multicellular life while balancing careers in both science and singing.

title: Inside Scientists’ Life-Saving Prediction of the Iceland Eruption
description: The Reykjanes Peninsula has entered a new volcanic era. Innovative efforts to map and monitor the subterranean magma are saving lives.

title: Quanta Relaunches Hyperjumps Math Game
description: Explore a universe of numbers and arithmetic in our new and improved interactive math game, Hyperjumps!

title: Hyperjumps Math Game
description: Play Quanta Magazine’s daily interactive math game, Hyperjumps!

title: Unfolding the Mysteries of Polygonal Billiards
description: The surprisingly subtle geometry of a familiar game shows how quickly math gets complicated.

title: How Did Altruism Evolve?
description: If evolution favors the survival of the fittest, where did the impulse to help others come from? Host Janna Levin speaks with Stephanie Preston, a neuropsychologist who studies the biology of altruism.

title: A ‘Lobby’ Where a Molecule Mob Tells Genes What to Do
description: Highly repetitive regions of junk DNA may be the key to a newly discovered mechanism for gene regulation.

title: How Quickly Do Large Language Models Learn Unexpected Skills?
description: A new study suggests that so-called emergent abilities actually develop gradually and predictably, depending on how you measure them.

title: To See Black Holes in Stunning Detail, She Uses ‘Echoes’ Like a Bat
description: The astrophysicist Erin Kara measures time lags in black holes’ X-ray glows, which reveal the complexity of the objects’ closest surroundings.

title: Scientists Find Optimal Balance of Data Storage and Time
description: Seventy years after the invention of a data structure called a hash table, theoreticians have found the most efficient possible configuration for it.

title: Maze Proof Establishes a ‘Backbone’ for Statistical Mechanics
description: Four mathematicians have estimated the chances that there’s a clear path through a random maze.

title: Radio Maps May Reveal the Universe’s Biggest Magnetic Fields
description: A controversial technique has produced detailed maps of the magnetic fields in colossal galaxy clusters. If confirmed, the approach could be used to reveal where cosmic magnetic fields come from.

title: What Your Brain Is Doing When You’re Not Doing Anything
description: When your mind is wandering, your brain’s “default mode” network is active. Its discovery 20 years ago inspired a raft of research into networks of brain regions and how they interact with each other.

title: In a ‘Dark Dimension,’ Physicists Search for the Universe’s Missing Matter
description: An idea derived from string theory suggests that dark matter is hiding in a (relatively) large extra dimension. The theory makes testable predictions that physicists are investigating now.

title: What Makes for ‘Good’ Mathematics?
description: Terence Tao, who has been called the “Mozart of Mathematics,” wrote an essay in 2007 about the common ingredients in “good” mathematical research. In this episode, the Fields Medalist joins Steven Strogatz to revisit the topic.

title: Plants Find Light Using Gaps Between Their Cells
description: A mutant seedling revealed how plant tissues scatter incoming light, allowing plants to sense its direction and move toward it.

title: How to Build an Origami Computer
description: Two mathematicians have shown that origami can, in principle, be used to perform any possible computation.

title: Researchers Approach New Speed Limit for Seminal Problem
description: Integer linear programming can help find the answer to a variety of real-world problems. Now researchers have found a much faster way to do it.

title: The Quest to Decode the Mandelbrot Set, Math’s Famed Fractal
description: For decades, a small group of mathematicians has patiently unraveled the mystery of what was once math’s most popular picture. Their story shows how technology transforms even the most abstract mathematical landscapes.

title: The Surprisingly Simple Math Behind Puzzling Matchups
description: If Anna beats Benji in a game and Benji beats Carl, will Anna beat Carl?

title: Why Locusts Swarm, Humans Do Good and Time Marches On
description: The Joy of Why podcast returns for a third season, with two co-hosts, 24 brilliant guests and 24 all-new episodes.

title: The Best Neighborhoods for Starting a Life in the Galaxy
description: Some neighborhoods in the Milky Way may be better suited for making habitable planets than others.

title: The Brain Region That Controls Movement Also Guides Feelings
description: The cerebellum is responsible for far more than coordinating movement. New techniques reveal that it is, in fact, a hub of sensory and emotional processing in the brain.

title: New Theory Suggests Chatbots Can Understand Text
description: Far from being “stochastic parrots,” the biggest large language models seem to learn enough skills to understand the words they’re processing.

title: Clashing Cosmic Numbers Challenge Our Best Theory of the Universe
description: As measurements of distant stars and galaxies become more precise, cosmologists are struggling to make sense of sparring values.

title: Math’s ‘Game of Life’ Reveals Long-Sought Repeating Patterns
description: John Conway’s Game of Life, a famous cellular automaton, has been found to have periodic patterns of every possible length.

title: The Quest for Simple Rules to Build a Microbial Community
description: Microbiologists are searching for a universal theory of how bacteria form communities based not on their species but on the roles they play.

title: How to Guarantee the Safety of Autonomous Vehicles
description: As computer-driven cars and planes become more common, the key to preventing accidents, researchers show, is to know what you don’t know.

title: The Mathematician Who Finds the Poetry in Math and the Math in Poetry
description: The links between math, music and art have been explored for thousands of years. Sarah Hart is now turning a mathematical eye to literature.

title: New Kind of Magnetism Spotted in an Engineered Material
description: In an atomically thin stack of semiconductors, a mechanism unseen in any natural substance causes electrons’ spins to align.

title: ‘Magical’ Error Correction Scheme Proved Inherently Inefficient
description: Locally correctable codes need barely any information to fix errors, but they’re extremely long. Now we know that the simplest versions can’t get any shorter.

title: Cells Across the Body Talk to Each Other About Aging
description: Biologists discovered that mitochondria in different tissues talk to each other to repair injured cells. When their signal fails, the biological clock starts winding down.

title: Mathematicians Identify the Best Versions of Iconic Shapes
description: Researchers are discovering the shortest knots and fattest Möbius strips, among other “optimal shapes.”

title: Deep Beneath Earth’s Surface, Clues to Life’s Origins
description: Last spring, scientists retrieved a trove of mantle rocks from underneath the Atlantic seafloor — a bounty that could help write the first chapter of life's story on Earth.

title: The ‘Accidental Activist’ Who Changed the Face of Mathematics
description: Throughout her 60-year career, Lenore Blum has developed new perspectives on logic and computation while championing women in mathematics and computer science. Now consciousness is on her mind.

title: Evolution: Fast or Slow? Lizards Help Resolve a Paradox.
description: Why does natural selection appear to happen slowly on long timescales and quickly on short ones? A multigenerational study of four lizard species addresses biology’s “paradox of stasis.”

title: The Year in Math
description: Landmark results in Ramsey theory and a remarkably simple aperiodic tile capped a year of mathematical delight and discovery.

title: The Year in Physics
description: From the smallest scales to the largest, the physical world provided no shortage of surprises this year.

title: The Year in Computer Science
description: Artificial intelligence learned how to generate text and art better than ever before, while computer scientists developed algorithms that solved long-standing problems.

title: New Clues for What Will Happen When the Sun Eats the Earth
description: Recent observations of an aging, alien planetary system are helping to answer the question: What will happen to our planet when the sun dies?

title: The Year in Biology
description: In a year packed with fascinating discoveries, biologists pushed the limits of synthetic life, probed how organisms keep time, and refined theories about consciousness and emotional health.

title: How This Marine Worm Can Tell Moonglow From Sunbeams
description: For the first time, scientists have decoded the molecular structure of a protein that helps to sync a biological clock to the phases of the moon.

title: A Close-Up View Reveals the ‘Melting’ Point of an Infinite Graph
description: Just as ice melts to water, graphs undergo phase transitions. Two mathematicians showed that they can pinpoint such transitions by examining only local structure.

title: Celebrated Cryptography Algorithm Gets an Upgrade
description: Two researchers have improved a well-known technique for lattice basis reduction, opening up new avenues for practical experiments in cryptography and mathematics.

title: New Cell Atlases Reveal Untold Variety in the Brain and Beyond
description: Recent efforts to map every cell in the human body have researchers floored by unfathomable diversity, with many thousands of subtly different types of cells in the human brain alone.

title: A Triplet Tree Forms One of the Most Beautiful Structures in Math
description: The Markov numbers reveal the secrets of irrational numbers and the patterns of the Fibonacci sequence. But there’s one question about them that has resisted proof for over a century.

title: Extra-Long Blasts Challenge Our Theories of Cosmic Cataclysms
description: Astronomers thought they had solved the mystery of gamma-ray bursts. A few recent events suggest otherwise.

title: She Studies How Addiction Hijacks Learning in the Brain
description: Erin Calipari works to understand how drugs like opioids and cocaine alter learning circuits and neurochemistry in one of the country's epicenters of substance use disorder and addiction.

title: ‘A-Team’ of Math Proves a Critical Link Between Addition and Sets
description: A team of four prominent mathematicians, including two Fields medalists, proved a conjecture described as a “holy grail of additive combinatorics.”

title: The (Often) Overlooked Experiment That Revealed the Quantum World
description: A century ago, the Stern-Gerlach experiment established the truth of quantum mechanics. Now it’s being used to probe the clash of quantum theory and gravity.

title: An Easy-Sounding Problem Yields Numbers Too Big for Our Universe
description: Researchers prove that navigating certain systems of vectors is among the most complex computational problems.

title: A Century Later, New Math Smooths Out General Relativity
description: Mathematicians prove a theorem that illuminates the geometry of universes with tiny amounts of mass.

title: The New Quest to Control Evolution
description: Modern scientists aren’t content with predicting how life evolves. They want to shape it.

title: Evolving Bacteria Can Evade Barriers to ‘Peak’ Fitness
description: Paradoxically, natural selection can sometimes seem to block organisms from evolving useful adaptations. But a new study of “fitness landscapes” and antibiotic resistance in bacteria shows that life still finds a way.

title: Meet Strange Metals: Where Electricity May Flow Without Electrons
description: For 50 years, physicists have understood current as a flow of charged particles. But a new experiment has found that in at least one strange material, this understanding falls apart.

title: Pierre de Fermat’s Link to a High School Student’s Prime Math Proof
description: How Fermat’s less famous "little theorem" got mathematicians young and old to play with prime-like Carmichael numbers.

title: In the Gut’s ‘Second Brain,’ Key Agents of Health Emerge
description: Sitting alongside the neurons in your enteric nervous system are underappreciated glial cells, which play key roles in digestion and disease that scientists are only just starting to understand.

title: Researchers Refute a Widespread Belief About Online Algorithms
description: Three computer scientists have disproved a long-standing conjecture about a fundamental problem involving imperfect information.

title: The Astonishing Behavior of Recursive Sequences
description: Some strange mathematical sequences are always whole numbers — until they’re not. The puzzling patterns have revealed ties to graph theory and prime numbers, awing mathematicians.

title: AI System Beats Chess Puzzles With ‘Artificial Brainstorming’
description: By bringing together disparate approaches, machines can reach a new level of creative problem-solving.

title: During Pregnancy, a Fake ‘Infection’ Protects the Fetus
description: Cells in the placenta have an unusual trick for activating gentle immune defenses and keeping them turned on when no infection is present. It involves crafting and deploying a fake virus.

title: Rogue Worlds Throw Planetary Ideas Out of Orbit
description: Scientists have recently discovered scores of free-floating worlds that defy classification. The new observations have forced them to rethink their theories of star and planet formation.

title: Why the Human Brain Perceives Small Numbers Better
description: The discovery that the brain has different systems for representing small and large numbers provokes new questions about memory, attention and mathematics.

title: The Scientist Who Decodes the Songs of Undersea Volcanoes
description: In the rumbles and groans of underwater volcanoes, Jackie Caplan-Auerbach finds her favorite harmonies — and clues to the Earth’s interior.

title: In the ‘Wild West’ of Geometry, Mathematicians Redefine the Sphere
description: High-dimensional spheres can have a much wider variety of structures than mathematicians thought possible.

title: Cryptographers Solve Decades-Old Privacy Problem
description: Three researchers have found a long-sought way to pull information from large databases secretly, moving us closer to fully private internet searches.

title: These Moons Are Dark and Frozen. So How Can They Have Oceans?
description: The moons orbiting Jupiter and Saturn appear to have subsurface oceans — tantalizing targets in the search for life beyond Earth. But it’s not clear why these seas exist at all.

title: The Hidden Connection That Changed Number Theory
description: Quadratic reciprocity lurks around many corners in mathematics. By proving it, number theorists reimagined their whole field.

title: Bats Use the Same Brain Cells to Map Physical and Social Worlds
description: New research in social bats raises the intriguing possibility that evolution can reprogram the brain’s “place cells,” which are typically associated with location, to encode all kinds of environmental information.

title: A Brief History of Tricky Mathematical Tiling
description: The discovery earlier this year of the “hat” tile marked the culmination of hundreds of years of work into tiles and their symmetries.

title: A New Generation of Mathematicians Pushes Prime Number Barriers
description: New work attacks a long-standing barrier to understanding how prime numbers are distributed.

title: Biophysicists Uncover Powerful Symmetries in Living Tissue
description: After identifying interlocking symmetries in mammalian cells, scientists can describe some tissues as liquid crystals — an observation that lays the groundwork for a fluid-dynamic theory of how tissues move.

title: The Computing Pioneer Helping AI See
description: Alexei Efros has spent his career learning how machines see differently from humans. Now he’s helping to bridge the gap.

title: Fossilized Molecules Reveal a Lost World of Ancient Life
description: A new analysis of ancient sediments fills a gap in the fossil record — revealing a massive dynasty of ancient eukaryotes, which may have reigned for 800 million years and shaped the history of life of Earth.

title: The Quest to Quantify Quantumness
description: What makes a quantum computer more powerful than a classical computer? It’s a surprisingly subtle question that physicists are still grappling with, decades into the quantum age.

title: These Cells Spark Electricity in the Brain. They’re Not Neurons.
description: For decades, researchers have debated whether brain cells called astrocytes can signal like neurons. Researchers recently published the best evidence yet that some astrocytes are part of the electrical conversation.

title: Thirty Years Later, a Speed Boost for Quantum Factoring
description: Shor’s algorithm will enable future quantum computers to factor large numbers quickly, undermining many online security protocols. Now a researcher has shown how to do it even faster.

title: The Mathematician Who Sculpted the Shape of Space
description: Eugenio Calabi, who died on September 25, conceived of novel geometric objects that later became fundamental to string theory.

title: Echoes of Electromagnetism Found in Number Theory
description: A new magnum opus posits the existence of a hidden mathematical link akin to the connection between electricity and magnetism.

title: The Deep Link Equating Math Proofs and Computer Programs
description: Mathematical logic and the code of computer programs are, in an exact way, mirror images of each other.

title: In Our Cellular Clocks, She’s Found a Lifetime of Discoveries
description: For decades, Carrie Partch has led pioneering structural research on the protein clockwork that keeps time for our circadian rhythm. Is time still on her side?

title: Invisible ‘Demon’ Discovered in Odd Superconductor
description: Physicists have long suspected that hunks of metal could vibrate in a peculiar way that would be all but invisible. Now physicists have spotted these “demon modes.”

title: Tiny Language Models Come of Age
description: To better understand how neural networks learn to simulate writing, researchers trained simpler versions on synthetic children’s stories.

title: Nobel Prize Honors Inventors of ‘Quantum Dot’ Nanoparticles
description: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to three researchers who harnessed the quantum behaviors of semiconductor nanocrystals.

title: Physicists Who Explored Tiny Glimpses of Time Win Nobel Prize
description: The development of attosecond pulses of light allowed researchers to explore the frame-by-frame movement of electrons.

title: Nobel Prize Awarded to mRNA Vaccine Scientists
description: Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman have been awarded the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries leading to mRNA vaccines, such as those that protect against Covid-19.

title: How Simple Math Moves the Needle
description: The spatial intuition behind a three-point turn offers an on-ramp to a century-old geometry problem.

title: In the Milky Way’s Stars, a History of Violence
description: Our galaxy's stars keep a record of its past. By reading those stories, astronomers are learning more about how the Milky Way came to be — and about the galaxy we live in today.

title: How Many Microbes Does It Take to Make You Sick?
description: Exposure to a virus isn’t an all-or-nothing proposition. The concept of “infectious dose” suggests ways to keep ourselves safer from harm.

title: To Defend the Genome, These Cells Destroy Their Own DNA
description: Under a microscope, cells in a worm embryo deliberately eliminated one-third of their genome — an uncompromising tactic that may combat harmful genetic parasites.

title: Mathematicians Cross the Line to Get to the Point
description: A new paper establishes a long-conjectured bound about the size of the overlap between sets of lines and points.

title: Behold Modular Forms, the ‘Fifth Fundamental Operation’ of Math
description: Modular forms are one of the most beautiful and mysterious objects in mathematics. What are they?

title: The Experimental Cosmologist Hunting for the First Sunrise
description: To catch even a whiff of the universe’s earliest epochs — an age of darkness, and one of new light — Cynthia Chiang builds her own equipment. Then she deploys it at the ends of the Earth.

title: The Physical Process That Powers a New Type of Generative AI
description: Some modern image generators rely on the principles of diffusion to create images. Alternatives based on the process behind the distribution of charged particles may yield even better results.

title: What Makes Life Tick? Mitochondria May Keep Time for Cells
description: Every species develops at its own unique tempo, leaving scientists to wonder what governs their timing. A suite of new findings suggests that cells use basic metabolic processes as clocks.

title: Machine Learning Aids Classical Modeling of Quantum Systems
description: By using “classical shadows,” ordinary computers can beat quantum computers at the tricky task of understanding quantum behaviors.

title: ‘Species Repulsion’ Enables High Biodiversity in Tropical Trees
description: Because tree seedlings don’t grow as well when close to their parents, more tree species can be packed into tropical forests.

title: A Tower of Conjectures That Rests Upon a Needle
description: On its surface, the Kakeya conjecture is a simple statement about rotating needles. But it underlies a wealth of mathematics.

title: Physicists Observe ‘Unobservable’ Quantum Phase Transition
description: Measurement and entanglement both have a “spooky” nonlocal flavor to them. Now physicists are harnessing that nonlocality to probe the spread of quantum information and control it.

title: The Biggest Smallest Triangle Just Got Smaller
description: A new proof breaks a decades-long drought of progress on the problem of estimating the size of triangles created by cramming points into a square.

title: How Scientists Are Tackling the Tricky Task of Solar Cycle Prediction
description: Scientists have struggled to accurately forecast the strength of the sun’s 11-year cycle — even after centuries of solar observations.

title: Magnetism May Have Given Life Its Molecular Asymmetry
description: The preferred “handedness” of biomolecules could have emerged from biased interactions between electrons and magnetic surfaces, new research suggests.

title: Alan Turing and the Power of Negative Thinking
description: Mathematical proofs based on a technique called diagonalization can be relentlessly contrarian, but they help reveal the limits of algorithms.

title: Why Mathematical Proof Is a Social Compact
description: Number theorist Andrew Granville on what mathematics really is — and why objectivity is never quite within reach.

title: The Usefulness of a Memory Guides Where the Brain Saves It
description: New research finds that the memories useful for future generalizations are held in the brain separately from those recording unusual events.

title: In a Monster Star’s Light, a Hint of Darkness
description: Astronomers are scouring the cosmos for fingerprints of the invisible — tiny clumps of pure dark matter that might solve a long-standing cosmic mystery.

title: The Hidden Brain Connections Between Our Hands and Tongues
description: Sticking out your tongue while doing delicate work with your hands reveals a history of evolutionary relationships.

title: New Codes Could Make Quantum Computing 10 Times More Efficient
description: Quantum computing is still really, really hard. But the rise of a powerful class of error-correcting codes suggests that the task might be slightly more feasible than many feared.

title: What a Contest of Consciousness Theories Really Proved
description: A five-year “adversarial collaboration” of consciousness theorists led to a stagy showdown in front of an audience. It crowned no winners — but it can still claim progress.

title: The AI Tools Making Images Look Better
description: Researchers have discovered ways around a fundamental trade-off between accuracy and beauty in digital images.

title: An Old Conjecture Falls, Making Spheres a Lot More Complicated
description: The telescope conjecture gave mathematicians a handle on ways to map one sphere to another. Now that it has been disproved, the universe of shapes has exploded.

title: Quaking Giants Might Solve the Mysteries of Stellar Magnetism
description: In their jiggles and shakes, red giant stars encode a record of the magnetic fields near their cores.

title: Complexity Theory’s 50-Year Journey to the Limits of Knowledge
description: How hard is it to prove that problems are hard to solve? Meta-complexity theorists have been asking questions like this for decades. A string of recent results has started to deliver answers.

title: Math Proof Draws New Boundaries Around Black Hole Formation
description: For a half century, mathematicians have tried to define the exact circumstances under which a black hole is destined to exist. A new proof shows how a cube can help answer the question.

title: Andreas Wagner Pursues the Secrets to Evolutionary Success
description: Why did mammals, grasses and some other groups of organisms explode in diversity only after millions of years? The evolutionary biologist Andreas Wagner plumbs the secrets of those “sleeping beauties.”

title: JWST Spots Giant Black Holes All Over the Early Universe
description: Giant black holes were supposed to be bit players in the early cosmic story. But recent James Webb Space Telescope observations are finding an unexpected abundance of the beasts.

title: Risky Giant Steps Can Solve Optimization Problems Faster
description: New results break with decades of conventional wisdom for the gradient descent algorithm.

title: Two Students Unravel a Widely Believed Math Conjecture
description: Mathematicians thought they were on the cusp of proving a conjecture about the ancient structures known as Apollonian circles. But a summer project would lead to its downfall.

title: Even Synthetic Life Forms With a Tiny Genome Can Evolve
description: By watching “minimal” cells regain the fitness they lost, researchers are testing whether a genome can be too simple to evolve.

title: Exoplanets Could Help Us Learn How Planets Make Magnetism
description: New observations of a faraway rocky world that might have its own magnetic field could help astronomers understand the seemingly haphazard magnetic fields swaddling our solar system’s planets.

title: Selfish, Virus-Like DNA Can Carry Genes Between Species
description: Genetic elements called Mavericks that have some viral features could be responsible for the large-scale smuggling of DNA between species.

title: Quantum Complexity Shows How to Escape Hawking’s Black Hole Paradox
description: Inside of a black hole, the two theoretical pillars of 20th-century physics appear to clash. Now a group of young physicists think they have resolved the conflict by appealing to the central pillar of the new century — the physics of quantum information.

title: Ninth Dedekind Number Found by Two Independent Groups
description: The numbers count a variety of seemingly unrelated mathematical structures.

title: How Genetic Surprises Complicate the Old Doctrine of DNA
description: For over a century, biologists have had to contend with a complicated picture of genetics, which they’ve only recently begun to understand.

title: The Cryptographer Who Ensures We Can Trust Our Computers
description: Yael Tauman Kalai’s breakthroughs secure our digital world, from cloud computing to our quantum future.

title: Does Nothingness Exist?
description: Even empty space bubbles with energy, according to quantum mechanics — and that fact affects almost every facet of physical reality. The theoretical physicist Isabel Garcia Garcia explains to Steven Strogatz why it’s so important in modern physics to understand what a true vacuum is.

title: Why Insect Memories May Not Survive Metamorphosis
description: The reshuffling of neurons during fruit fly metamorphosis suggests that larval memories don’t persist in adults.

title: How (Nearly) Nothing Might Solve Cosmology’s Biggest Questions
description: By measuring the universe’s emptiest spaces, scientists can study how matter clumps together and how fast it flies apart.

title: New Proof Shows That ‘Expander’ Graphs Synchronize
description: The proof establishes new conditions that cause connected oscillators to sway in sync.

title: Math That Lets You Think Locally but Act Globally
description: Knowing a little about the local connections on flight maps and other networks can reveal a lot about a system’s global structure.

title: To Move Fast, Quantum Maze Solvers Must Forget the Past
description: Quantum algorithms can find their way out of mazes exponentially faster than classical ones, at the cost of forgetting the path they took. A new result suggests that the trade-off may be inevitable.

title: Mathematicians Solve Long-Standing Coloring Problem
description: A new result shows how much of the plane can be colored by points that are never exactly one unit apart.

title: How Quantum Physicists Explained Earth’s Oscillating Weather Patterns
description: By treating Earth as a topological insulator — a state of quantum matter — physicists found a powerful explanation for the movements of the planet’s air and seas.

title: Underground Cells Make ‘Dark Oxygen’ Without Light
description: In some deep subterranean aquifers, cells have a chemical trick for making oxygen that could sustain whole underground ecosystems.

title: How to Build a Big Prime Number
description: A new algorithm brings together the advantages of randomness and deterministic processes to reliably construct large prime numbers.

title: Can Math and Physics Save an Arrhythmic Heart?
description: Abnormal waves of electrical activity can cause a heart’s muscle cells to beat out of sync. In this episode, Flavio Fenton, an expert in cardiac dynamics, talks with Steve Strogatz about ways to treat heart arrhythmias without resorting to painful defibrillators.

title: In a Fierce Desert, Microbe ‘Crusts’ Show How Life Tamed the Land
description: Extreme microorganisms carpeting the Atacama Desert in Chile illuminate how life might have first taken hold on Earth’s surface.

title: New Proof Threads the Needle on a Sticky Geometry Problem
description: A new proof marks major progress toward solving the Kakeya conjecture, a deceptively simple question that underpins a tower of conjectures.

title: The Physicist Who’s Challenging the Quantum Orthodoxy
description: For decades, physicists have struggled to develop a quantum theory of gravity. But what if gravity — and space-time — are fundamentally classical?

title: The Lawlessness of Large Numbers
description: Mathematicians can often figure out what happens as quantities grow infinitely large. What about when they are just a little big?

title: Elliptic Curves Yield Their Secrets in a New Number System
description: Ana Caraiani and James Newton have extended an important result in number theory to the imaginary realm.

title: Microbes Gained Photosynthesis Superpowers From a ‘Proton Pump’
description: New research reveals how marine microbes use an extra membrane that once had digestive functions to boost their yield from photosynthesis.

title: A New Map of the Universe, Painted With Cosmic Neutrinos
description: Physicists finally know where at least some of these high-energy particles come from, which helps make the neutrinos useful for exploring fundamental physics.

title: An Enormous Gravity ‘Hum’ Moves Through the Universe
description: Astronomers have found a background din of exceptionally long-wavelength gravitational waves pervading the cosmos.

title: What Can Jellyfish Teach Us About Fluid Dynamics?
description: Jellyfish and other aquatic creatures embody solutions to diverse problems in engineering, medicine and mathematics. John Dabiri, a fluid dynamics expert, talks with Steven Strogatz about what jellyfish can teach us about going with the flow.

title: How Math Achieved Transcendence
description: Transcendental numbers include famous examples like e and π, but it took mathematicians centuries to understand them.

title: The Key to Species Diversity May Be in Their Similarities
description: New modeling work suggests why nature is more diverse than niche-based ecological theory predicts.

title: Computer Scientists Inch Closer to Major Algorithmic Goal
description: A new paper finds a faster method for determining when two mathematical groups are the same.

title: Mathematicians Discover Novel Way to Predict Structure in Graphs
description: Mathematicians probe the limits of randomness in new work estimating quantities called Ramsey numbers.

title: The Simple Geometry That Predicts Molecular Mosaics
description: By treating molecules as geometric tessellations, scientists devised a new way to forecast how 2D materials might self-assemble.

title: How the Brain Protects Itself From Blood-Borne Threats
description: To buffer the brain against menaces in the blood, a dynamic, multi-tiered system of protection is built into the brain’s blood vessels.

title: Neural Networks Need Data to Learn. Even If It’s Fake.
description: Real data can be hard to get, so researchers are turning to synthetic data to train their artificial intelligence systems.

title: Flow Proof Helps Mathematicians Find Stability in Chaos
description: A series of new papers describes how to fully characterize key dynamical systems with relatively little data.

title: What Causes Giant Rogue Waves?
description: Wave-science researcher Ton van den Bremer and Steven Strogatz discuss how rogue waves can form in relatively calm seas and whether their threat can be predicted.

title: ‘Embryo Models’ Challenge Legal, Ethical and Biological Concepts
description: With embryolike constructs built entirely from stem cells, researchers can revolutionize our understanding of development. But how close to an embryo is too close?

title: A New Experiment Casts Doubt on the Leading Theory of the Nucleus
description: By measuring inflated helium nuclei, physicists have challenged our best understanding of the force that binds protons and neutrons.

title: Sparse Networks Come to the Aid of Big Physics
description: A novel type of neural network is helping physicists with the daunting challenge of data analysis.

title: An Explorer of Abyssal Depths Looks to Oceans on Other Worlds
description: The marine geochemist Chris German brings decades of experience studying seafloor hydrothermal vents to NASA’s preparations for visits to other ocean worlds in our solar system.

title: In New Paradox, Black Holes Appear to Evade Heat Death
description: The puzzling behavior of black hole interiors has led researchers to propose a new physical law: the second law of quantum complexity.

title: First-Year Graduate Student Finds Paradoxical Set
description: No two pairs have the same sum; add three numbers together, and you can get any whole number.

title: How Math Has Changed the Shape of Gerrymandering
description: New tools make it possible to detect hidden manipulation of maps.

title: What Is the Nature of Consciousness?
description: Consciousness, our experience of being in the world, is one of the mind’s greatest mysteries, but as the neuroscientist Anil Seth explains to Steven Strogatz, research is making progress in understanding this elusive phenomenon.

title: Data Compression Drives the Internet. Here’s How It Works.
description: One student’s desire to get out of a final exam led to the ubiquitous algorithm that shrinks data without sacrificing information.

title: How 3D Changes in the Genome Turned Sharks Into Skates
description: Changes in the 3D structure of their genome gave skates and rays their distinctive winglike fins and pancake flatness.

title: The Physicist Who Glues Together Universes
description: Renate Loll has helped pioneer a radically new approach to quantum gravity. She assumes that the fabric of space-time is a blend of all possible fabrics, and she has developed the computational tools needed to calculate the far-reaching implications of that assumption.

title: Is It Real or Imagined? How Your Brain Tells the Difference.
description: New experiments show that the brain distinguishes between perceived and imagined mental images by checking whether they cross a “reality threshold.”

title: Math Patterns That Go On Forever but Never Repeat
description: Simple math can help explain the complexities of the newly discovered aperiodic monotile.

title: Some Neural Networks Learn Language Like Humans
description: Researchers uncover striking parallels in the ways that humans and machine learning models acquire language skills.

title: Secret Messages Can Hide in AI-Generated Media
description: In steganography, an ordinary message masks the presence of a secret communication. Humans can never do it perfectly, but a new study shows it’s possible for machines.

title: Are There Reasons to Believe in a Multiverse?
description: Several areas of physics suggest reasons to think that unobservable universes with different natural laws could lie beyond ours. The theoretical physicist David Kaplan talks with Steven Strogatz about the mysteries that a multiverse would solve.

title: Memories Help Brains Recognize New Events Worth Remembering
description: Memories may affect how well the brain will learn about future events by shifting our perceptions of the world.

title: New Proof Finds the ‘Ultimate Instability’ in a Solar System Model
description: For the first time, mathematicians have proved that planetary orbits in a solar system will always be unstable.

title: The Tiny Physics Behind Immense Cosmic Eruptions
description: A new theory describes how particle interactions fuel fast magnetic reconnection, the process behind solar flares and other astrophysical jets.

title: Chatbots Don’t Know What Stuff Isn’t
description: Today’s language models are more sophisticated than ever, but they still struggle with the concept of negation. That’s unlikely to change anytime soon.

title: A Plan to Address the World’s Challenges With Math
description: Minhyong Kim is leading a new initiative called Mathematics for Humanity that encourages mathematicians to apply their skills to solving social problems.

title: Physicists Create Elusive Particles That Remember Their Pasts
description: In two landmark experiments, researchers used quantum processors to engineer exotic particles that have captivated physicists for decades. The work is a step toward crash-proof quantum computers.

title: A Mutation Turned Ants Into Parasites in One Generation
description: A new genetics study of ant “social parasites” shows how complex sets of features can emerge rapidly and potentially split species.

title: A New Idea for How to Assemble Life
description: If we want to understand complex constructions, such as ourselves, assembly theory says we must account for the entire history of how such entities came to be.

title: Is Perpetual Motion Possible at the Quantum Level?
description: A new phase of matter called a “time crystal” plays with our expectations of thermodynamics. The physicist Vedika Khemani talks with Steven Strogatz about its surprising quantum behavior.

title: The Most Important Machine That Was Never Built
description: When he invented Turing machines in 1936, Alan Turing also invented modern computing.

title: A Very Big Small Leap Forward in Graph Theory
description: Four mathematicians have found a new upper limit to the “Ramsey number,” a crucial property describing unavoidable structure in graphs.

title: How a Human Smell Receptor Works Is Finally Revealed
description: After decades of frustration, researchers have determined how an airborne scent molecule links to a human smell receptor.

title: The Computer Scientist Peering Inside AI’s Black Boxes
description: Cynthia Rudin wants machine learning models, responsible for increasingly important decisions, to show their work.

title: Why Mathematicians Re-Prove What They Already Know
description: It’s been known for thousands of years that the primes go on forever, but new proofs give fresh insights into how theorems depend on one another.

title: How Pools of Genetic Diversity Affect a Species’ Fate
description: A new, deeper understanding of how the breeding structure of species affects their genetic diversity is giving conservationists better tools for saving animals.

title: Tiny Jets on the Sun Power the Colossal Solar Wind
description: A new analysis argues that ubiquitous eruptions in the sun’s corona explain the vast flow of charged particles seen streaming out through the solar system.

title: The Number 15 Describes the Secret Limit of an Infinite Grid
description: The “packing coloring” problem asks how many numbers are needed to fill an infinite grid so that identical numbers never get too close to one another. A new computer-assisted proof finds a surprisingly straightforward answer.

title: Why the Brain’s Connections to the Body Are Crisscrossed
description: In all bilaterally symmetrical animals, from humans down to simple worms, nerves cross from one side of the body to the opposite side of the brain. Geometry may explain why.

title: How Can Some Infinities Be Bigger Than Others?
description: All infinities go on forever, so how is it possible for some infinities to be larger than others? The mathematician Justin Moore discusses the mysteries of infinity with Steven Strogatz.

title: A New Kind of Symmetry Shakes Up Physics
description: So-called “higher symmetries” are illuminating everything from particle decays to the behavior of complex quantum systems.

title: She Tracks the DNA of Elusive Species That Hide in Harsh Places
description: On Mount Everest and in the Peruvian Andes, Tracie Seimon uses DNA to study how species and ecosystems respond to climate change, pathogens and other influences.

title: A New Approach to Computation Reimagines Artificial Intelligence
description: By imbuing enormous vectors with semantic meaning, we can get machines to reason more abstractly — and efficiently — than before.

title: Mathematicians Find Hidden Structure in a Common Type of Space
description: In 50 years of searching, mathematicians found only one example of a “subspace design” in a vector space. A new proof reveals that there are infinitely more out there.

title: Primitive Asgard Cells Show Life on the Brink of Complexity
description: As researchers race to cultivate more of the intriguing cells from the deep seafloor, the few cells now growing in labs are giving us our best glimpses of the forerunners of all complex life.

title: The Electron Is So Round That It’s Ruling Out Potential New Particles
description: If the electron’s charge wasn’t perfectly round, it could reveal the existence of hidden particles. A new measurement approaches perfection.

title: How to Tame the Endless Infinities Hiding in the Heart of Particle Physics
description: In the math of particle physics, every calculation should result in infinity. The set of techniques known as “resurgence” points toward an escape.

title: Animal Mutation Rates Reveal Traits That Speed Evolution
description: The first large-scale comparison of mutation rates gives insights into how quickly species can evolve.

title: What Has the Pandemic Taught Us About Vaccines?
description: Should Covid-19 vaccines be judged by how well they prevent disease or how well they prevent death? Anna Durbin, a public health expert and vaccine researcher, talks with Steven Strogatz about the science behind vaccines.

title: Hobbyist Finds Math’s Elusive ‘Einstein’ Tile
description: The surprisingly simple tile is the first single, connected tile that can fill the entire plane in a pattern that never repeats — and can’t be made to fill it in a repeating way.

title: How Randomness Improves Algorithms
description: Unpredictability can help computer scientists solve otherwise intractable problems.

title: How a DNA ‘Parasite’ May Have Fragmented Our Genes
description: A novel type of “jumping gene” may explain why the genomes of complex cells aren’t all equally stuffed with noncoding sequences.

title: The Colorful Problem That Has Long Frustrated Mathematicians
description: The four-color problem is simple to explain, but its complex proof continues to be both celebrated and despised.

title: Astronomers Dig Up the Stars That Birthed the Milky Way
description: There once was a cosmic seed that sprouted the Milky Way galaxy. Astronomers have discovered its last surviving remnants.

title: Emmy Murphy Is a Mathematician Who Finds Beauty in Flexibility
description: The prize-winning geometer feels most fulfilled when exploring the fertile ground where constraint meets creation.

title: The Symmetry That Makes Solving Math Equations Easy
description: Learn why the quadratic formula works and why quadratics are easier to solve than cubics.

title: Wormhole Experiment Called Into Question
description: Last fall, a team of physicists announced that they had teleported a qubit through a holographic wormhole in a quantum computer. Now another group suggests that’s not quite what happened.

title: Bob Metcalfe, Ethernet Pioneer, Wins Turing Award
description: The American researcher was recognized for his central role in inventing, standardizing and commercializing the ubiquitous networking technology.

title: Is There Math Beyond the Equal Sign?
description: Can mathematics handle things that are essentially the same without being exactly equal? Category theorist Eugenia Cheng and host Steven Strogatz discuss the power and pleasures of abstraction.

title: Surprise Computer Science Proof Stuns Mathematicians
description: For decades, mathematicians have been inching forward on a problem about which sets contain evenly spaced patterns of three numbers. Last month, two computer scientists blew past all of those results.

title: Dinosaur Bone Study Reveals That Not All Giants Grew Alike
description: A survey of prehistoric bones reveals that T. rex and some of its cousins had more than one way to reach enormous sizes. Evolution may have preserved that variation in modern animals too.

title: The Unpredictable Abilities Emerging From Large AI Models
description: Large language models like ChatGPT are now big enough that they’ve started to display startling, unpredictable behaviors.

title: Coloring by Numbers Reveals Arithmetic Patterns in Fractions
description: In a recent paper, two mathematicians showed that a particular pattern is unavoidable when fractions are categorized.

title: Global Microbiome Study Gives New View of Shared Health Risks
description: The most comprehensive survey of how we share our microbiomes suggests a new way of thinking about the risks of developing some diseases that aren’t usually considered contagious.

title: Shadows in the Big Bang Afterglow Reveal Invisible Cosmic Structures
description: Cosmologists are using secondary signatures from the cosmic microwave background to map the universe’s hidden matter.

title: The Researcher Who Would Teach Machines to Be Fair
description: Arvind Narayanan uses quantitative methods to expose and correct the misuse of quantitative methods.

title: New Proof Distinguishes Mysterious and Powerful ‘Modular Forms’
description: Using “refreshingly old” tools, mathematicians resolved a 50-year-old conjecture about how to categorize important functions called modular forms, with consequences for number theory and theoretical physics.

title: Can We Program Our Cells?
description: By genetically instructing cells to perform tasks that they wouldn’t in nature, synthetic biologists can learn deep secrets about how life works. Steven Strogatz discusses the potential of this young field with researcher Michael Elowitz.

title: Room-Temperature Superconductor Discovery Meets With Resistance
description: A paper in Nature reports the discovery of a superconductor that operates at room temperatures and near-room pressures. The claim has divided the research community.

title: Black Holes Will Eventually Destroy All Quantum States, Researchers Argue
description: New calculations suggest that the event horizons around black holes will ‘decohere’ quantum possibilities — even those that are far away.

title: Simpler Math Predicts How Close Ecosystems Are to Collapse
description: By replacing thousands of equations with just one, ecology modelers can more accurately assess how close fragile environments are to a disastrous “tipping point.”

title: In Neural Networks, Unbreakable Locks Can Hide Invisible Doors
description: Cryptographers have shown how perfect security can undermine machine learning models.

title: An Applied Mathematician With an Unexpected Toolbox
description: Lek-Heng Lim uses tools from algebra, geometry and topology to answer questions in machine learning.

title: How Loneliness Reshapes the Brain
description: Feelings of loneliness prompt changes in the brain that further isolate people from social contact.

title: Strange Solar Gamma Rays Discovered at Even Higher Energies
description: There appear to be too many gamma rays coming from the sun. New higher-energy measurements reveal that this excess continues for a bit, then disappears — a cutoff that could help clarify what’s going on.

title: Can Our Brains Be Taken Over?
description: Several real-life pathogens can change a host’s behavior against their will. Here’s what we know about these zombie-like infections.

title: Physicists Use Quantum Mechanics to Pull Energy out of Nothing
description: The quantum energy teleportation protocol was proposed in 2008 and largely ignored. Now two independent experiments have shown that it works.

title: How Will the Universe End?
description: Big Freeze, Big Rip, Big Crunch, Bounce or vacuum decay? Steven Strogatz speaks with theoretical cosmologist Katie Mack about the five ways that scientists think the universe could come to an end.

title: With Nothing to Eat Except Viruses, Some Microbes Thrive
description: “Virovores” — organisms that survive and multiply by eating viruses — might influence the flow of energy through ecosystems.

title: Quantum Field Theory Pries Open Mathematical Puzzle
description: Mathematicians have struggled to understand the moduli space of graphs. A new paper uses tools from physics to peek inside.

title: To Teach Computers Math, Researchers Merge AI Approaches
description: Large language models still struggle with basic reasoning tasks. Two new papers that apply machine learning to math provide a blueprint for how that could change.

title: Gene Expression in Neurons Solves a Brain Evolution Puzzle
description: The neocortex of our brain is the seat of our intellect. New data suggests that mammals created it with new types of cells that they developed only after their evolutionary split from reptiles.

title: She Studies Growing Arteries to Aid Heart Attack Recovery
description: Regenerative medicine researcher Kristy Red Horse’s discoveries may someday help damaged hearts heal better. Her stewardship of her Native American heritage may advance science in other ways too.

title: Mathematicians Complete Quest to Build ‘Spherical Cubes’
description: Is it possible to fill space “cubically” with shapes that act like spheres? A proof at the intersection of geometry and theoretical computer science says yes.

title: The Joy of Asking About Infinity, Jellyfish and the End of the Universe
description: As The Joy of Why podcast returns for a second season, producer Polly Stryker and host Steven Strogatz invite listeners to join them and their brilliant new guests on another voyage of discovery.

title: What Lights the Universe’s Standard Candles?
description: Type Ia supernovas are astronomers’ best tools for measuring cosmic distances. In a first, researchers have managed to re-create one on a supercomputer, giving a boost to a leading hypothesis for how they form.

title: Researchers Discover a More Flexible Approach to Machine Learning
description: “Liquid” neural nets, based on a worm’s nervous system, can transform their underlying algorithms on the fly, giving them unprecedented speed and adaptability.

title: How Our Reality May Be a Sum of All Possible Realities
description: Richard Feynman’s path integral is both a powerful prediction machine and a philosophy about how the world is. But physicists are still struggling to figure out how to use it, and what it means.

title: Mathematicians Eliminate Long-Standing Threat to Knot Conjecture
description: A new proof shows that a knot some thought would contradict the famed slice-ribbon conjecture doesn’t.

title: Machines Learn Better if We Teach Them the Basics
description: A wave of research improves reinforcement learning algorithms by pre-training them as if they were human.

title: When Does the Brain Operate at Peak Performance?
description: The critical brain hypothesis suggests that neural networks do their best work when connections are not too weak or too strong.

title: Astronomers Say They Have Spotted the Universe’s First Stars
description: Theory has it that “Population III” stars brought light to the cosmos. The James Webb Space Telescope may have just glimpsed them.

title: How Quantum Physicists ‘Flipped Time’ (and How They Didn’t)
description: Two teams have made photons act as if time were simultaneously flowing in two directions. The experiments demonstrate a way to potentially boost the performance of quantum devices.

title: The Cause of Depression Is Probably Not What You Think
description: Depression has often been blamed on low levels of serotonin in the brain. That answer is insufficient, but alternatives are coming into view and changing our understanding of the disease.

title: The Computer Scientist Who Finds Life Lessons in Games
description: In Shang-Hua Teng’s work, theoretical and practical questions have long been intertwined. Now he’s turning his focus to the impractical.

title: Mathematicians Find an Infinity of Possible Black Hole Shapes
description: In three-dimensional space, the surface of a black hole must be a sphere. But a new result shows that in higher dimensions, an infinite number of configurations are possible.

title: The Basic Algebra Behind Secret Codes and Space Communication
description: Whether you’re passing secret notes in class or downloading images from a space probe, Reed-Solomon codes offer an ingenious way to embed information and correct for errors.

title: Standard Model of Cosmology Survives a Telescope’s Surprising Finds
description: Reports that the James Webb Space Telescope killed the reigning cosmological model turn out to have been exaggerated. But astronomers still have much to learn from distant galaxies glimpsed by Webb.

title: Mathematicians Roll Dice and Get Rock-Paper-Scissors
description: Mathematicians have uncovered a surprising wealth of rock-paper-scissors-like patterns in randomly chosen dice.

title: Finally, a Fast Algorithm for Shortest Paths on Negative Graphs
description: Researchers can now find the shortest route through a network nearly as fast as theoretically possible, even when some steps can cancel out others.

title: Mobile Genes From the Mother Shape the Baby’s Microbiome
description: Tiny genetic sequences in a mother’s bacteria seem to hop into the infant's bacteria, perhaps ensuring a healthy microbiome later in life.

title: Probability and Number Theory Collide — in a Moment
description: Mathematicians are taking ideas developed to study random numbers and applying them to a broad range of categories.

title: Starfish Whisperer Develops a Physical Language of Life
description: Nikta Fakhri is adapting and extending concepts from physics to describe how tiny biological components give rise to living organisms.

title: Ants Live 10 Times Longer by Altering Their Insulin Responses
description: Queen ants live far longer than genetically identical workers. Researchers are learning what their longevity secrets could mean for aging in other species.

title: New Algorithm Closes Quantum Supremacy Window
description: Random circuit sampling, a popular technique for showing the power of quantum computers, doesn’t scale up if errors go unchecked.

title: The Physics Principle That Inspired Modern AI Art
description: Diffusion models generate incredible images by learning to reverse the process that, among other things, causes ink to spread through water.

title: Inside Ancient Asteroids, Gamma Rays Made Building Blocks of Life
description: A new radiation-based mechanism adds to the ways that amino acids could have been made in space and brought to the young Earth.

title: Google Researcher, Long Out of Math, Cracks Devilish Problem About Sets
description: On nights and weekends, Justin Gilmer attacked an old question in pure math using the tools of information theory.

title: The Year in Comments
