description: While the internet is awash in the noise of unmoderated comments, Quanta has attempted to provide a quiet, information-rich spot where readers, listeners and viewers can contemplate the complexity of nature.

title: The Year in Math
description: Four Fields Medals were awarded for major breakthroughs in geometry, combinatorics, statistical physics and number theory, even as mathematicians continued to wrestle with how computers are changing the discipline.

title: The Year in Physics
description: In a year filled with sweet new observations in astronomy and tantalizing breakthroughs in condensed matter physics, the brand-new space telescope takes the cake.

title: The Year in Computer Science
description: Computer scientists this year learned how to transmit perfect secrets, why transformers seem so good at everything, and how to improve on decades-old algorithms (with a little help from AI).

title: The Year in Biology
description: Momentum for new ideas in Alzheimer’s research joined advances in neuroscience, developmental biology and origin-of-life studies to make 2022 a memorable year of biological insights.

title: ‘Fullertubes’ Join the Family of Carbon Crystals
description: The buckminsterfullerene revolution never came, but some researchers are eagerly exploring the properties of newfound carbon crystals known as fullertubes.

title: She Finds Keys to Ecology in Cells That Steal From Others
description: The ecologist Holly Moeller studies microorganisms that expand their range by absorbing organelles and gaining new metabolic talents from their prey.

title: ‘Nasty’ Geometry Breaks Decades-Old Tiling Conjecture
description: Mathematicians predicted that if they imposed enough restrictions on how a shape might tile space, they could force a periodic pattern to emerge. But they were wrong.

title: How the Brain Distinguishes Memories From Perceptions
description: The neural representations of a perceived image and the memory of it are almost the same. New work shows how and why they are different.

title: What Does It Mean to Align AI With Human Values?
description: Making sure our machines understand the intent behind our instructions is an important problem that requires understanding intelligence itself.

title: She Turns Fluids Into ‘Black Holes’ and ‘Inflating Universes’
description: By using fluids to model inaccessible realms of the cosmos, Silke Weinfurtner is “looking for a deeper truth beyond one system.” But what can such experiments teach us?

title: What Causes Alzheimer’s? Scientists Are Rethinking the Answer. (Pt. 2)
description: If plaques of amyloid protein in the brain aren’t the root cause of Alzheimer’s disease, what is?

title: What Causes Alzheimer’s? Scientists Are Rethinking the Answer.
description: After decades in the shadow of the reigning model for Alzheimer’s disease, alternative explanations are finally getting the attention they deserve.

title: After a Quantum Clobbering, One Approach Survives Unscathed
description: A quantum approach to data analysis that relies on the study of shapes will likely remain an example of a quantum advantage — albeit for increasingly unlikely scenarios.

title: From Systems in Motion, Infinite Patterns Appear
description: Mathematicians are finding inevitable structures in sufficiently large sets of integers.

title: Asymmetry Detected in the Distribution of Galaxies
description: Two new studies suggest that certain tetrahedral arrangements of galaxies outnumber their mirror images, potentially reflecting details of the universe’s birth. But confirmation is needed.

title: The Math Behind Wordle Guesses
description: Wordle is a word game. But you can use math to optimize your chances of winning (without cheating).

title: Crucial Computer Program for Particle Physics at Risk of Obsolescence
description: Maintenance of the software that’s used for the hardest physics calculations rests almost entirely with a retiree. The situation reveals the problematic incentive structure of academia.

title: Physicists Create a Holographic Wormhole Using a Quantum Computer
description: The unprecedented experiment explores the possibility that space-time somehow emerges from quantum information.

title: Mathematical Trio Advances Centuries-Old Number Theory Problem
description: The work — the first-ever limit on how many whole numbers can be written as the sum of two cubed fractions — makes significant headway on “a recurring embarrassment for number theorists.”

title: The Brain Uses Calculus to Control Fast Movements
description: Researchers discover that to sharpen its control over precision maneuvers, the brain uses comparisons between control signals — not the signals themselves.

title: AI Reveals New Possibilities in Matrix Multiplication
description: Inspired by the results of a game-playing neural network, mathematicians have been making unexpected advances on an age-old math problem.

title: A Mathematician Dancing Between Algebra and Geometry
description: Wei Ho, the first director of the Women and Mathematics program at the Institute for Advanced Study, combines algebra and geometry in her work on an ancient class of curves.

title: The Simple Geometry Behind Brownie Bake Offs and Equal Areas
description: Proving that two polygons have the same area can be as easy as cutting them up and rearranging the pieces.

title: Why This Universe? A New Calculation Suggests Our Cosmos Is Typical.
description: Two physicists have calculated that the universe has a higher entropy — and is therefore more likely — than alternative possible universes.

title: Computer Proof ‘Blows Up’ Centuries-Old Fluid Equations
description: For more than 250 years, mathematicians have wondered if the Euler equations might sometimes fail to describe a fluid’s flow. A new computer-assisted proof marks a major breakthrough in that quest.

title: The Gut Microbiome Helps Social Skills Develop in the Brain
description: New research in fish suggests that gut microbes can have a crucial early influence on the brain’s social development.

title: How to Think About Relativity
description: Albert Einstein’s ideas about space-time aren’t exactly intuitive, and they aren’t exactly Einstein’s, either.

title: New Chip Expands the Possibilities for AI
description: An energy-efficient chip called NeuRRAM fixes an old design flaw to run large-scale AI algorithms on smaller devices, reaching the same accuracy as wasteful digital computers.

title: Cryptography’s Future Will Be Quantum-Safe. Here’s How It Will Work.
description: Lattice cryptography promises to protect secrets from the attacks of far-future quantum computers.

title: How Supergenes Fuel Evolution Despite Harmful Mutations
description: Supergenes that lock inherited traits together are widespread in nature. Recent work shows that their blend of genetic benefits and risks for species can be complex.

title: The Enduring Mystery of the Dragonfly 44 Galaxy
description: A growing catalog of huge but dim galaxies such as Dragonfly 44 is forcing astronomers to invent new theories of galactic evolution.

title: A Dream of Discovering Alien Life Finds New Hope
description: For Lisa Kaltenegger and her generation of exoplanet astronomers, decades of planning have set the stage for an epochal detection.

title: Ocean Bacteria Reveal an Unexpected Multicellular Form
description: Marine bacteria normally seen as single cells join together as a “microscopic snow globe” to consume bulky floating carbohydrates.

title: A Mathematician Who Fled to Freedom but Still Stares Down Doubts
description: Svetlana Jitomirskaya was born in Ukraine, but left the Soviet Union to escape sexism and antisemitism. Even though her work in mathematical physics has now been honored with one of the field’s top prizes, she finds herself still fighting old battles.

title: Why Mathematicians Study Knots
description: Far from being an abstract mathematical curiosity, knot theory has driven many findings in math and beyond.

title: How Genes Can Leap From Snakes to Frogs in Madagascar
description: The discovery of a hot spot for horizontal gene transfer draws attention to the possible roles of parasites and ecology in such changes.

title: Brightest-Ever Space Explosion Reveals Possible Hints of Dark Matter
description: A recent gamma-ray burst known as the BOAT — “brightest of all time” — appears to have produced a high-energy particle that shouldn’t exist. For some, dark matter provides the explanation.

title: How to Win at Wordle (Without Cheating)
description: Solve these puzzle questions to level up your Wordle game.

title: New Entanglement Results Hint at Better Quantum Codes
description: A team of physicists has entangled three photons over a considerable distance, which could lead to more powerful quantum cryptography.

title: Experiments Spell Doom for Decades-Old Explanation of Quantum Weirdness
description: Physical-collapse theories have long offered a natural solution to the central mystery of the quantum world. But a series of increasingly precise experiments are making them untenable.

title: Inside the Proton, the ‘Most Complicated Thing You Could Possibly Imagine’
description: The positively charged particle at the heart of the atom is an object of unspeakable complexity, one that changes its appearance depending on how it is probed.

title: The Computer Scientist Who’s Boosting Privacy on the Internet
description: Harry Halpin wants our internet conversations to be more private. He’s helped create a new kind of network that might make it possible.

title: Mathematicians Discover the Fibonacci Numbers Hiding in Strange Spaces
description: Recent explorations of unique geometric worlds reveal perplexing patterns, including the Fibonacci sequence and the golden ratio.

title: Teenager Solves Stubborn Riddle About Prime Number Look-Alikes
description: In his senior year of high school, Daniel Larsen proved a key theorem about Carmichael numbers — strange entities that mimic the primes.

title: Human Brains Are Hard to Study. He Grows Useful Substitutes.
description: With stem cell technology and lab-grown brain organoids, Sergiu Paşca seeks the causes of autism and other neuropsychiatric conditions.

title: Lab-Grown Human Cells Form Working Circuits in Rat Brains
description: Letting human brain organoids grow in animal brains could be an ethical new option for experimental studies of neurological disorders.

title: How Do You Prove a Secret?
description: Zero-knowledge proofs allow researchers to prove their knowledge without divulging the knowledge itself.

title: Machine Learning Highlights a Hidden Order in Scents
description: Efforts to build a better digital “nose” suggest that our perception of scents reflects both the structure of aromatic molecules and the metabolic processes that make them.

title: ‘Monumental’ Math Proof Solves Triple Bubble Problem and More
description: The decades-old Sullivan’s conjecture, about the best way to minimize the surface area of a bubble cluster, was thought to be out of reach for three bubbles and up — until a new breakthrough result.

title: Molecule-Building Innovators Win Nobel Prize in Chemistry
description: The chemists Carolyn Bertozzi, Morten Meldal and K. Barry Sharpless were recognized for their development of click chemistry and bioorthogonal chemistry.

title: Pioneering Quantum Physicists Win Nobel Prize in Physics
description: Alain Aspect, John Clauser and Anton Zeilinger have won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics for groundbreaking experiments with entangled particles.

title: Geneticist Awarded Nobel Prize for Studies of Extinct Human Ancestors
description: Svante Pääbo has been awarded the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for studying our extinct ancestors’ DNA.

title: How Star Trek ’s Lieutenant Uhura Overcame Astronomical Odds
description: Readers rescued a Star Trek crew from a probabilistic predicament armed only with the power of mathematical reasoning.

title: What We Know About Monkeypox
description: Even though we’ve learned a lot about this relative of smallpox, some mysteries remain due to a lack of political will.

title: Biologists Use Genetic Circuits to Program Plant Roots
description: Using inserted genetic circuitry, synthetic biologists controlled the growth of plant roots for the first time.

title: How Big Is Infinity?
description: Of all the endless questions children and mathematicians have asked about infinity, one of the biggest has to do with its size.

title: Physicists Rewrite a Quantum Rule That Clashes With Our Universe
description: The past and the future are tightly linked in conventional quantum mechanics. Perhaps too tightly. A tweak to the theory could let quantum possibilities increase as space expands.

title: The New Math of Wrinkling
description: A comprehensive mathematical framework treats wrinkling patterns as elegant solutions to geometric problems.

title: High-Temperature Superconductivity Understood at Last
description: A new atomic-scale experiment all but settles the origin of the strong form of superconductivity seen in cuprate crystals, confirming a 35-year-old theory.

title: How Do Fireflies Flash in Sync? Studies Suggest a New Answer.
description: Field research suggests a new explanation for the synchronized flashing in fireflies and confirms that a novel form of “chimeric” synchrony occurs naturally.

title: How Mathematical Curves Enable Advanced Communication
description: A simple geometric idea has been used to power advances in information theory, cryptography and even blockchain technology.

title: Chaos Researchers Can Now Predict Perilous Points of No Return
description: A custom-built machine learning algorithm can predict when a complex system is about to switch to a wildly different mode of behavior.

title: Record-Breaking Robot Highlights How Animals Excel at Jumping
description: Robots can surpass the limitations on how high and far animals can jump, but their success only underscores nature’s ingenuity in making the most of what’s available.

title: The Math Evangelist Who Preaches Problem-Solving
description: Richard Rusczyk, founder of Art of Problem Solving, has a vision for bringing “joyous, beautiful math” — and problem-solving — to classrooms everywhere.

title: How Transformers Seem to Mimic Parts of the Brain
description: Neural networks originally designed for language processing turn out to be great models of how our brains understand places.

title: A Black Hole’s Orbiting Ring of Light Could Encrypt Its Inner Secrets
description: Physicists have discovered that the ring of photons orbiting a black hole exhibits a special kind of symmetry, hinting at a deeper meaning.

title: A Good Memory or a Bad One? One Brain Molecule Decides.
description: When the brain encodes memories as positive or negative, one molecule determines which way they will go.

title: How Shannon Entropy Imposes Fundamental Limits on Communication
description: What’s a message, really? Claude Shannon recognized that the elemental ingredient is surprise.

title: Webb Space Telescope Snaps Its First Photo of an Exoplanet
description: The grainy image of a “super-Jupiter” is a sign of what’s to come as the telescope’s exoplanet observations ramp up.

title: How Isaac Newton Discovered the Binomial Power Series
description: Rethinking questions and chasing patterns led Newton to find the connection between curves and infinite sums.

title: The AI Researcher Giving Her Field Its Bitter Medicine
description: Anima Anandkumar wants computer scientists to move beyond the matrix, among other challenges.

title: Bacteria’s Immune Sensors Reveal a Novel Way to Detect Viruses
description: A new study reveals that bacteria can fight viruses in a surprisingly elegant way that has no known counterpart in more complex life.

title: Old Problem About Mathematical Curves Falls to Young Couple
description: Eric Larson and Isabel Vogt have solved the interpolation problem — a centuries-old question about some of the most basic objects in geometry. Some credit goes to the chalkboard in their living room.

title: Why and How Do We Dream?
description: Dreams are subjective, but there are ways to peer into the minds of people while they are dreaming. Steven Strogatz speaks with sleep researcher Antonio Zadra about how new experimental methods have changed our understanding of dreams.

title: ‘Post-Quantum’ Cryptography Scheme Is Cracked on a Laptop
description: Two researchers have broken an encryption protocol that many saw as a promising defense against the power of quantum computing.

title: What Drives Galaxies? The Milky Way’s Black Hole May Be the Key.
description: Supermassive black holes have come to the fore as engines of galactic evolution, but new observations of the Milky Way and its central hole don’t yet hang together.

title: Electric Fish Genomes Reveal How Evolution Repeats Itself
description: By studying how electric organs arose in different lineages of fish, scientists gain new insights into a long-standing question of evolutionary biology.

title: Help Star Trek ’s Lieutenant Uhura Overcome Astronomical Odds
description: In honor of the actor and activist Nichelle Nichols, this month’s puzzle imagines a Star Trek adventure in which her character, Lieutenant Uhura, faces a life-and-death conundrum.

title: Epigenetic ‘Clocks’ Predict Animals’ True Biological Age
description: A statistical analysis of chemical tags on DNA may help unify disparate theories of aging.

title: Physics Duo Finds Magic in Two Dimensions
description: In exploring a family of two-dimensional crystals, a husband-and-wife team is uncovering a potent variety of new electron behaviors.

title: A Numerical Mystery From the 19th Century Finally Gets Solved
description: Two mathematicians have proven Patterson’s conjecture, which was designed to explain a strange pattern in sums involving prime numbers.

title: Self-Taught AI Shows Similarities to How the Brain Works
description: Self-supervised learning allows a neural network to figure out for itself what matters. The process might be what makes our own brains so successful.

title: What Is Quantum Field Theory and Why Is It Incomplete?
description: Quantum field theory may be the most successful scientific theory of all time, but there’s reason to think it’s missing something. Steven Strogatz speaks with theoretical physicist David Tong about this enigmatic theory.

title: Mathematicians Crack a Simple but Stubborn Class of Equations
description: Ever since Archimedes, mathematicians have been fascinated by equations that involve a difference between squares. Now two mathematicians have proven how often these equations have solutions, concluding a decades-old quest.

title: How the Physics of Nothing Underlies Everything
description: The key to understanding the origin and fate of the universe may be a more complete understanding of the vacuum.

title: A Biochemist’s View of Life’s Origin Reframes Cancer and Aging
description: The biochemist Nick Lane thinks life first evolved in hydrothermal vents where precursors of metabolism appeared before genetic information. His ideas could lead us to think differently about aging and cancer.

title: At Long Last, Mathematical Proof That Black Holes Are Stable
description: The solutions to Einstein’s equations that describe a spinning black hole won’t blow up, even when poked or prodded.

title: Geometric Analysis Reveals How Birds Mastered Flight
description: Partnerships between engineers and biologists have begun to reveal how birds evolved their superb maneuverability.

title: The Computer Scientist Challenging AI to Learn Better
description: Christopher Kanan is building algorithms that can continuously learn over time — the way we do.

title: Particle Physicists Puzzle Over a New Duality
description: A hidden link has been found between two seemingly unrelated particle collision outcomes. It’s the latest example of a mysterious web of mathematical connections between disparate theories of physics.

title: Seeking Mathematical Truth in Counterfeit Coin Puzzles
description: Readers balanced logical reasoning and mathematical insights to find phony coins with a double-pan balance scale.

title: Neuronal Scaffolding Plays Unexpected Role in Pain
description: Perineuronal nets, rigid structures that hold certain neurons in place, affect a surprising amount of brain activity, including some associated with chronic pain.

title: Why Do We Get Old, and Can Aging Be Reversed?
description: Everybody gets older, but not everyone ages in the same way. In this episode, Steven Strogatz speaks with Judith Campisi and Dena Dubal, two biomedical researchers who study the aging process.

title: Hidden Chaos Found to Lurk in Ecosystems
description: New research finds that chaos plays a bigger role in population dynamics than decades of ecological data seemed to suggest.

title: A Question About a Rotating Line Helps Reveal What Makes Real Numbers Special
description: The Kakeya conjecture predicts how much room you need to point a line in every direction. In one number system after another — with one important exception — mathematicians have been proving it true.

title: Two Weeks In, the Webb Space Telescope Is Reshaping Astronomy
description: In the days after the mega-telescope started delivering data, astronomers reported new discoveries about galaxies, stars, exoplanets and even Jupiter.

title: How Can Infinitely Many Primes Be Infinitely Far Apart?
description: Mathematicians have been studying the distribution of prime numbers for thousands of years. Recent results about a curious kind of prime offer a new take on how spread out they can be.

title: The Astrophysicist Who Sculpts Stars Before They Are Born
description: Nia Imara is working to understand the mysterious clouds of gas and dust that collapse into stars.

title: How the ‘Diamond of the Plant World’ Helped Land Plants Evolve
description: Structural studies of the robust material called sporopollenin reveal how it made plants hardy enough to reproduce on dry land.

title: Computer Science Proof Unveils Unexpected Form of Entanglement
description: Three computer scientists have posted a proof of the NLTS conjecture, showing that systems of entangled particles can remain difficult to analyze even away from extremes.

title: Hypergraphs Reveal Solution to 50-Year-Old Problem
description: In 1973, Paul Erdős asked if it was possible to assemble sets of “triples” — three points on a graph — so that they abide by two seemingly incompatible rules. A new proof shows it can always be done.

title: How Do Mathematicians Know Their Proofs Are Correct?
description: What makes a proof stronger than a guess? What does evidence look like in the realm of mathematical abstraction? Hear the mathematician Melanie Matchett Wood explain how probability helps to guide number theorists toward certainty.

title: Mass and Angular Momentum, Left Ambiguous by Einstein, Get Defined
description: Surprising as it may sound, 107 years after the introduction of general relativity, the meanings of basic concepts are still being worked out.

title: Embryo Cells Set Patterns for Growth by Pushing and Pulling
description: Patterns that guide the development of feathers and other features can be set by mechanical forces in the embryo, not just by gradients of chemicals.

title: Quantum Algorithms Conquer a New Kind of Problem
description: Computer scientists have found a new type of problem that quantum computers can solve dramatically faster than their classical counterparts.

title: The Scientist Who Developed a New Way to Understand Communication
description: Mark Braverman has spent his career translating thorny problems into the language of information complexity.

title: A Solver of the Hardest Easy Problems About Prime Numbers
description: On his way to winning a Fields Medal, James Maynard has cut a path through simple-sounding questions about prime numbers that have stumped mathematicians for centuries.

title: For His Sporting Approach to Math, a Fields Medal
description: With Hugo Duminil-Copin, thinking rarely happens without moving. His insights into the flow-related properties of complex networks have earned him the Fields Medal.

title: He Dropped Out to Become a Poet. Now He’s Won a Fields Medal.
description: June Huh wasn’t interested in mathematics until a chance encounter during his sixth year of college. Now his profound insights connecting combinatorics and geometry have led to math’s highest honor.

title: In Times of Scarcity, War and Peace, a Ukrainian Finds the Magic in Math
description: With her homeland mired in war, the sphere-packing number theorist Maryna Viazovska has become the second woman to win a Fields Medal in the award’s 86-year history.

title: Life Helps Make Almost Half of All Minerals on Earth
description: A new origins-based system for classifying minerals reveals the huge geochemical imprint that life has left on Earth. It could help us identify other worlds with life too.

title: The Sordid Past of the Cubic Formula
description: The quest to solve cubic equations led to duels, betrayals — and modern mathematics.

title: Can Computers Be Mathematicians?
description: Artificial intelligence has bested humans at problem-solving challenges like chess and Go. Is mathematics research next? Steven Strogatz speaks with mathematician Kevin Buzzard to learn about the effort to translate math into language that computers understand.

title: Controversy Continues Over Whether Hot Water Freezes Faster Than Cold
description: Decades after a Tanzanian teenager initiated study of the “Mpemba effect,” the effort to confirm or refute it is leading physicists toward new theories about how substances relax to equilibrium.

title: Protein Blobs Linked to Alzheimer’s Affect Aging in All Cells
description: Protein buildups like those seen around neurons in Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and other brain diseases occur in all aging cells, a new study suggests. Learning their significance may reveal new strategies for treating age-related diseases.

title: How to Weigh Truth With a Balance Scale
description: In recreational mathematics, the balance scale is an endless source of puzzles that require precise and elaborate logic and teach the fundamentals of generalization.

title: By Exploring Virtual Worlds, AI Learns in New Ways
description: Intelligent beings learn by interacting with the world. Artificial intelligence researchers have adopted a similar strategy to teach their virtual agents new tricks.

title: Mathematical Connect-the-Dots Reveals How Structure Emerges
description: A new proof identifies precisely how large a mathematical graph must be before it contains a regular substructure.

title: The Spooky Quantum Phenomenon You’ve Never Heard Of
description: Quantum computers may derive their power from the “magical” way that properties of particles change depending on the context.

title: An Immunologist Fights Covid with Tweets and a Nasal Spray
description: Akiko Iwasaki, an immunologist who became a lifeline for the worried and the curious during the pandemic, thinks that nasal spray vaccines could be the next needed breakthrough in our fight against the coronavirus.

title: Surfaces So Different Even a Fourth Dimension Can’t Make Them the Same
description: For decades mathematicians have searched for a specific pair of surfaces that can’t be transformed into each other in four-dimensional space. Now they’ve found them.

title: What Is Life?
description: Without a good definition of life, how do we look for it on alien planets? Steven Strogatz speaks with Robert Hazen, a mineralogist and astrobiologist, and Sheref Mansy, a chemist, to learn more.

title: Wheel Made of ‘Odd Matter’ Spontaneously Rolls Uphill
description: Physicists have solved a key problem of robotic locomotion by revising the usual rules of interaction between simple component parts.

title: The Brain Has a ‘Low-Power Mode’ That Blunts Our Senses
description: Neuroscientists uncovered an energy-saving mode in vision-system neurons that works at the cost of being able to see fine-grained details.

title: The Computer Scientist Who Parlays Failures Into Breakthroughs
description: Daniel Spielman solves important problems by thinking hard — about other questions.

title: Astronomers Reimagine the Making of the Planets
description: Observations of faraway planets have forced a near-total rewrite of the story of how our solar system came to be.

title: Researchers Achieve ‘Absurdly Fast’ Algorithm for Network Flow
description: Computer scientists can now solve a decades-old problem in practically the time it takes to write it down.

title: Reshuffled Rivers Bolster the Amazon’s Hyper-Biodiversity
description: The lush biodiversity of the Amazon may be due in part to the dynamics of branching rivers, which serve as invisible fences that continuously barricade and merge bird populations.

title: Graduate Student’s Side Project Proves Prime Number Conjecture
description: Jared Duker Lichtman, 26, has proved a longstanding conjecture relating prime numbers to a broad class of “primitive” sets. To his adviser, it came as a “complete shock.”

title: Brain-Signal Proteins Evolved Before Animals Did
description: Some animal neuropeptides have been around longer than nervous systems.

title: Surfaces Beyond Imagination Are Discovered After Decades-Long Search
description: Using ideas borrowed from graph theory, two mathematicians have shown that extremely complex surfaces are easy to traverse.

title: What Is the Langlands Program?
description: The Langlands program provides a beautifully intricate set of connections between various areas of mathematics, pointing the way toward novel solutions for old problems.

title: How Could Life Evolve From Cyanide?
description: How did life arise on Earth? Steven Strogatz speaks with the Nobel Prize-winning biologist Jack Szostak and Betül Kaçar, a paleogeneticist and astrobiologist, to explore our best understanding of how we all got here.

title: How to Make the Universe Think for Us
description: Physicists are building neural networks out of vibrations, voltages and lasers, arguing that the future of computing lies in exploiting the universe’s complex physical behaviors.

title: The Secret Math Behind Mind-Reading Magic Tricks
description: Four puzzle solutions reveal different ways to divine someone’s hidden number with impossibly little information.

title: Physicists Rewrite the Fundamental Law That Leads to Disorder
description: The second law of thermodynamics is among the most sacred in all of science, but it has always rested on 19th century arguments about probability. New arguments trace its true source to the flows of quantum information.

title: Why Claude Shannon Would Have Been Great at Wordle
description: A bit of information theory can help you analyze — and improve — your Wordle game.

title: Life’s First Peptides May Have Grown on RNA Strands
description: RNA and peptides coevolving in the primordial world might have jointly served as a precursor to the modern ribosome.

title: How Computer Scientists Learned to Reinvent the Proof
description: Why verify every line of a proof, when just a few checks will do?

title: Simple Gene Circuits Hint at How Stem Cells Find New Identities
description: Synthetic biology experiments suggest a “MultiFate” model for how genetically identical cells become the many different types found in complex organisms like us.

title: Will the James Webb Space Telescope Reveal Another Earth?
description: The space telescope is one of the most ambitious scientific projects ever undertaken. Marcia Rieke and Nikole Lewis, two of the scientists leading JWST investigations, talk to Steven Strogatz about how it may transform our understanding of the universe.

title: How Complex Is a Knot? New Proof Reveals Ranking System That Works.
description: “Ribbon concordance” will let mathematicians compare knots by linking them across four-dimensional space.

title: How to Write Software With Mathematical Perfection
description: Leslie Lamport revolutionized how computers talk to each other. Now he’s working on how engineers talk to their machines.

title: Puzzling Quantum Scenario Appears Not to Conserve Energy
description: By resolving a paradox about light in a box, researchers hope to clarify the concept of energy in quantum theory.

title: Black Hole Image Reveals the Beast Inside the Milky Way’s Heart
description: In 2019, the Event Horizon Telescope released a historic image of a supermassive black hole in another galaxy. The follow-up — an image of Sagittarius A* — shows it shimmering at the center of our own.

title: Computer Scientists Prove That Certain Problems Are Truly Hard
description: Finding out whether a question is too difficult to ever solve efficiently depends on figuring out just how hard it is. Researchers have now shown how to do that for a major class of problems.

title: Powerful ‘Machine Scientists’ Distill the Laws of Physics From Raw Data
description: Researchers say we’re on the cusp of “GoPro physics,” where a camera can point at an event and an algorithm can identify the underlying physics equation.

title: Why ‘De-Extinction’ Is Impossible (But Could Work Anyway)
description: Several projects are aiming to bring back mammoths and other species that have vanished from the planet. Whether that’s technically possible is beside the point.

title: In Test Tubes, RNA Molecules Evolve Into a Tiny Ecosystem
description: When researchers gave a genetic molecule the ability to replicate, it evolved over time into a complex network of “hosts” and “parasites” that both competed and cooperated to survive.

title: Where Do Space, Time and Gravity Come From?
description: Einstein’s description of curved space-time doesn’t easily mesh with a universe made up of quantum wavefunctions. Theoretical physicist Sean Carroll discusses the quest for quantum gravity with host Steven Strogatz.

title: Think of a Number. How Do Math Magicians Know What It Is?
description: Mathematical magic can seem like mind reading. Your job is to reveal the secret behind these four tricks.

title: Physicists Pin Down How Quantum Uncertainty Sharpens Measurements
description: Throwing out data seems to make measurements of distances and angles more precise. The reason why has been traced to Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle.

title: Mathematicians Coax Fluid Equations Into Nonphysical Solutions
description: The famed Navier-Stokes equations can lead to cases where more than one result is possible, but only in an extremely narrow set of situations.

title: Secrets of the Moon’s Permanent Shadows Are Coming to Light
description: Robots are about to venture into the sunless depths of lunar craters to investigate ancient water ice trapped there, while remote studies find hints about how water arrives on rocky worlds.

title: What Happens When We Give Animals Our Diseases?
description: While it’s understandable to focus on the diseases affecting humans, it’s important to study how our illnesses may affect animals.

title: Ancient Genes for Symbiosis Hint at Mitochondria’s Origins
description: Was the addition of mitochondria a first step in the formation of complex cells or one of the last? A new study of bacteria tries to answer this contentious question in evolutionary biology.

title: Elegant Six-Page Proof Reveals the Emergence of Random Structure
description: Two young mathematicians have astonished their colleagues with a full proof of the Kahn-Kalai conjecture — a sweeping statement about how structure emerges in random sets and graphs.

title: New Proof Illuminates the Hidden Structure of Common Equations
description: Van der Waerden’s conjecture mystified mathematicians for 85 years. Its solution shows how polynomial roots relate to one another.

title: Why Is Inflammation a Dangerous Necessity?
description: The immune system protects us from a full spectrum of pathogens, but without balance, it can end up hurting us over time, too. The immunologist Shruti Naik explains how our defenses can turn on us.

title: Pondering the Bits That Build Space-Time and Brains
description: Vijay Balasubramanian investigates whether the fabric of the universe might be built from information, and what it means that physicists can even ask such a question.

title: In Sexy Worms, Inheritance Beyond Genes Can Help Evolution
description: Traits from RNA molecules passed between multiple generations of worms can work with genetic changes to influence future evolution.

title: Which Computational Universe Do We Live In?
description: Cryptographers want to know which of five possible worlds we inhabit, which will reveal whether truly secure cryptography is even possible.

title: Researchers Gain New Understanding From Simple AI
description: Language processing programs are notoriously hard to interpret, but smaller versions can provide important insights into how they work.

title: Scientists Unravel How the Tonga Volcano Caused Worldwide Tsunamis
description: The Tonga eruption in January was “basically like Krakatoa 2.” This time, geophysicists could explain the tiny tsunamis that cropped up all over the planet, solving a 139-year-old mystery about Tonga’s predecessor.

title: Deep Learning Poised to ‘Blow Up’ Famed Fluid Equations
description: For centuries, mathematicians have tried to prove that Euler’s fluid equations can produce nonsensical answers. A new approach to machine learning has researchers betting that “blowup” is near.

title: Life With Longer Genetic Codes Seems Possible — but Less Likely
description: Life could use a more expansive genetic code in theory, but new work shows that improving on three-letter codons would be a challenge.

title: The Secrets of Zugzwang in Chess, Math and Pizzas
description: Learn the magic and math of how to win games when your opponent goes first.

title: Newly Measured Particle Seems Heavy Enough to Break Known Physics
description: A new analysis of W bosons suggests these particles are significantly heavier than predicted by the Standard Model of particle physics.

title: Untangling Why Knots Are Important
description: Steven Strogatz explores the mysteries of knots with the mathematicians Colin Adams and Lisa Piccirillo.

title: Researchers Identify ‘Master Problem’ Underlying All Cryptography
description: The existence of secure cryptography depends on one of the oldest questions in computational complexity.

title: Mitochondria Double as Tiny Lenses in the Eye
description: The optical properties of mitochondrial bundles in the retina may improve how efficiently the eye captures light.

title: Father-Son Team Solves Geometry Problem With Infinite Folds
description: The result could help researchers answer a larger question about flattening objects from the fourth dimension to the third dimension.

title: Beyond the Second Law
description: Thanks to the power of fluctuation relations, physicists are taking the second law of thermodynamics to settings once thought impossible.

title: In Music and Math, Lillian Pierce Builds Landscapes
description: Lillian Pierce wants to transform access to the world of mathematics, while making headway on problems that bridge the discrete and continuous.

title: Massive Black Holes Shown to Act Like Quantum Particles
description: Physicists are using quantum math to understand what happens when black holes collide. In a surprise, they’ve shown that a single particle can describe a collision’s entire gravitational wave.

title: Cells Blaze Their Own Trails to Navigate Through the Body
description: With self-generated gradients of chemicals and physical tension, cells in the body steer themselves to vital destinations.

title: What a Math Party Game Tells Us About Graph Theory
description: Play this simple math game with your friends to gain insights into fundamental principles of graph theory.

title: Dennis Sullivan, Uniter of Topology and Chaos, Wins the Abel Prize
description: The American mathematician invented entire new ways to understand shapes and spaces.

title: Why Do We Die Without Sleep?
description: The reasons why sleep is so vital often hide in unexpected parts of the body, as host Steven Strogatz discovers in conversations with researchers Dragana Rogulja and Alex Keene.

title: Brain Chemical Helps Signal to Neurons When to Start a Movement
description: Dopamine, a neurochemical often associated with reward behavior, also seems to help organize precisely when the brain initiates movements. It’s the latest revelation about the power of neuromodulators.

title: A New Tool for Finding Dark Matter Digs Up Nothing
description: Physicists are devising clever new ways to exploit the extreme sensitivity of gravitational wave detectors like LIGO. But so far, they’ve seen no signs of exotica.

title: Deep Curiosity Inspires The Joy of Why Podcast
description: The noted mathematician and author Steven Strogatz explains how the conversations with experts in his new Quanta Magazine podcast address his lifelong fascination with timeless mysteries.

title: This Animal’s Behavior Is Mechanically Programmed
description: Biomechanical interactions, rather than neurons, control the movements of one of the simplest animals. The discovery offers a glimpse into how animal behavior worked before neurons evolved.

title: An Antimatter Experiment Shows Surprises Near Absolute Zero
description: An experiment conducted on hybrid matter-antimatter atoms has defied researchers’ expectations.

title: Machine Learning Reimagines the Building Blocks of Computing
description: Traditional algorithms power complicated computational tools like machine learning. A new approach, called algorithms with predictions, uses the power of machine learning to improve algorithms.

title: Tiny Galaxies Reveal Secrets of Supermassive Black Holes
description: Dwarf galaxies weren’t supposed to have big black holes. Their surprise discovery has revealed clues about how the universe’s biggest black holes could have formed.

title: Will Transformers Take Over Artificial Intelligence?
description: A simple algorithm that revolutionizes how neural networks approach language is now taking on image classification as well. It may not stop there.

title: Math’s ‘Oldest Problem Ever’ Gets a New Answer
description: A new proof significantly strengthens a decades-old result about the ubiquity of ways to represent whole numbers as sums of unit fractions.

title: Peptides on Stardust May Have Provided a Shortcut to Life
description: The discovery that short peptides can form spontaneously on cosmic dust hints at more of a role for them in the earliest stages of life’s origin, on Earth or elsewhere.

title: In New Math Proofs, Artificial Intelligence Plays to Win
description: A new computer program fashioned after artificial intelligence systems like AlphaGo has solved several open problems in combinatorics and graph theory.

title: Scientists Watch a Memory Form in a Living Brain
description: While watching a fearful memory take shape in the brain of a living fish, neuroscientists see an unexpected level of rewiring occur in the synaptic connections.

title: How We Can Make Sense of Chaos
description: Dynamical systems can be chaotic and impossible to predict, but mathematicians have discovered tools to help understand them.

title: A Deepening Crisis Forces Physicists to Rethink Structure of Nature’s Laws
description: Physicists are reexamining a longstanding assumption: that big stuff consists of smaller stuff.

title: Four Years On, New Experiment Sees No Sign of ‘Cosmic Dawn’
description: When astronomers tried to confirm a signal from the birth of the first stars after the Big Bang, they saw nothing.

title: Cryptographers Achieve Perfect Secrecy With Imperfect Devices
description: For the first time, experiments demonstrate the possibility of sharing secrets with perfect privacy — even when the devices used to share them cannot be trusted.

title: Most Complete Simulation of a Cell Probes Life’s Hidden Rules
description: A 3D digital model of a “minimal cell” leads scientists closer to understanding the barest requirements for life.

title: In Search of Cracks in Albert Einstein’s Theory of Gravity
description: Celia Escamilla-Rivera is combining large data sets with supercomputers to test general relativity against its little-known competitors.

title: Play First and Lose: Zugzwang in Chess, Math and Pizzas
description: How to win games by going second and leaving your opponent with no good options.

title: AI Overcomes Stumbling Block on Brain-Inspired Hardware
description: Algorithms that use the brain’s communication signal can now work on analog neuromorphic chips, which closely mimic our energy-efficient brains.

title: A Billion Years Before Sex, Ancient Cells Were Equipped for It
description: Molecular detective work is zeroing in on the origins of sexual reproduction. The protein tools for cell mergers seem to have long predated sex — so what were they doing?

title: Machine Learning Becomes a Mathematical Collaborator
description: Two recent collaborations between mathematicians and DeepMind demonstrate the potential of machine learning to help researchers generate new mathematical conjectures.

title: The Mysterious Forces Inside the Nucleus Grow a Little Less Strange
description: The strong force holds protons and neutrons together, but the theory behind it is largely inscrutable. Two new approaches show how it works.

title: Computer Scientists Prove Why Bigger Neural Networks Do Better
description: Two researchers show that for neural networks to be able to remember better, they need far more parameters than previously thought.

title: New Map of Meaning in the Brain Changes Ideas About Memory
description: Researchers have mapped hundreds of semantic categories to the tiny bits of the cortex that represent them in our thoughts and perceptions. What they discovered might change our view of memory.

title: An Ancient Geometry Problem Falls to New Mathematical Techniques
description: Three mathematicians show, for the first time, how to form a square with the same area as a circle by cutting them into interchangeable pieces that can be visualized.

title: Quantum Complexity Tamed by Machine Learning
description: If only scientists understood exactly how electrons act in molecules, they’d be able to predict the behavior of everything from experimental drugs to high-temperature superconductors. Following decades of physics-based insights, artificial intelligence systems are taking the next leap.

title: Machine Learning Gets a Quantum Speedup
description: Two teams have shown how quantum approaches can solve problems faster than classical computers, bringing physics and computer science closer together.

title: Mathematicians Prove 30-Year-Old André-Oort Conjecture
description: A team of mathematicians has solved an important question about how solutions to polynomial equations relate to sophisticated geometric objects called Shimura varieties.

title: Secrets of Early Animal Evolution Revealed by Chromosome ‘Tectonics’
description: Large blocks of genes conserved through hundreds of millions of years of evolution hint at how the first animal chromosomes came to be.

title: Why Triangles Are Easy and Tetrahedra Are Hard
description: The triangle angle sum theorem makes working with triangles easy. What happens when you can’t rely on it?

title: A Solution to the Faint-Sun Paradox Reveals a Narrow Window for Life
description: We might have a past faint sun to owe for life’s existence. This has consequences for the possibility of life outside Earth.

title: How the Physics of Resonance Shapes Reality
description: The same phenomenon by which an opera singer can shatter a wineglass also underlies the very existence of subatomic particles.

title: Researchers Build AI That Builds AI
description: By using hypernetworks, researchers can now preemptively fine-tune artificial neural networks, saving some of the time and expense of training.

title: How Infinite Series Reveal the Unity of Mathematics
description: Infinite sums are among the most underrated yet powerful concepts in mathematics, capable of linking concepts across math’s vast web.

title: In a Numerical Coincidence, Some See Evidence for String Theory
description: In a quest to map out a quantum theory of gravity, researchers have used logical rules to calculate how much Einstein’s theory must change. The result matches string theory perfectly.

title: Any Single Galaxy Reveals the Composition of an Entire Universe
description: In computer simulations of possible universes, researchers have discovered that a neural network can infer the amount of matter in a whole universe by studying just one of its galaxies.

title: Computer Scientists Eliminate Pesky Quantum Computations
description: For years, intermediate measurements made it hard to quantify the complexity of quantum algorithms. New work establishes that those measurements aren’t necessary after all.

title: Neural Noise Shows the Uncertainty of Our Memories
description: The electrical chatter of our working memories reflects our uncertainty about their contents.

title: Mathematicians Clear Hurdle in Quest to Decode Primes
description: Paul Nelson has solved the subconvexity problem, bringing mathematicians one step closer to understanding the Riemann hypothesis and the distribution of prime numbers.

title: Symmetries Reveal Clues About the Holographic Universe
description: Physicists have been busy exploring how our universe might emerge like a hologram out of a two-dimensional sheet. New clues have come from the symmetries found on an infinitely distant “celestial sphere.”

title: Evolution ‘Landscapes’ Predict What’s Next for COVID Virus
description: Studies that map the adaptive value of viral mutations hint at how the COVID-19 pandemic might progress next.

title: Euler’s 243-Year-Old ‘Impossible’ Puzzle Gets a Quantum Solution
description: A surprising new solution to Leonhard Euler’s famous “36 officers puzzle” offers a novel way of encoding quantum information.

title: Qubits Can Be as Safe as Bits, Researchers Show
description: A new result shows that quantum information can theoretically be protected from errors just as well as classical information can.

title: Flying Fish and Aquarium Pets Yield Secrets of Evolution
description: New studies reveal the ancient, shared genetic “grammar” underpinning the diverse evolution of fish fins and tetrapod limbs.

title: An Injection of Chaos Solves Decades-Old Fluid Mystery
description: In the 1960s, drillers noticed that certain fluids would firm up if they flowed too fast. Researchers have finally explained why.

title: Mathematicians Outwit Hidden Number Conspiracy
description: Decades ago, a mathematician posed a warmup problem for some of the most difficult questions about prime numbers. It turned out to be just as difficult to solve, until now.

title: The Year in Math and Computer Science
description: Mathematicians and computer scientists answered major questions in topology, set theory and even physics, even as computers continued to grow more capable.

title: The Year in Physics
description: Puzzling particles, quirky (and controversial) quantum computers, and one of the most ambitious science experiments in history marked the year’s milestones.

title: The Year in Biology
description: The detailed understanding of brains and multicellular bodies reached new heights this year, while the genomes of the COVID-19 virus and various organisms yielded more surprises.

title: Detailed Footage Finally Reveals What Triggers Lightning
description: Scientists have never been able to adequately explain where lightning comes from. Now the first detailed observations of its emergence inside a cloud have exposed how electric fields grow strong enough to let bolts fly.

title: What Does It Mean for AI to Understand?
description: It’s simple enough for AI to seem to comprehend data, but devising a true test of a machine’s knowledge has proved difficult.

title: Mathematician Hurls Structure and Disorder Into Century-Old Problem
description: A new paper shows how to create longer disordered strings than mathematicians had thought possible, proving that a well-known recent conjecture is “spectacularly wrong.”

title: When a Gene Illness Discovery Means Breaking Bad News
description: When scientists discover genes linked to dangerous illnesses in their samples, how should they convey that news to the study participants? The geneticist Cristen Willer had to tackle that challenge.

title: Cosmologists Parry Attacks on the Vaunted Cosmological Principle
description: A central pillar of cosmology — the universe is the same everywhere and in all directions — is surviving a storm of possible evidence against it.

title: Mathematicians Transcend Geometric Theory of Motion
description: More than 30 years ago, Andreas Floer changed geometry. Now, two mathematicians have finally figured out how to extend his revolutionary perspective.

title: Gravitational Waves Should Permanently Distort Space-Time
description: The “gravitational memory effect” predicts that a passing gravitational wave should forever alter the structure of space-time. Physicists have linked the phenomenon to fundamental cosmic symmetries and a potential solution to the black hole information paradox.

title: AI Researchers Fight Noise by Turning to Biology
description: Tiny amounts of artificial noise can fool neural networks, but not humans. Some researchers are looking to neuroscience for a fix.

title: New Brain Maps Can Predict Behaviors
description: Rapid advances in large-scale connectomics are beginning to spotlight the importance of individual variations in the neural circuitry. They also highlight the limitations of “wiring diagrams” alone.

title: The Webb Space Telescope Will Rewrite Cosmic History. If It Works.
description: The James Webb Space Telescope has the potential to rewrite the history of the cosmos and reshape humanity’s position within it. But first, a lot of things have to work just right.

title: Quantum Simulators Create a Totally New Phase of Matter
description: One of the first goals of quantum computing has been to recreate bizarre quantum systems that can’t be studied in an ordinary computer. A dark-horse quantum simulator has now done just that.

title: Will We Ever Get Rid of COVID-19?
description: No matter how much we’d like to eradicate SARS-CoV-2, it may be better to settle for other forms of control.

title: Wildfires of Varying Intensity Can Be Good for Biodiversity
description: The spate of furious wildfires around the world during the past decade has revealed to ecologists how much biodiversity and “pyrodiversity” go hand in hand.

title: Why e , the Transcendental Math Constant, Is Just the Best
description: The solution to our puzzle about Euler’s number explains why e pops up in situations that involve optimality.

title: Researchers Defeat Randomness to Create Ideal Code
description: By carefully constructing a multidimensional and well-connected graph, a team of researchers has finally created a long-sought locally testable code that can immediately betray whether it’s been corrupted.

title: At the Dawn of Life, Heat May Have Driven Cell Division
description: A mathematical model shows how a thermodynamic mechanism could have made protocells split in two.

title: The Algorithm That Lets Particle Physicists Count Higher Than Two
description: Through his encyclopedic study of the electron, an obscure figure named Stefano Laporta found a handle on the subatomic world’s fearsome complexity. His algorithm has swept the field.

title: What Hot Dogs Can Teach Us About Number Theory
description: The Chinese remainder theorem is an ancient and powerful extension of the simple math of least common multiples.

title: The Mathematician Who Delights in Building Bridges
description: Ana Caraiani seeks to unify mathematics through her work on the ambitious Langlands program.

title: How Quantum Computers Will Correct Their Errors
description: Quantum bits are fussy and fragile. Useful quantum computers will need to use an error-correction technique like the one that was recently demonstrated on a real machine.

title: To Be Energy-Efficient, Brains Predict Their Perceptions
description: Results from neural networks support the idea that brains are “prediction machines” — and that they work that way to conserve energy.

title: A New Theory for Systems That Defy Newton’s Third Law
description: In nonreciprocal systems, where Newton’s third law falls apart, “exceptional points” are helping researchers understand phase transitions and possibly other phenomena.

title: Laws of Logic Lead to New Restrictions on the Big Bang
description: Physicists are translating commonsense principles into strict mathematical constraints on how our universe must have behaved at the beginning of time.

title: Mathematicians Find Structure in Biased Polynomials
description: New work establishes a tighter connection between the rank of a polynomial and the extent to which it favors particular outputs.

title: The Brain Can Recall and Reawaken Past Immune Responses
description: The brain not only helps to regulate immune responses, but also stores and retrieves “memories” of them.

title: Sponge Genes Hint at the Origins of Neurons and Other Cells
description: A new study of gene expression in sponges reveals the complex diversity of their cells as well as some possibly ancient connections between the nervous, immune and digestive systems.

title: Researchers Revise Recipe for Building a Rocky Planet Like Earth
description: Over the past decade, researchers have completely rewritten the story of how gas giants such as Jupiter and Saturn form. They’re now debating whether the same process might hold for Earth.

title: Her Machine Learning Tools Pull Insights From Cell Images
description: The computational biologist Anne Carpenter creates software that brings the power of machine learning to researchers seeking answers in mountains of cell images.

title: Surprising Limits Discovered in Quest for Optimal Solutions
description: Algorithms that zero in on solutions to optimization problems are the beating heart of machine reasoning. New results reveal surprising limits.

title: Is the Great Neutrino Puzzle Pointing to Multiple Missing Particles?
description: Years of conflicting neutrino measurements have led physicists to propose a “dark sector” of invisible particles — one that could simultaneously explain dark matter, the puzzling expansion of the universe, and other mysteries.

title: Where Transcendental Numbers Hide in Everyday Math
description: The transcendental number π is as familiar as it is ubiquitous, but how does Euler’s number e transcend the ordinary?

title: How Tadayuki Watanabe Disproved a Major Conjecture About Spheres
description: Watanabe invented a new way of distinguishing shapes on his way to solving the last open case of the Smale conjecture, a central question in topology about symmetries of the sphere.

title: An Ultra-Precise Clock Links the Quantum World With Gravity
description: Time was found to flow differently between the top and bottom of a single cloud of atoms. Physicists hope that such a system will one day help them combine quantum mechanics and Einstein’s theory of gravity.

title: The Brain Processes Speech in Parallel With Other Sounds
description: Scientists thought that the brain’s hearing centers might just process speech along with other sounds. But new work suggests that speech gets some special treatment very early on.

title: The Uselessness of Useful Knowledge
description: Today’s powerful but little-understood artificial intelligence breakthroughs echo past examples of unexpected scientific progress.

title: A Hint of Dark Matter Sends Physicists Looking to the Skies
description: After a search of neutron stars finds preliminary evidence for hypothetical dark matter particles called axions, astrophysicists are devising new ways to spot them.

title: Neuron Bursts Can Mimic Famous AI Learning Strategy
description: A new model of learning centers on bursts of neural activity that act as teaching signals — approximating backpropagation, the algorithm behind learning in AI.

title: How Animals Map 3D Spaces Surprises Brain Researchers
description: When animals move through 3D spaces, the neat system of grid cell activity they use for navigating on flat surfaces gets more disorderly. That has implications for some ideas about memory and other processes.

title: How Wavelets Allow Researchers to Transform, and Understand, Data
description: Built upon the ubiquitous Fourier transform, the mathematical tools known as wavelets allow unprecedented analysis and understanding of continuous signals.

title: The Astronomer Who’s About to See the Skies of Other Earths
description: After the ultra-powerful James Webb Space Telescope launches later this year, Laura Kreidberg will lead two efforts to check the weather on rocky planets orbiting other stars.

title: A New Link to an Old Model Could Crack the Mystery of Deep Learning
description: To help them explain the shocking success of deep neural networks, researchers are turning to older but better-understood models of machine learning.

title: Mathematicians Prove Melting Ice Stays Smooth
description: After decades of effort, mathematicians now have a complete understanding of the complicated equations that model the motion of free boundaries, like the one between ice and water.

title: Chemistry Nobel Prize Honors Technique for Building Molecules
description: Benjamin List and David MacMillan received the 2021 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their development of asymmetrical organocatalysis.

title: Work on Earth’s Climate and Other Complex Systems Earns Nobel Prize in Physics
description: Syukuro Manabe and Klaus Hasselmann have been honored for their work that led to reliable predictions of the effects of climate change. They will share the Nobel with Giorgio Parisi, who has made pioneering studies of chaotic physical systems.

title: Medicine Nobel Prize Goes to Temperature and Touch Discoveries
description: David Julius and Ardem Patapoutian were awarded the 2021 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discoveries of how we detect heat and touch.

title: Anil Seth Finds Consciousness in Life’s Push Against Entropy
description: How does consciousness arise in mere flesh and blood? To the neuroscientist Anil Seth, our organic bodies are the key to the experience.

title: Major Quantum Computing Strategy Suffers Serious Setbacks
description: So-called topological quantum computing would avoid many of the problems that stand in the way of full-scale quantum computers. But high-profile missteps have led some experts to question whether the field is fooling itself.

title: In Topology, When Are Two Shapes the Same?
description: As topologists seek to classify shapes, the effort hinges on how to define a manifold and what it means for two of them to be equivalent.

title: ‘Impossible’ Particle Discovery Adds Key Piece to the Strong Force Puzzle
description: The unexpected discovery of the double-charm tetraquark has given physicists a new tool with which to hone their understanding of the strongest of nature’s fundamental forces.

title: The Simple Math Behind the Mighty Roots of Unity
description: Solutions to the simplest polynomial equations — called “roots of unity” — have an elegant structure that mathematicians still use to study some of math’s greatest open questions.

title: Single Cells Evolve Large Multicellular Forms in Just Two Years
description: Researchers have discovered that environments favoring clumpy growth are all that’s needed to quickly transform single-celled yeast into complex multicellular organisms.

title: Mathematician Answers Chess Problem About Attacking Queens
description: The n -queens problem is about finding how many different ways queens can be placed on a chessboard so that none attack each other. A mathematician has now all but solved it.

title: Mathematical Analysis of Fruit Fly Wings Hints at Evolution’s Limits
description: A painstaking study of wing morphology shows both the striking uniformity of individuals in a species and a subtle pattern of linked variations that evolution can exploit.

title: Biologists Rethink the Logic Behind Cells’ Molecular Signals
description: The molecular signaling systems of complex cells are nothing like simple electronic circuits. The logic governing their operation is riotously complex — but it has advantages.

title: A Massive Subterranean ‘Tree’ Is Moving Magma to Earth’s Surface
description: Deep in the mantle, a branching plume of intensely hot material appears to be the engine powering vast volcanic activity.

title: How Ancient War Trickery Is Alive in Math Today
description: Legend says the Chinese military once used a mathematical ruse to conceal its troop numbers. The technique relates to many deep areas of modern math research.

title: The Journey to Define Dimension
description: The concept of dimension seems simple enough, but mathematicians struggled for centuries to precisely define and understand it.

title: New Math Book Rescues Landmark Topology Proof
description: Michael Freedman’s momentous 1981 proof of the four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture was on the verge of being lost. The editors of a new book are trying to save it.

title: Karen Miga Fills In the Missing Pieces of Our Genome
description: Driven by her fascination with highly repetitive, hard-to-read parts of our DNA, Karen Miga led a coalition of researchers to finish sequencing the human genome after almost two decades.

title: One Lab’s Quest to Build Space-Time Out of Quantum Particles
description: For over two decades, physicists have pondered how the fabric of space-time may emerge from some kind of quantum entanglement. In Monika Schleier-Smith’s lab at Stanford University, the thought experiment is becoming real.

title: How Computationally Complex Is a Single Neuron?
description: Computational neuroscientists taught an artificial neural network to imitate a biological neuron. The result offers a new way to think about the complexity of single brain cells.

title: The Complex Truth About ‘Junk DNA’
description: Genomes hold immense quantities of noncoding DNA. Some of it is essential for life, some seems useless, and some has its own agenda.

title: The New Thermodynamic Understanding of Clocks
description: Investigations of the simplest possible clocks have revealed their fundamental limitations — as well as insights into the nature of time itself.

title: To Learn More Quickly, Brain Cells Break Their DNA
description: New work shows that neurons and other brain cells use DNA double-strand breaks, often associated with cancer, neurodegeneration and aging, to quickly express genes related to learning and memory.

title: Banach-Tarski and the Paradox of Infinite Cloning
description: One of the strangest results in mathematics explains how it’s possible to turn one sphere into two identical copies, simply by rearranging its pieces.

title: Math Can, in Theory, Help You Escape a Hungry Bear
description: How readers used their geometry skills to survive a dangerous puzzle.

title: The Brain Doesn’t Think the Way You Think It Does
description: Familiar categories of mental functions such as perception, memory and attention reflect our experience of ourselves, but they are misleading about how the brain works. More revealing approaches are emerging.

title: This Physicist Discovered an Escape From Hawking’s Black Hole Paradox
description: The five-decade-old paradox — long thought key to linking quantum theory with Einstein’s theory of gravity — is falling to a new generation of thinkers. Netta Engelhardt is leading the way.

title: How Big Data Carried Graph Theory Into New Dimensions
description: Researchers are turning to the mathematics of higher-order interactions to better model the complex connections within their data.

title: How Big Can the Quantum World Be? Physicists Probe the Limits.
description: By showing that even large objects can exhibit bizarre quantum behaviors, physicists hope to illuminate the mystery of quantum collapse, identify the quantum nature of gravity, and perhaps even make Schrödinger’s cat a reality.

title: Computer Scientists Discover Limits of Major Research Algorithm
description: The most widely used technique for finding the largest or smallest values of a math function turns out to be a fundamentally difficult computational problem.

title: How Do New Organs Evolve? A Beetle Gland Shows the Way.
description: The evolution of a defensive gland in beetles shows how organs can arise from novel cells carving out new functional niches for their neighbors.

title: Physicists Create a Bizarre ‘Wigner Crystal’ Made Purely of Electrons
description: The unambiguous discovery of a Wigner crystal relied on a novel technique for probing the insides of complex materials.

title: How Steven Weinberg Transformed Physics and Physicists
description: When Steven Weinberg died last month, the world lost one of its most profound thinkers.

title: Turing Patterns Turn Up in a Tiny Crystal
description: The mechanism behind leopard spots and zebra stripes also appears to explain the patterned growth of a bismuth crystal, extending Alan Turing’s 1952 idea to the atomic scale.

title: Animals Count and Use Zero. How Far Does Their Number Sense Go?
description: Crows recently demonstrated an understanding of the concept of zero. It’s only the latest evidence of animals’ talents for numerical abstraction — which may still differ from our own grasp of numbers.

title: Mathematicians Solve Decades-Old Classification Problem
description: A pair of researchers has shown that trying to classify groups of numbers called “torsion-free abelian groups” is as hard as it can possibly be.

title: Neither Star nor Planet: A Strange Brown Dwarf Puzzles Astronomers
description: Brown dwarfs such as “The Accident” are illuminating the murky borderlands that separate planets from stars.

title: Galois Groups and the Symmetries of Polynomials
description: By focusing on relationships between solutions to polynomial equations, rather than the exact solutions themselves, Évariste Galois changed the course of modern mathematics.

title: Mating Contests Among Females, Long Ignored, May Shape Evolution
description: Showy male competitions over mating privileges have grabbed scientists’ attention more often, but new work hints that sexual selection is also widespread among females.

title: Eternal Change for No Energy: A Time Crystal Finally Made Real
description: Like a perpetual motion machine, a time crystal forever cycles between states without consuming energy. Physicists claim to have built this new phase of matter inside a quantum computer.

title: Proof Assistant Makes Jump to Big-League Math
description: Mathematicians using the computer program Lean have verified the accuracy of a difficult theorem at the cutting edge of research mathematics.

description: A centuries-old concept in soil science has recently been thrown out. Yet it remains a key ingredient in everything from climate models to advanced carbon-capture projects.

title: The ‘Weirdest’ Matter, Made of Partial Particles, Defies Description
description: Theorists are in a frenzy over “fractons,” bizarre, but potentially useful, hypothetical particles that can only move in combination with one another.

description: Using high school algebra and geometry, and knowing just one rational point on a circle or elliptic curve, we can locate infinitely many others.

title: Plasmid, Virus or Other? DNA ‘Borgs’ Blur Boundaries.
description: Scientists have reported large DNA structures in some archaea that defy easy categorization.

title: How Bell’s Theorem Proved ‘Spooky Action at a Distance’ Is Real
description: The root of today’s quantum revolution was John Stewart Bell’s 1964 theorem showing that quantum mechanics really permits instantaneous connections between far-apart locations.

description: Laurent Fargues and Peter Scholze have found a new, more powerful way of connecting number theory and geometry as part of the sweeping Langlands program.

description: The Standard Model is a sweeping equation that has correctly predicted the results of virtually every experiment ever conducted, as Quanta explores in a new video.

title: How Many Numbers Exist? Infinity Proof Moves Math Closer to an Answer.
description: For 50 years, mathematicians have believed that the total number of real numbers is unknowable. A new proof suggests otherwise.

description: Melanie Mitchell has worked on digital minds for decades. She says they’ll never truly be like ours until they can make analogies.

description: The DNA of some viruses doesn’t use the same four nucleotide bases found in all other life. New work shows how this exception is possible and hints that it could be more common than we think.

description: A group of mathematicians has shown that at critical moments, a symmetry called rotational invariance is a universal property across many physical systems.

title: Neurons Unexpectedly Encode Information in the Timing of Their Firing
description: A temporal pattern of activity observed in human brains may explain how we can learn so quickly.

description: Mitochondria appear to communicate and cooperate with one another, both within and between cells. Biologists are only just beginning to understand how and why.

description: Other diseases with long-term symptoms can help us understand how COVID can affect us long after the virus itself is gone.

description: These ultrabright flashes have recently been tracked for days, upending ideas about the cataclysms that create them.

title: Can Math Help You Escape a Hungry Bear?
description: In this month’s puzzle, math is a question of life or death.

description: Even in an incomplete state, quantum field theory is the most successful physical theory ever discovered. Nathan Seiberg, one of its leading architects, talks about the gaps in QFT and how mathematicians could fill them.

description: Jupiter and Saturn should be freezing cold. Instead, they’re hot. Researchers now know why.

title: Secret Workings of Smell Receptors Revealed for First Time
description: Researchers have finally seen how some smell receptors bind to odor molecules. The work yields new insights into one of the most mysterious and versatile senses.

description: In three towering papers, a team of mathematicians has worked out the details of Liouville quantum field theory, a two-dimensional model of quantum gravity.

title: How Animals Color Themselves With Nanoscale Structures
description: Animals sculpt the optical properties of their tissues at the nanoscale to give themselves “structural colors.” New work is piecing together how they do it.

description: Federica Coppari uses the world’s most powerful laser to recreate the cores of distant worlds.

description: Superconductivity has been discovered in graphene devices without any twists, suggesting the form of superconductivity in the material might be mundane after all.

description: The accelerating effort to understand the mathematics of quantum field theory will have profound consequences for both math and physics.

title: DNA Jumps Between Animal Species. No One Knows How Often.

description: To understand what quantum computers can do — and what they can’t — avoid falling for overly simple explanations.

description: Scientists have long struggled to understand how common planets form. A new supercomputer simulation shows that the missing ingredient may be magnetism.

title: Mathematicians Identify Threshold at Which Shapes Give Way
description: A new proof establishes the boundary at which a shape becomes so corrugated, it can be crushed.

title: RNA Brakes May Stabilize a Cellular Symbiosis
description: In some symbiotic partnerships, an RNA-based mechanism may sabotage the growth of greedy hosts.

title: A Burp or a Blast? Seismic Signals Reveal the Volcanic Eruption to Come
description: Scientists have begun to decipher the subtle signs that reveal how explosive a volcanic eruption is going to be.

title: How a Simple Arithmetic Puzzle Can Guide Discovery
description: Playing with numbers can lead to deep mathematical and scientific insights.

title: A Number Theorist Who Connects Math to Other Creative Pursuits
description: Jordan Ellenberg enjoys studying — and writing about — the mathematics underlying everyday phenomena.

description: Groundbreaking results show that neutron stars of different masses may have the same size — upending astrophysical models.

description: Hilbert’s 12th problem asked for novel analogues of the roots of unity, the building blocks for certain number systems. Now, over 100 years later, two mathematicians have produced them.

description: New work suggests that the radiolytic splitting of water supports giant subsurface ecosystems of life on Earth — and could do it elsewhere, too.

description: Supermassive black holes emit jets of white-hot plasma that stretch thousands of light-years across the cosmos. For the first time, researchers have identified what’s creating these jets.

description: A pair of mathematicians solved a legendary question about the proportion of vertices in a graph with an odd number of connections.

description: Studies of sleep are usually neurological. But some of nature’s simplest animals suggest that sleep evolved for metabolic reasons, long before brains even existed.

description: Eve Marder’s research into the plasticity and resilience of nervous systems finds universal principles guiding life’s responses to stress.

description: A mathematical shortcut for analyzing black hole collisions works even in cases where it shouldn’t. As astronomers use it to search for new classes of hidden black holes, others wonder: Why?

description: Originally devised as a rigorous means of counting holes, homology provides a scaffolding for mathematical ideas, allowing for a new way to analyze the shapes within data.

description: The secret to making a qubit for future quantum computers might depend on knowing how to tie knots in unusual materials, argues the physicist Charlie Marcus.

description: New work shows that histones, long treated as boring spools for DNA, sit at the center of the origin story of eukaryotes and continue to play important roles in evolution and disease.

description: A new proposal would use quantum hard drives to combine the light of multiple telescopes, letting astronomers create incredibly high-resolution optical images.

description: An enigmatic connection between the forces of nature is allowing physicists to explore gravity’s quantum side.

title: Amie Wilkinson Sees the Dynamic Chaos in Puff Pastry
description: To a dynamicist like Amie Wilkinson, understanding the universe is about knowing all the right moves.

title: Researchers Read the Sugary ‘Language’ on Cell Surfaces
description: Glycans, the complex sugars that stud cellular surfaces, are like a language that life uses to mediate vital interactions. Researchers are learning how to read their meaning.
