description: Chiara Marletto is trying to build a master theory — a set of ideas so fundamental that all other theories would spring from it. Her first step: Invoke the impossible.

title: A Backdoor Lets the Immune System Monitor the Brain
description: A newfound hub of immune system activity at the back of the brain solves a century-old puzzle.

description: Ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays twist and turn on their way to Earth, which has made it nearly impossible to identify the colossal monsters that create them.

description: Anesthesia is very different from sleep — which is why it offers unique opportunities for studying the human brain, says the physician-researcher and statistician Emery Brown.

description: Researchers have proved a special case of the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture, which shows what happens in graphs that exclude anything resembling a pentagon.

title: How Maxwell’s Demon Continues to Startle Scientists
description: The thorny thought experiment has been turned into a real experiment — one that physicists use to probe the physics of information.

title: DNA of Giant ‘Corpse Flower’ Parasite Surprises Biologists
description: The bizarre genome of the world’s most mysterious flowering plants shows how far parasites will go in stealing, deleting and duplicating DNA.

description: Playing with arithmetic can lead us to unexpected and profound discoveries that point toward deeper mathematics and sometimes even deeper science.

description: To build a general artificial intelligence, we may need to know more about our own minds, argues the computer scientist Melanie Mitchell.

description: Two new approaches allow deep neural networks to solve entire families of partial differential equations, making it easier to model complicated systems and to do so orders of magnitude faster.

description: Some populations of neurons simultaneously process sensations and memories. New work shows how the brain rotates those representations to prevent interference.

description: About 60 million years ago, India plowed into Eurasia and pushed up the Himalayas. But when Lucía Pérez-Díaz reconstructed the event in detail, she found that its central mystery depended on a broken geological clock.

description: Radio waves, longer and less energetic than visible light, give astronomers access to some of the most obscure physics in the cosmos.

title: Trachette Jackson Fights Cancer With Math
description: Quantitative models built by the mathematical biologist Trachette Jackson can make cancer therapies safer and more effective.

title: Mathematician Disproves 80-Year-Old Algebra Conjecture
description: Inside the symmetries of a crystal shape, a postdoctoral researcher has unearthed a counterexample to a basic conjecture about multiplicative inverses.

description: A patchwork of genomic differences in the placenta may explain the organ’s “live fast, die young” strategy and its connections to cancer.

title: ‘Last Hope’ Experiment Finds Evidence for Unknown Particles
description: Today’s long-anticipated announcement by Fermilab’s Muon g-2 team appears to solidify a tantalizing conflict between nature and theory. But a separate calculation, published at the same time, has clouded the picture.

title: Iceland’s Eruptions Reveal the Hot History of Mars
description: The new volcanic fissures are more otherworldly than they first appear.

title: Rediet Abebe on Using Algorithms for Social Justice
description: The computer scientist Rediet Abebe’s passion for applied mathematics closely aligns with her passion to solve problems with poverty and social inequality.

title: Mathematicians Settle Erdős Coloring Conjecture
description: Fifty years ago, Paul Erdős and two other mathematicians came up with a graph theory problem that they thought they might solve on the spot. A team of mathematicians has finally settled it.

description: Rediet Abebe uses the tools of theoretical computer science to understand pressing social problems — and try to fix them.

title: Cells Form Into ‘Xenobots’ on Their Own
description: Embryonic cells can self-assemble into new living forms that don’t resemble the bodies they usually generate, challenging old ideas of what defines an organism.

title: Mathematicians Find a New Class of Digitally Delicate Primes
description: Despite finding no specific examples, researchers have proved the existence of a pervasive kind of prime number so delicate that changing any of its infinite digits renders it composite.

description: The mathematician Federico Ardila takes a creative approach to the search for useful answers hiding among inconceivably huge numbers of possible ones.

description: Black holes seemed to come only in sizes small and XXL. A new search strategy has uncovered a black hole of “intermediate” mass, raising hopes of more to come.

title: Finding Zen in the Art of Puzzle Solving
description: Readers used their Zen-like puzzle solving skills to discover hidden insights.

description: New data indicating that Earth’s surface broke up about 3.2 billion years ago helps clarify how plate tectonics drove the evolution of complex life.

description: The zoo of spontaneously emerging particlelike entities known as quasiparticles has grown quickly and become more and more exotic. Here are a few of the most curious and potentially useful examples.

description: A recent paper set the fastest record for multiplying two matrices. But it also marks the end of the line for a method researchers have relied on for decades to make improvements.

title: Sharon Glotzer’s Deep Curiosity About Order From Chaos
description: The computational physicist Sharon Glotzer finds unifying principles that structure the chaotic dance of the particles that make up matter.

title: Chasing the Elusive Numbers That Define Epidemics
description: Most modeling efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic have sought to address urgent practical concerns. But some groups aim to bolster the theoretical underpinnings of that work instead.

title: Why Extraterrestrial Life May Not Seem Entirely Alien
description: The zoologist Arik Kershenbaum argues that because some evolutionary challenges are truly universal, life throughout the cosmos may share certain features.

title: Pioneers Linking Math and Computer Science Win the Abel Prize
description: Avi Wigderson and László Lovász won for their work developing complexity theory and graph theory, respectively, and for connecting the two fields.

title: A New Twist Reveals Superconductivity’s Secrets
description: An unexpected superconductor was beginning to look like a fluke, but a new theory and a second discovery have revealed that emergent quasiparticles may be behind the effect.

title: Frank Wilczek on the Strong Force, Quarks and Dark Matter
description: The theoretical physicist Frank Wilczek explained what holds atomic nuclei together, and he is still pushing at the limits of what the standard model can tell us.

description: Enter the world of perfect numbers and explore the mystery mathematicians have spent thousands of years trying to solve.

description: Spurred on by quantum experiments that scramble the ordering of causes and their effects, some physicists are figuring out how to abandon causality altogether.

title: New Kind of Space Explosion Reveals the Birth of a Black Hole
description: A supernova-like explosion dubbed the Camel appears to be the result of a newborn black hole eating a star from the inside out.

title: What Is Life? Its Vast Diversity Defies Easy Definition.
description: Scientists have struggled to formulate a universal definition of life. Is it possible they don’t need one?

title: Bonnie Bassler on Talkative Bacteria and Eavesdropping Viruses
description: The molecular biologist Bonnie Bassler is deciphering the chemical languages that bacteria use to coordinate their assaults on a host.

title: New Algorithm Breaks Speed Limit for Solving Linear Equations
description: By harnessing randomness, a new algorithm achieves a fundamentally novel — and faster — way of performing one of the most basic computations in math and computer science.

title: Isadore Singer Transcended Mathematical Boundaries
description: A former graduate student reflects on how Isadore Singer, who died on February 11, brought together mathematicians, physicists and anyone else interested in the deeper connections between diverse fields.

title: Imaginary Numbers May Be Essential for Describing Reality
description: A new thought experiment indicates that quantum mechanics doesn’t work without strange numbers that turn negative when squared.

title: New Season of The Joy of x Podcast Explores Scientists’ Inner Lives
description: In a second season of enlightened conversations, Steven Strogatz and leading researchers nourish our pandemic-starved minds.

title: Neil Shubin on Tiktaalik , Ballistic Tongues and Evolution
description: The paleontologist Neil Shubin talks with host Steven Strogatz about hunting for a 375 million-year-old fossil and finding novel traits that evolved many times.

title: Statistics Postdoc Tames Decades-Old Geometry Problem
description: To the surprise of experts in the field, a postdoctoral statistician has solved one of the most important problems in high-dimensional convex geometry.

title: How to Understand COVID-19 Variants and Their Effects on Vaccines
description: Researchers are tracking the different strains of SARS-CoV-2 and studying how they spread through our population and our bodies.

title: Decades-Long Quest Reveals Details of the Proton’s Inner Antimatter
description: Twenty years ago, physicists set out to investigate a mysterious asymmetry in the proton’s interior. Their results, published today, show how antimatter helps stabilize every atom’s core.

title: Podcast Preview: The Joy of x , Season Two
description: Hosted by Steven Strogatz, The Joy of x podcast is back with new episodes that explore the inner worlds of top-tier scientists and mathematicians like Frank Wilczek, Bonnie Bassler and Amie Wilkinson.

title: Cloud-Making Aerosol Could Devastate Polar Sea Ice
description: An overlooked but powerful driver of cloud formation could accelerate the loss of polar sea ice.

title: Mathematicians Set Numbers in Motion to Unlock Their Secrets
description: A new proof demonstrates the power of arithmetic dynamics, an emerging discipline that combines insights from number theory and dynamical systems.

title: Artificial Neural Nets Finally Yield Clues to How Brains Learn
description: The learning algorithm that enables the runaway success of deep neural networks doesn’t work in biological brains, but researchers are finding alternatives that could.

title: Growing Inventory of Black Holes Offers a Radical Probe of the Cosmos
description: One black hole is nice, but astrophysicists can do a lot more science with 50 of them.

title: The Coach Who Led the U.S. Math Team Back to the Top
description: Po-Shen Loh has harnessed his competitive impulses and iconoclastic tendencies to reinvigorate the U.S. Math Olympiad program.

title: In Violation of Einstein, Black Holes Might Have ‘Hair’
description: A new study shows that extreme black holes could break the famous “no-hair” theorem, and in a way that we could detect.

title: Zen and the Art of Puzzle Solving
description: Sometimes the act of solving a puzzle can itself reveal hidden insights.

description: A group of MIT undergraduates is searching for tetrahedra that tile space, the latest effort in a millennia-long inquiry. They’ve already made a new discovery.

description: By digging out signals hidden within the brain’s electrical chatter, scientists are getting new insights into sleep, aging and more.

description: Micrometeorites constantly fall on every corner of Earth. Matthew Genge is using these shards of interplanetary space to understand Earth and its place in the solar system.

description: Unusual proteins that can quickly fold into different shapes provide cells with a novel regulatory mechanism.

description: Four mathematicians have cataloged all the tetrahedra with rational angles, resolving a question about basic geometric shapes using techniques from number theory.

description: The relationships among the properties of flexible shapes have fascinated mathematicians for centuries.

description: Three-dimensional supernova simulations have solved the mystery of why they explode at all.

description: In grafted plants, shrunken chloroplasts can jump between species by slipping through unexpected gateways in cell walls.

description: Long considered solved, David Hilbert’s question about seventh-degree polynomials is leading researchers to a new web of mathematical connections.

title: A Prodigy Who Cracked Open the Cosmos

description: A glass sponge found deep in the Pacific shows a remarkable ability to withstand compression and bending, on top of the sponge’s other unusual properties.

title: A Newfound Source of Cellular Order in the Chemistry of Life

description: “Rainbow colorings” recently led to a new proof. It’s not the first time they’ve come in handy.

title: Cori Bargmann on the Genetics of Transparent Worms, Supertasters and Cancer
description: The neurogenetics pioneer Cori Bargmann speaks with host Steven Strogatz about why a transparent worm became her favorite animal and how a genetic discovery she made inspired a revolutionary cancer treatment.

title: Axions Would Solve Another Major Problem in Physics
description: In a new paper, physicists argue that hypothetical particles called axions could explain why the universe isn’t empty.

title: Tadashi Tokieda’s Special Kind of Magic

title: How Rational Math Catches Slippery Irrational Numbers

description: To combat resistant bacteria and refill the trickling antibiotic pipeline, scientists are getting help from deep learning networks.

title: Biodiversity May Thrive Through Games of Rock-Paper-Scissors
description: Recent findings add weight to the evidence that the intransitive competitions between species enrich the diversity of nature.

title: Landmark Computer Science Proof Cascades Through Physics and Math
description: Computer scientists established a new boundary on computationally verifiable knowledge. In doing so, they solved major open problems in quantum mechanics and pure mathematics.

title: Janna Levin on Seeing and Hearing Black Holes

description: As the founding director of a new institute for fundamental research in Rwanda, the physicist Omololu Akin-Ojo hopes to stem the brain drain of Africa’s brightest minds.

description: The recent discovery of some of the first galaxies in the universe illuminates the darkest era in cosmic history.

description: A proposal for building wormhole-connected black holes offers a way to probe the paradoxes of quantum information.

description: A problem confronts cosmology: Two independent measurements of the universe’s expansion give incompatible answers. Now a third method, advanced by an astronomy pioneer, appears to bridge the divide.

title: John Urschel: From NFL Player to Mathematician
description: John Urschel, who retired from playing professional football with the Baltimore Ravens to become a mathematician, talks to host Steven Strogatz about the fascinations of graph theory that lured him away from the NFL.

title: The Animal Origins of Coronavirus and Flu
description: Zoonotic diseases like influenza and many coronaviruses start out in animals, but their biological machinery often enables them to jump to humans.

description: Faced with a decision, the brain weighs its options by bundling them into rapidly alternating cycles of brain waves.

description: Mathematicians have proved that copies of smaller graphs can always be used to perfectly cover larger ones.

description: The mathematical biologist Corina Tarnita explains to host Steven Strogatz how quantitative modeling solved the mystery of fairy circles.

description: Calculations involving a higher dimension are guiding physicists toward a misstep in Stephen Hawking’s legendary black hole analysis.

description: An experiment caught a quantum system in the middle of a jump — something the originators of quantum mechanics assumed was impossible.

title: Immune Cells Measure Time to Identify Foreign Proteins
description: Immunologists confirm an old hunch: T-cells identify what belongs in the body by timing how long they can bind to it.

title: Why the Proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem Doesn’t Need to Be Enhanced
description: Decades after the landmark proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem, ideas abound for how to make it even more reliable. But such efforts reflect a deep misunderstanding of what makes the proof so important.

title: The Body’s Clock Offers a Rhythmic Target to Viruses
description: Viruses and other parasites may sync with their host’s biological clock — or reset it — to gain an advantage.

title: Ancient DNA Yields Snapshots of Vanished Ecosystems
description: Surviving fragments of genetic material preserved in sediments allow scientists to see the full diversity of past life — even microbes.

title: What’s the Magic Behind Graphene’s ‘Magic’ Angle?
description: A new theoretical model may help explain the shocking onset of superconductivity in stacked, twisted carbon sheets.

title: Computer Scientists Expand the Frontier of Verifiable Knowledge
description: The universe of problems that a computer can check has grown. The researchers’ secret ingredient? Quantum entanglement.

title: How Geometry, Data and Neighbors Predict Your Favorite Movies
description: A little high school geometry can help you understand the basic math behind movie recommendation engines.

title: Viruses Can Scatter Their Genes Among Cells and Reassemble
description: Some viruses can replicate without infecting any one cell with all their genes.

title: The Hidden Heroines of Chaos
description: Two women programmers played a pivotal role in the birth of chaos theory. Their previously untold story illustrates the changing status of computation in science.

title: Solution: ‘The Bulldogs That Bulldogs Fight’
description: To minimize brain strain when thinking recursively, start simply, look for a pattern and let the pattern do the work.

title: As Planet Discoveries Pile Up, a Gap Appears in the Pattern
description: Astronomers are puzzling over a paucity of planets in the galaxy measuring between 1.5 and two times Earth's size.

title: In Ecology Studies and Selfless Ants, He Finds Hope for the Future
description: For more than six decades, the influential biologist Edward O. Wilson has drawn connections between evolution, ecology and behavior, often sparking controversies inside and outside of science.

title: How Feynman Diagrams Revolutionized Physics
description: In the late 1940s, Richard Feynman invented a visual tool for simplifying particle calculations that forever changed theoretical physics.

title: Out of a Magic Math Function, One Solution to Rule Them All
description: Mathematicians used “magic functions” to prove that two highly symmetric lattices solve a myriad of problems in eight- and 24-dimensional space.

title: Rapid Oxygen Changes Fueled an Explosion in Ancient Animal Diversity
description: Skyrocketing animal diversity a half-billion years ago was linked to spikes and dips in marine oxygen levels, according to a detailed geological study.

title: Black, Hot Ice May Be Nature’s Most Common Form of Water
description: A new experiment confirms the existence of “superionic ice,” a bizarre form of water that might comprise the bulk of giant icy planets throughout the universe.

title: The Subtle Art of the Mathematical Conjecture
description: It’s an educated guess, not a proof. But a good conjecture will guide math forward, pointing the way into the mathematical unknown.

title: Universal Pattern Explains Why Materials Conduct
description: Mathematicians have found that materials conduct electricity when electrons follow a universal mathematical pattern.

title: Brains Speed Up Perception by Guessing What’s Next
description: Your expectations shape and quicken your perceptions. A new model that explains how that happens also suggests it’s time to update theories about sensory perception and decision making.

title: The Sun Is Stranger Than Astrophysicists Imagined
description: The sun radiates far more high-frequency light than expected, raising questions about unknown features of the sun’s magnetic field and the possibility of even more exotic physics.

title: With a Simple Twist, a ‘Magic’ Material Is Now the Big Thing in Physics
description: The stunning emergence of a new type of superconductivity with the mere twist of a carbon sheet has left physicists giddy, and its discoverer nearly overwhelmed.

title: Dark Matter Gets a Reprieve in New Analysis
description: A strange glow coming from the Milky Way’s center was thought to be due to ordinary pulsars. But a new look at a years-old study shows that dark matter might still be responsible.

title: Scientists Discover Nearly 200,000 Kinds of Ocean Viruses
description: New work raises the estimated diversity of viruses in the seas more than twelvefold and lays the groundwork for a better understanding of their impact on global nutrient cycles.

title: A New Approach to Multiplication Opens the Door to Better Quantum Computers
description: Quantum computers can’t selectively forget information. A new algorithm for multiplication shows a way around that problem.

title: New Turmoil Over Predicting the Effects of Genes
description: Promising efforts at disentangling the effects of genes and the environment on complicated traits may have been confounded by statistical problems.

title: Icefish Study Adds Another Color to the Story of Blood
description: The rainbow of pigments that animals use for blood illustrates a central truth of evolution.

title: The Astronomer Who’d Rather Build Space Cameras
description: Jim Gunn shaped the theory of the evolution of the cosmos before building cameras and spectrographs for major observatories like the Hubble Space Telescope.

title: The Bulldogs That Bulldogs Fight
description: Solve a linguistic whodunit about a college mascot by thinking like a self-referencing computer subroutine.

title: Heat-Loving Microbes, Once Dormant, Thrive Over Decades-Old Fire
description: In harsh ecosystems around the world, microbiologists are finding evidence that “microbial seed banks” protect biodiversity from changing conditions.

title: Viruses Have a Secret, Altruistic Social Life
description: Researchers are beginning to understand the ways in which viruses strategically manipulate and cooperate with one another.

title: Mathematicians Discover the Perfect Way to Multiply
description: By chopping up large numbers into smaller ones, researchers have rewritten a fundamental mathematical speed limit.

title: What the Sight of a Black Hole Means to a Black Hole Physicist
description: The astrophysicist Janna Levin reflects on the newly unveiled, first-ever photograph of a black hole.

title: Researchers Rethink the Ancestry of Complex Cells
description: New studies revise ideas about the symbiosis that gave mitochondria to cells and about whether the last common ancestor of all eukaryotes was one cell or many.

title: The Scientist Who Cooks Up the Skies of Faraway Worlds
description: Astronomers will soon take their first glance at the atmosphere of a distant exoplanet. Sarah Hörst is writing the guidebook for these exoplanetary explorers, one that will reveal what a distinctive atmosphere says about the world underneath.

title: Scientists Discover Exotic New Patterns of Synchronization
description: In a world seemingly filled with chaos, physicists have discovered new forms of synchronization and are learning how to predict and control them.

title: Usain Bolt’s Split Times and the Power of Calculus
description: Just how fast can the fastest human run? This adapted book excerpt from Infinite Powers reveals how calculus helps us investigate the nature of motion and change.

title: Cryptography That Is Provably Secure
description: Researchers have just released hacker-proof cryptographic code — programs with the same level of invincibility as a mathematical proof.

title: In Quantum Games, There’s No Way to Play the Odds
description: These games combine quantum entanglement, infinity and impossible-to-calculate winning probabilities. But if researchers can crack them, they’ll reveal deep mathematical secrets.

title: Goals and Rewards Redraw the Brain’s Map of the World
description: Two new studies show that the brain’s navigation system changes how it represents physical space to reflect personal experience.

title: Proof Finds That All Change Is a Mix of Order and Randomness
description: All descriptions of change are a unique blend of chance and determinism, according to the sweeping mathematical proof of the “weak Pinsker conjecture.”

title: Sum-of-Three-Cubes Problem Solved for ‘Stubborn’ Number 33
description: A number theorist with programming prowess has found a solution to 33 = x³ + y³ + z³, a much-studied equation that went unsolved for 64 years.

title: How the Brain Links Gestures, Perception and Meaning
description: Neuroscience has found that gestures are not merely important as tools of expression but as guides of cognition and perception.

title: Solution: ‘How to Find Simple Treasures in Complex Numbers’
description: Puzzle solvers used “imaginary” numbers to solve a real world problem: finding long-lost treasure.

title: She Finds Clues to Future Sustainability in Old Food Webs
description: By reconstructing prehistoric food webs and analyzing the diverse interactions of humans with other species, the ecologist Jennifer Dunne is developing a new understanding of sustainability through network science.

title: Quantum Machine Appears to Defy Universe’s Push for Disorder
description: One of the first quantum simulators has produced a puzzling phenomenon: a row of atoms that repeatedly pops back into place.

title: Karen Uhlenbeck, Uniter of Geometry and Analysis, Wins Abel Prize
description: A founder of modern geometric analysis who produced “some of the most dramatic advances in mathematics in the last 40 years,” Uhlenbeck is the first woman to be awarded this top honor.

title: Biologists Discover Unknown Powers in Mighty Mitochondria
description: Mitochondria are most famous as sources of metabolic energy. But by splitting and combining, they can also release chemical signals to regulate cell activities, including the generation of neurons.

title: Where Proof, Evidence and Imagination Intersect
description: In mathematics, where proofs are everything, evidence is important too. But evidence is only as good as the model, and modeling can be dangerous business. So how much evidence is enough?

title: The Math That Tells Cells What They Are
description: During development, cells seem to decode their fate through optimal information processing, which could hint at a more general principle of life.

title: Math Duo Maps the Infinite Terrain of Minimal Surfaces
description: A pair of mathematicians has built on an obscure, 30-year-old mathematical theory to show that soap-filmlike minimal surfaces appear abundantly in a wide range of shapes.

title: How Artificial Intelligence Is Changing Science
description: The latest AI algorithms are probing the evolution of galaxies, calculating quantum wave functions, discovering new chemical compounds and more. Is there anything that scientists do that can’t be automated?

description: Astronomers claim in a new paper that star motions should make it easy for civilizations to spread across the galaxy, but still we might find ourselves alone.

title: Neuroscience Readies for a Showdown Over Consciousness Ideas
description: To make headway on the mystery of consciousness, some researchers are trying a rigorous new way to test competing theories.

title: The Universe’s Ultimate Complexity Revealed by Simple Quantum Games
description: A two-player game can reveal whether the universe has an infinite amount of complexity.

description: No new particles have been found at the Large Hadron Collider since the Higgs boson in 2012, but physicists say there’s much we can still learn from the Higgs itself.

description: Brief cosmic blips called fast radio bursts have puzzled astronomers since their discovery earlier this decade. Now researchers appear to be close to understanding what powers them.

title: Doudna’s Confidence in CRISPR’s Research Potential Burns Bright
description: Jennifer Doudna, one of CRISPR’s primary innovators, stays optimistic about how the gene-editing tool will continue to empower basic biological understanding.

description: As researchers delve deeper into the behavior of decentralized collective systems, they’re beginning to question some of their initial assumptions.

description: Physicists have devised a holographic model of “de Sitter space,” the term for a universe like ours, that could give us new clues about the origin of space and time.

title: Möbius Strips Defy a Link With Infinity
description: A new proof shows why an uncountably infinite number of Möbius strips will never fit into a three-dimensional space.

title: New Squid Genome Shines Light on Symbiotic Evolution
description: Researchers hope that the genes of a glowing squid can illuminate how animals evolved organs for beneficial bacteria.

title: How to Find Simple Treasures in Complex Numbers
description: In spite of their name, “imaginary” numbers are as real as any other numbers, especially when it comes to hunting for lost treasure.

title: Mysterious Quantum Rule Reconstructed From Scratch
description: The new work promises to give researchers a better grip on the core mystery of quantum mechanics.

title: How the Brain Creates a Timeline of the Past
description: The brain can’t directly encode the passage of time, but recent work hints at a workaround for putting timestamps on memories of events.

title: Smaller Is Better: Why Finite Number Systems Pack More Punch
description: Recent progress on the “sum product” problem recalls a celebrated mathematical result that revealed the power of miniature number systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Finds Ancient ‘Ghosts’ in Modern DNA
description: With the help of deep learning techniques, paleoanthropologists find evidence of long-lost branches on the human family tree.

title: How a Strange Grid Reveals Hidden Connections Between Simple Numbers
description: A graduate student has helped illuminate a long-suspected connection between addition and multiplication.

title: Fragile DNA Enables New Adaptations to Evolve Quickly
description: If highly repetitive gene-regulating sequences in DNA are easily lost, that may explain why some adaptations evolve quickly and repeatedly.

title: An Astrophysicist Who Maps the Universe’s Terra Incognita
description: Priyamvada Natarajan has pioneered the mapping and modeling of the universe’s invisible contents, especially dark matter and supermassive black holes.

title: Foundations Built for a General Theory of Neural Networks
description: Neural networks can be as unpredictable as they are powerful. Now mathematicians are beginning to reveal how a neural network’s form will influence its function.

description: Among these cave insects, the females evolved to have penises — twice. The reasons challenge common assumptions about sex.

title: The Double Life of Black Holes
description: Perfect black holes are versatile mathematical tools. Just don’t mistake them for the real thing.

title: The Trouble With Turbulence
description: Turbulence is everywhere, yet it is one of the most difficult concepts for physicists to understand.

title: A Child’s Puzzle Has Helped Unlock the Secrets of Magnetism
description: People have known about magnets since ancient times, but the physics of ferromagnetism remains a mystery. Now a familiar puzzle is getting physicists closer to the answer.

title: Gene Drives Work in Mice (if They’re Female)
description: Biologists have demonstrated for the first time that a controversial genetic engineering technology works, with caveats, in mammals.

title: A Movement to Close the Gender Gap in Mathematics
description: The Brazilian mathematician Carolina Araujo, who calls herself “a bit of an anarchist,” is organizing meetings and building a support network to study and solve the problems women face in mathematics.

title: Asteroid Rate Jumped in Solar System’s Past
description: An analysis of lunar craters has found that we’ve been living in a relatively violent period in cosmic history.

description: A science fiction novelist and an internet commenter made breakthroughs on a longstanding problem about the number of ways you can arrange a set of items. What did they discover?

title: How Nearby Stellar Explosions Could Have Killed Off Large Animals
description: Subatomic particles called muons are thought to have streamed through the atmosphere and irradiated megafauna like the monster shark megalodon.

title: The Brain Maps Out Ideas and Memories Like Spaces
description: Emerging evidence suggests that the brain encodes abstract knowledge in the same way that it represents positions in space, which hints at a more universal theory of cognition.

title: A New Approach to Understanding How Machines Think
description: Neural networks are famously incomprehensible, so Been Kim is developing a “translator for humans.”

description: Astronomers couldn’t find enough satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way. Now they have the opposite problem.

title: Jellyfish Genome Hints That Complexity Isn’t Genetically Complex
description: Jellyfish didn’t need novel genes to take an evolutionary leap in complexity.

title: Why the Best Place to Find Dark Matter May Be in a Rock
description: Dark matter may occasionally interact with minerals in the earth, leaving telltale tracks that physicists hope to decipher.

title: How Space and Time Could Be a Quantum Error-Correcting Code
description: The same codes needed to thwart errors in quantum computers may also give the fabric of space-time its intrinsic robustness.

title: Ancient Turing Pattern Builds Feathers, Hair — and Now, Shark Skin
description: A primordial developmental toolkit shared by all vertebrates, and described by a theory of the mathematician Alan Turing, sets the growth pattern for all types of skin structures.

description: Celebrate a year’s worth of scientific and mathematical insights by solving this brain-teasing cryptic crossword from our puzzle columnist.

title: The Year in Math and Computer Science
description: Several mathematicians under the age of 30 left their marks all over the field, and amateur problem-solvers of all ages made significant contributions to long-dormant puzzles.

description: Biologists gained new insights into life’s genomically tumultuous past, viruses as crucial components of life, the hidden talents of complex cells and basic aspects of cognition and memory.

description: The field of fundamental physics is experiencing both a period of confusion and an openness to new ideas.

title: How Complex Wholes Emerge From Simple Parts

description: In a Paris lab, researchers have shown for the first time that quantum methods of transmitting information are superior to classical ones.

description: Planetary geologist Meenakshi Wadhwa uses Martian meteorites to trace the history of our solar system.

description: Digital security depends on the difficulty of factoring large numbers. A new proof shows why one method for breaking digital encryption won’t work.

description: Two independent papers vanquish lingering doubts about LIGO’s historic discovery of gravitational waves.

title: A ‘Self-Aware’ Fish Raises Doubts About a Cognitive Test
description: A report that a fish can pass the “mirror test” for self-awareness reignites debates about how to define and measure that elusive quality.

description: Neither animal, plant, fungus nor familiar protozoan, a strange microbe that sits in its own “supra-kingdom” of life foretells incredible biodiversity yet to be discovered by new sequencing technologies.

title: In the Universe of Equations, Virtually All Are Prime
description: Equations, like numbers, cannot always be split into simpler elements.

title: Why Black Hole Interiors Grow (Almost) Forever
description: The renowned physicist Leonard Susskind has identified a possible quantum origin for the ever-growing volume of black holes.

title: On the Best Use of Science to Safeguard Humanity
description: For 50 years, the astrophysicist Martin Rees has contributed to our understanding of cosmology. Now he is speaking up about the promise and potential dangers of the science and technology that will arrive over the next 50 years and beyond.

title: What Defines a Stem Cell? Scientists Rethink the Answer
description: As it becomes clear that the body’s cells have more diverse regenerative capabilities than expected, experts have had to reconsider their approach to stem cell research.

title: New Quantum Paradox Clarifies Where Our Views of Reality Go Wrong
description: The Frauchiger-Renner thought experiment has shaken up the world of quantum foundations.

title: Mathematical Simplicity May Drive Evolution’s Speed
description: Some researchers are using a complexity framework thought to be purely theoretical to understand evolutionary dynamics in biological and computational systems.

title: A Universal Law for the ‘Blood of the Earth’
description: Simple physical principles can be used to describe how rivers grow everywhere from Florida to Mars.

title: A Collector of Math and Physics Surprises
description: Tadashi Tokieda discovers new physical phenomena by looking at the everyday world with the eyes of a child.

title: ‘Lava-Lamp’ Proteins May Help Cells Cheat Death
description: With proteins that reversibly self-assemble into droplets, cells may control their metabolism — and harden themselves against harsh conditions.

title: Quanta Writers and Editors Discuss Trends in Science and Math
description: On November 16, 2018, more than 200 readers joined writers and editors from Quanta Magazine for a wide-ranging panel discussion that examined the newest ideas in fundamental physics, biology and mathematics research.

title: Galactic Beacons Get Snuffed Out in a Cosmic Eyeblink
description: Quasars powered by supermassive black holes have been unexpectedly vanishing. Scientists have started to figure out why.

description: How does evolution select the fittest “individuals” when they are ecosystems made up of hosts and their microbiomes? Biologist debate the need to revise theories.

title: Universal Quantum Phenomenon Found in Strange Metals
description: Experiments suggest that exotic superconducting materials share a “strange metal” state characterized by a quantum speed limit that somehow acts as a fundamental organizing principle.

title: Amateur Mathematician Finds Smallest Universal Cover
description: Through exacting geometric calculations, Philip Gibbs has found the smallest known cover for any possible shape.

description: In the latest campaign to reconcile Einstein’s theory of gravity with quantum mechanics, many physicists are studying how a higher dimensional space that includes gravity arises like a hologram from a lower dimensional particle theory.

description: A scientist and programmer with a literary bent, Valeria Pettorino thinks multiple angles and diverse points of view are needed to unriddle the nature of dark matter and dark energy.

description: Stem cells seem to retain memories of old injuries to improve future healing. When that system goes wrong, chronic inflammation can result.

description: Puzzle solvers explored how evolution may have used negative and positive control mechanisms to shape the conflicting parental functions of reproduction and child rearing.

title: Theorists Debate How ‘Neutral’ Evolution Really Is
description: For 50 years, evolutionary theory has emphasized the importance of neutral mutations rather than adaptive ones at the level of DNA. Real genomic data challenges that assumption.

description: Alexander Smith’s work on the Goldfeld conjecture reveals fundamental characteristics of elliptic curves.

description: Using a new CRISPR-based technique, researchers are examining how the position of DNA within the nucleus affects gene expression and cell function.

title: Mystery Math Whiz and Novelist Advance Permutation Problem
description: A new proof from the Australian science fiction writer Greg Egan and a 2011 proof anonymously posted online are now being hailed as significant advances on a puzzle mathematicians have been studying for at least 25 years.

description: The astrochemist and winner of the 2018 Kavli Prize in Astrophysics has wondered about the cosmic origin of water while enjoying Noordwijk beach near her hometown of Leiden.

description: A new statistical model appears to undermine long-held assumptions in number theory. How much should it be trusted when all that really matters is proof?

title: Astronomers Creep Up to the Edge of the Milky Way’s Black Hole
description: Hot spots have been discovered orbiting just outside the supermassive black hole at the galaxy’s center. Their motions have given us the closest look at that violent environment.

description: As chemists tie the most complicated molecular knot yet, biophysicists create a “periodic table” that describes what kinds of knots are possible.

title: The (Imaginary) Numbers at the Edge of Reality
description: Odd enough to potentially model the strangeness of the physical world, complex numbers with “imaginary” components are rooted in the familiar.

title: Prepping for a Flood of Heavenly Bodies
description: Mario Jurić is leading the push to get astronomy ready for the torrents of data that are about to flow.

title: A Proof About Where Symmetries Can’t Exist
description: In a major mathematical achievement, a small team of researchers has proven Zimmer’s conjecture.

title: World’s Oldest Fossils Now Appear to Be Squished Rocks
description: Evidence for life in 3.7-billion-year-old rocks appears to be crumbling away.

title: Why the Many-Worlds Interpretation Has Many Problems
description: The idea that the universe splits into multiple realities with every measurement has become an increasingly popular proposed solution to the mysteries of quantum mechanics. But this “many-worlds interpretation” is incoherent, Philip Ball argues in this adapted excerpt from his new book Beyond Weird.

title: How Equality and Inequality Shape the Birds and the Bees
description: Two dynamic, seemingly opposing forces likely played an important role in the evolution of reproduction and child rearing in social animals like bees and humans.

title: ‘Broadband’ Networks of Viruses May Help Bacteria Evolve Faster
description: A newly discovered mechanism may enable viruses to shuttle genes between bacteria 1,000 times as often as was thought — making them a major force in those cells’ evolution.

title: In the Ticking of the Embryonic Clock, She Finds Answers
description: Renee Reijo Pera has spent decades uncovering how the timing of embryonic development contributes to health and disease.

title: Famous Experiment Dooms Alternative to Quantum Weirdness
description: Oil droplets guided by “pilot waves” have failed to reproduce the results of the quantum double-slit experiment, crushing a century-old dream that there exists a single, concrete reality.

title: Interstellar Visitor Found to Be Unlike a Comet or an Asteroid
description: The mystery of ’Oumuamua, the first interstellar object ever observed, continues to deepen.

title: Forests Emerge as a Major Overlooked Climate Factor
description: New work at the intersection of atmospheric science and ecology is finding that forests can influence rainfall and climate from across a continent.

title: Graduate Student Solves Quantum Verification Problem
description: Urmila Mahadev spent eight years in graduate school solving one of the most basic questions in quantum computation: How do you know whether a quantum computer has done anything quantum at all?

title: Planets Found to Be Larger Than the Disks They Come From
description: The new finding is challenging established theories of how planets come to be.

title: Three Biochemists Win Chemistry Nobel for Directing Evolution
description: By using the power of evolution to solve practical problems, three researchers opened new avenues to chemical discovery.

title: Laser Physicists, Including Third Woman Ever, Win Physics Nobel
description: Three researchers shared the Nobel Prize in Physics for advances in laser physics. The winners include a woman for the first time in 55 years.

title: Unexpected Diversity Found in 16 New Lab Mouse Genomes
description: The availability of 16 new mouse genomes will help accelerate research into the genetic underpinnings of human traits and diseases.

title: Nobel Prize Awarded for Cancer Immunotherapy
description: James P. Allison and Tasuku Honjo shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing ways to unleash the immune system more effectively against cancers.

title: ‘Traffic Jams’ of Cells Help to Sculpt Embryos
description: By measuring mechanical forces inside an embryo for the first time, researchers have shown how a physical “jamming” mechanism assists development.

title: How Nature Defies Math in Keeping Ecosystems Stable
description: Paradoxically, the abundance of tight interactions among living species usually leads to disasters in ecological models. New analyses hint at how nature seemingly defies the math.

title: ‘Quantum Atmospheres’ May Reveal Secrets of Matter
description: A new theory proposes that the quantum properties of an object extend into an “atmosphere” that surrounds the material.

title: Titans of Mathematics Clash Over Epic Proof of ABC Conjecture
description: Two mathematicians have found what they say is a hole at the heart of a proof that has convulsed the mathematics community for nearly six years.

description: A visual prank exposes an Achilles’ heel of computer vision systems: Unlike humans, they can’t do a double take.

title: A Short History of the Missing Universe
description: Astronomers have known where the universe’s missing matter has been hiding for the past 20 years. So why did it take so long to find it?

title: New AI Strategy Mimics How Brains Learn to Smell
description: Machine learning techniques are commonly based on how the visual system processes information. To beat their limitations, scientists are drawing inspiration from the sense of smell.

title: Why Mathematicians Can’t Find the Hay in a Haystack
description: In math, sometimes the most common things are the hardest to find.

title: On Waste Plastics at Sea, She Finds Unique Microbial Multitudes
description: Maria-Luiza Pedrotti is illuminating the unseen worlds of plastic-eating bacteria that teem in massive ocean garbage patches.

title: World’s Simplest Animal Reveals Hidden Diversity
description: The first animal genus defined purely by genetic characters represents a new era for the sorting and naming of animals.

title: A New Test for the Leading Big Bang Theory
description: Cosmologists have predicted the existence of an oscillating signal that could distinguish between cosmic inflation and alternative theories of the universe’s birth.

title: The Last of the Universe’s Ordinary Matter Has Been Found
description: For decades, astronomers weren’t able to find all of the atomic matter in the universe. A series of recent papers has revealed where it’s been hiding.

title: Solution: ‘Evolutionary Math and Just-So Stories’
description: How much stock should we put in mathematical models of evolution that have not been validated by rigorous empirical data?

description: The 19th-century discovery of numbers called “quaternions” gave mathematicians a way to describe rotations in space, forever changing physics and math.

description: An upstart field that simplifies complex shapes is letting mathematicians understand how those shapes depend on the space in which you visualize them.
