description: Computer vision researchers have uncovered a world of visual signals hiding in our midst, including subtle motions that betray what’s being said and faint images of what’s around a corner.

title: To Heal Some Wounds, Adult Cells Turn More Fetal
description: Once again, body cells reveal unexpected plasticity: In a newly discovered type of wound healing, which some researchers call “paligenosis,” adult cells revert to a more fetal state.

title: To Understand Volcanoes on Other Worlds, Stand On Our Own
description: Rosaly Lopes has visited dozens of active volcanoes on Earth and discovered even more elsewhere in the solar system. Her work is helping to establish whether volcanoes on distant moons could create conditions friendly to life.

title: The End of Theoretical Physics as We Know It
description: Computer simulations and custom-built quantum analogues are changing what it means to search for the laws of nature.

title: The Universal Pattern Popping Up in Math, Physics and Biology
description: Quanta’s In Theory video series returns with an exploration of a mysterious mathematical pattern found throughout nature.

title: Black Hole Firewalls Could Be Too Tepid to Burn
description: String theorists elide a paradox about black holes by extinguishing the walls of fire feared to surround them.

title: You Are Getting Sleepy — Tagged Proteins May Point to Why
description: The identification of SNIPPs, a set of proteins found primarily at the brain’s synapses, brings science closer to understanding why we need to sleep.

title: How Network Math Can Help You Make Friends
description: Studying the structure of existing friendships in your community can help you forge the best connections when forming a new circle of friends.

title: ‘Functional Fingerprint’ May Identify Brains Over a Lifetime
description: A unique neurological “functional fingerprint” allows scientists to explore the influence of genetics, environment and aging on brain connectivity.

title: Evolutionary Math and Just-So Stories
description: Evolutionary stories like the grandmother hypothesis are easy to construct from mathematical models, but how well do they reflect reality?

title: How Insulin Helped Create Ant Societies
description: Evolution may have coopted an ancient metabolic mechanism to set social insects on the path toward one of the most puzzling behaviors found in nature.

title: Universal Method to Sort Complex Information Found
description: The nearest neighbor problem asks where a new point fits into an existing data set. A few researchers set out to prove that there was no universal way to solve it. Instead, they found such a way.

title: Dark Energy May Be Incompatible With String Theory
description: A controversial new paper argues that universes with dark energy profiles like ours do not exist in the “landscape” of universes allowed by string theory.

title: Star-Swallowing Black Holes Reveal Secrets in Exotic Light Shows
description: Black holes occasionally reveal themselves when passing stars get ripped apart by their gravity. These tidal disruption events have created a new way for astronomers to map the hidden cosmos.

title: A Number Theorist Who Bridges Math and Time
description: Akshay Venkatesh, a former prodigy who struggled with the genius stereotype, has won a Fields Medal for his “profound contributions to an exceptionally broad range of subjects in mathematics.”

title: A Poet of Computation Who Uncovers Distant Truths
description: The theoretical computer scientist Constantinos Daskalakis has won the Rolf Nevanlinna Prize for explicating core questions in game theory and machine learning.

title: A Master of Numbers and Shapes Who Is Rewriting Arithmetic
description: The 30-year-old math sensation Peter Scholze is now one of the youngest Fields medalists for “the revolution that he launched in arithmetic geometry.”

title: An Innovator Who Brings Order to an Infinitude of Equations
description: The mathematician Caucher Birkar was born on a subsistence farm and raised in the middle of the brutal war between Iran and Iraq. After fleeing to England, he has gone on to impose order on a wild landscape of mathematical equations.

title: A Traveler Who Finds Stability in the Natural World
description: The mathematician Alessio Figalli is rarely in one place for very long. But his work has established the stability of everything from crystals to weather fronts by using concepts derived from Napoleonic fortifications.

title: Major Quantum Computing Advance Made Obsolete by Teenager
description: 18-year-old Ewin Tang has proven that classical computers can solve the “recommendation problem” nearly as fast as quantum computers. The result eliminates one of the best examples of quantum speedup.

title: A Math Theory for Why People Hallucinate
description: Psychedelic drugs can trigger characteristic hallucinations, which have long been thought to hold clues about the brain’s circuitry. After nearly a century of study, a possible explanation is crystallizing.

title: Swarming Bacteria Create an ‘Impossible’ Superfluid
description: Researchers explore a loophole that extracts useful energy from a fluid’s seemingly random motion. The secret? Sugar and asymmetry.

title: Closed Loophole Confirms the Unreality of the Quantum World
description: A quickly closed loophole has proved that the “great smoky dragon” of quantum mechanics may forever elude capture.

title: To Remember, the Brain Must Actively Forget
description: Researchers find evidence that neural systems actively remove memories, suggesting that forgetting may be the default mode of the brain.

title: How Artificial Intelligence Can Supercharge the Search for New Particles
description: In the hunt for new fundamental particles, physicists have always had to make assumptions about how the particles will behave. New machine learning algorithms don’t.

title: The Peculiar Math That Could Underlie the Laws of Nature
description: New findings are fueling an old suspicion that fundamental particles and forces spring from strange eight-part numbers called “octonions.”

title: Three Major Physics Discoveries and Counting
description: Sau Lan Wu spent decades working to establish the Standard Model of particle physics. Now she’s searching for what lies beyond it.

title: Why Nature Prefers Couples, Even for Yeast
description: Some species have the equivalent of many more than two sexes, but most do not. A new model suggests the reason depends on how often they mate.

title: A Short Guide to Hard Problems
description: What’s easy for a computer to do, and what’s almost impossible? Those questions form the core of computational complexity. We present a map of the landscape.

title: Neutrinos Linked With Cosmic Source for the First Time
description: High-energy neutrinos have been traced back to a flaring supermassive black hole known as a blazar. The long-sought link opens the door to an entirely new way to study the universe.

title: The Hunt for Earth’s Deep Hidden Oceans
description: Water-bearing minerals reveal that Earth’s mantle could hold more water than all its oceans. Researchers now ask: Where did it all come from?

title: To Make Sense of the Present, Brains May Predict the Future
description: A controversial theory suggests that perception, motor control, memory and other brain functions all depend on comparisons between ongoing actual experiences and the brain’s modeled expectations.

title: Slime Molds Remember — but Do They Learn?
description: Evidence mounts that organisms without nervous systems can in some sense learn and solve problems, but researchers disagree about whether this is “primitive cognition.”

title: What Is the Sun Made Of and When Will It Die?
description: If and when physicists are able to pin down the metal content of the sun, that number could upend much of what we thought we knew about the evolution and life span of stars.

title: Why Can’t We Find Planet Nine?
description: Astronomers suspect that there’s a large planet hiding out in the distant fringes of the solar system. At a recent workshop, they brainstormed ways to coax it into view.

title: Salamander’s Genome Guards Secrets of Limb Regrowth
description: With a fully sequenced genome in hand, scientists hope they are finally poised to learn how axolotls regenerate lost body parts.

title: Solution: ‘The Slippery Math of Causation’
description: The all-too-intuitive picture of a straight arrow going from cause to effect is far too simplistic to describe the real world.

title: The Young Milky Way Collided With a Dwarf Galaxy
description: Astronomers have found stars dating from a long-ago collision between the Milky Way and another galaxy. The crash helps to explain why the Milky Way looks the way it does.

title: Mathematicians Tame Turbulence in Flattened Fluids
description: By squeezing fluids into flat sheets, researchers can get a handle on the strange ways that turbulence feeds energy into a system instead of eating it away.

title: Mathematics Shows How to Ensure Evolution
description: New results emerging from graph theory prove that the way a population is organized can guarantee the eventual triumph of natural selection — or permanently thwart it.

title: Real-Life Schrödinger’s Cats Probe the Boundary of the Quantum World
description: Recent experiments have put relatively large objects into quantum states, illuminating the processes by which the ordinary world emerges out of the quantum one.

title: Finally, a Problem That Only Quantum Computers Will Ever Be Able to Solve
description: Computer scientists have been searching for years for a type of problem that a quantum computer can solve but that any possible future classical computer cannot. Now they’ve found one.

title: Theory Suggests That All Genes Affect Every Complex Trait
description: The more closely geneticists look at complex traits and diseases, the harder it gets to find active genes that don’t play some part in them.

title: Her Key to Modeling Brains: Ignore the Right Details
description: Being able to think like a physicist helps Carina Curto, a mathematician-turned-neuroscientist, pull insights about the human brain out of theoretical models.

title: Four Is Not Enough
description: How many colors do you need to color an infinite plane so that no points 1 unit apart are the same color?

title: Brains May Teeter Near Their Tipping Point
description: In a renewed attempt at a grand unified theory of brain function, physicists now argue that brains optimize performance by staying near — though not exactly at — the critical point between two phases.

title: Too Small for Big Muscles, Tiny Animals Use Springs
description: Elastic springs help tiny animals stay fast and strong. New work is finding what size critters must be to benefit from the springs.

title: The Universe Is Not a Simulation, but We Can Now Simulate It
description: Computer simulations have become so accurate that cosmologists can now use them to study dark matter, supermassive black holes and other mysteries of the real evolving cosmos.

title: The Physics of Glass Opens a Window Into Biology
description: The physicist Lisa Manning studies the dynamics of glassy materials to understand embryonic development and disease.

title: Why Earth’s Cracked Crust May Be Essential for Life
description: Life needs more than water alone. Recent discoveries suggest that plate tectonics has played a critical role in nourishing life on Earth. The findings carry major consequences for the search for life elsewhere in the universe.

title: Overtaxed Working Memory Knocks the Brain Out of Sync
description: Researchers find that when working memory gets overburdened, dialogue between three brain regions breaks down. The discovery provides new support for a larger concept about how the brain works.

title: Victoria Meadows’ Earthly Visions of Alien Life
description: A living, breathing garden in Seattle serves as the perfect backdrop to an astrobiologist’s search for life on faraway planets.

title: There Are No Laws of Physics. There’s Only the Landscape.
description: Scientists seek a single description of reality. But modern physics allows for many different descriptions, many equivalent to one another, connected through a vast landscape of mathematical possibility.

title: Evidence Found for a New Fundamental Particle
description: An experiment at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory near Chicago has detected far more electron neutrinos than predicted — a possible harbinger of a revolutionary new elementary particle called the sterile neutrino, though many physicists remain skeptical.

title: CRISPR Gene-Editing Pioneers Win Kavli Prize for Nanoscience
description: The inventors of a “Swiss army knife” for genome editing received prestigious honors, as did pioneering scientists in astrophysics and neuroscience.

title: The Slippery Math of Causation
description: If a forest is burning and we don’t know what’s responsible, does it have a cause?

title: Cores From Coral Reefs Hold Secrets of the Seas’ Past and Future
description: Layered deposits of coral skeletons hold vast stores of environmental data from thousands of years ago, including annual records of ocean temperatures, water pollution and storm activity.

title: Questioning Truth, Reality and the Role of Science
description: In an era when untestable ideas such as the multiverse hold sway, Michela Massimi defends science from those who think it hopelessly unmoored from physical reality.

title: A Classical Math Problem Gets Pulled Into the Modern World
description: A century ago, the great mathematician David Hilbert posed a probing question in pure mathematics. A recent advance in optimization theory is bringing Hilbert’s work into a world of self-driving cars.

title: How Brain Waves Surf Sound Waves to Process Speech
description: By paying more attention to behaviors, and not just the activity of neurons, two researchers critical of most neuroscience learned how brains make sense of spoken language.

title: Stellar Disks Reveal How Planets Get Made
description: Detailed images of disks swirling around young stars show the details of how solar systems come to be.

title: Mathematicians Disprove Conjecture Made to Save Black Holes
description: Mathematicians have disproved the strong cosmic censorship conjecture. Their work answers one of the most important questions in the study of general relativity and changes the way we think about space-time.

title: A New World’s Extraordinary Orbit Points to Planet Nine
description: Astronomers argue that there’s an undiscovered giant planet far beyond the orbit of Neptune. A newly discovered rocky body has added evidence to the circumstantial case for it.

title: To Build Truly Intelligent Machines, Teach Them Cause and Effect
description: Judea Pearl, a pioneering figure in artificial intelligence, argues that AI has been stuck in a decades-long rut. His prescription for progress? Teach machines to understand the question why.

title: A Chemist Shines Light on a Surprising Prime Number Pattern
description: When a crystallographer treated prime numbers as a system of particles, the resulting diffraction pattern created a new view of existing conjectures in number theory.

title: Vaccines Are Pushing Pathogens to Evolve
description: Just as antibiotics have bred resistance in bacteria, vaccines can potentially lose their effectiveness over diseases they controlled. Researchers are working to head off the evolution of new threats.

title: Artificial Neural Nets Grow Brainlike Navigation Cells
description: Faced with a navigational challenge, neural networks spontaneously evolved units resembling the grid cells that help living animals find their way.

title: What Astronomers Are Learning From Gaia’s New Milky Way Map
description: A roundup of some of the most important discoveries gleaned so far from the Gaia space observatory’s new map of the galaxy.

title: A Thermodynamic Answer to Why Birds Migrate
description: New modeling studies suggest that birds migrate to strike a favorable balance between their input and output of energy.

title: Three Decades Later, Mystery Numbers Explained
description: Zeta values seem to connect distant geometric worlds. In a new proof, mathematicians finally explain why.

title: Cells Talk in a Language That Looks Like Viruses
description: Disease-causing viruses and message-carrying vesicles sit at the ends of a spectrum of membranous particles that cells release.

title: A Radically Conservative Solution for Cosmology’s Biggest Mystery
description: Two ways of measuring the universe’s expansion rate yield two conflicting answers. Many point to the possibility of new physics at work, but a new analysis argues that unseen errors could be to blame.

title: Troubled Times for Alternatives to Einstein’s Theory of Gravity
description: New observations of extreme astrophysical systems have “brutally and pitilessly murdered” attempts to replace Einstein’s general theory of relativity.

title: Solution: ‘The DNA Computer Program’
description: Computer code serves as a useful analogy for what our genes do, but the complexity and messiness of life go well beyond simple analogies and mathematical models.

title: Cell by Cell, Scientists Map the Genetic Steps as Eggs Become Animals
description: For the first time, researchers have traced the genetic programs that guide the development of each cell in early embryos. Surprisingly, even cells that start out different can end up the same.

title: First Big Steps Toward Proving the Unique Games Conjecture
description: The latest in a new series of proofs brings theoretical computer scientists within striking distance of one of the great conjectures of their discipline.

title: Chronological Clues to Life’s Early History Lurk in Gene Transfers
description: To date the branches on the evolutionary tree of life, researchers are looking at horizontal gene transfers among ancient microorganisms, which once seemed only to muddle the record.

title: Cells Talk and Help One Another via Tiny Tube Networks
description: Long-overlooked “tunneling nanotubes” and other bridges between cells act as conduits for sharing RNA, proteins or even whole organelles.

title: How Many Genes Do Cells Need? Maybe Almost All of Them
description: An ambitious study in yeast shows that the health of cells depends on the highly intertwined effects of many genes, few of which can be deleted together without consequence.

title: Machine Learning’s ‘Amazing’ Ability to Predict Chaos
description: In new computer experiments, artificial-intelligence algorithms can tell the future of chaotic systems.

title: Decades-Old Graph Problem Yields to Amateur Mathematician
description: By making the first progress on the “chromatic number of the plane” problem in over 60 years, an anti-aging pundit has achieved mathematical immortality.

title: Ultra-Accurate Clocks Lead Search for New Laws of Physics
description: Atomic clocks are letting physicists tighten the lasso around elusive phenomena such as dark matter.

title: Trouble Detected in Infamous Dark Matter Signal
description: Independent scientists have cast serious doubt on a claimed detection of dark matter.

title: A Revealer of Secrets in the Data of Life and the Universe
description: The statistician Donald Richards lives to uncover subtle patterns hiding in real-world data.

title: The Elusive Calculus of Insects’ Altruism and Kin Selection
description: How the ultra-cooperative behavior of ants, bees and other social insects could have evolved continues to challenge formal analysis. But a new theory about hedging bets against nature’s unpredictability may change the math and shift the debate.

title: Mathematicians Explore Mirror Link Between Two Geometric Worlds
description: Decades after physicists happened upon a stunning mathematical coincidence, researchers are getting close to understanding the link between two seemingly unrelated geometric universes.

title: How the DNA Computer Program Makes You and Me
description: Can a set of simple instructions produce complex, three-dimensional living structures?

title: New Brain Maps With Unmatched Detail May Change Neuroscience
description: A technique based on genetic bar codes can easily map the connections of individual brain cells in unprecedented numbers. Unexpected complexity in the visual system is only the first secret it has revealed.

title: Quantum Correlations Reverse Thermodynamic Arrow of Time
description: A recent experiment shows how quantum mechanics can make heat flow from a cold body to a hot one, an apparent (though not real) violation of the second law of thermodynamics.

title: Why Winning in Rock-Paper-Scissors (and in Life) Isn’t Everything
description: What does John Nash’s game theory equilibrium concept look like in Rock-Paper-Scissors?

title: Whisper From the First Stars Sets Off Loud Dark Matter Debate
description: A surprise discovery announced a month ago suggested that the early universe looked very different than previously believed. Initial theories that the discrepancy was due to dark matter have come under fire.

title: A Victory for Dark Matter in a Galaxy Without Any
description: Paradoxically, a small galaxy that seems to contain none of the invisible stuff known as “dark matter” may help prove that it exists.

title: Brains Cling to Old Habits When Learning New Tricks
description: Using a brain-computer interface, scientists are beginning to learn why learning is hard.

title: The Infinite Primes and Museum Guard Proofs, Explained
description: A simple, step-by-step breakdown of two “perfect” math proofs.

title: Black Hole Echoes Would Reveal Break With Einstein’s Theory
description: Gravitational waves have opened up new ways to test the properties of black holes — and Einstein’s theory of gravity along with them.

title: Complex Animals Led to More Oxygen, Says Maverick Theory
description: For decades, researchers have commonly assumed that higher oxygen levels led to the sudden diversification of animal life 540 million years ago. But one iconoclast argues the opposite: that new animal behaviors raised oxygen levels and remade the environment.

title: Robert Langlands, Mathematical Visionary, Wins the Abel Prize
description: Generations of researchers have pursued his “Langlands program,” which seeks to create a grand unified theory of mathematics.

title: In Search of God’s Perfect Proofs
description: The mathematicians Günter Ziegler and Martin Aigner have spent the past 20 years collecting some of the most beautiful proofs in mathematics.

title: Why Stephen Hawking’s Black Hole Puzzle Keeps Puzzling
description: The renowned British physicist, who died at 76, left behind a riddle that could eventually lead his successors to the theory of quantum gravity.

title: How Einstein Lost His Bearings, and With Them, General Relativity
description: By 1913, Albert Einstein had nearly completed general relativity. But a simple mistake set him on a tortured, two-year reconsideration of his theory. Today, mathematicians still grapple with the issues he confronted.

title: Brainless Embryos Suggest Bioelectricity Guides Growth
description: Researchers are building a case that long before the nervous system works, the brain sends crucial bioelectric signals to guide the growth of embryonic tissues.

title: Why the Tiny Weight of Empty Space Is Such a Huge Mystery
description: The amount of energy infusing empty space seems too small to explain without a multiverse. But physicists have at least one alternative left to explore.

title: To Test Einstein’s Equations, Poke a Black Hole
description: Two teams of researchers have made significant progress toward proving the black hole stability conjecture, a critical mathematical test of Einstein’s theory of general relativity.

title: Oxygen and Stem Cells May Have Reshaped Early Complex Animals
description: An unlikely team offers a controversial hypothesis about what enabled animal life to get more complex during the Cambrian explosion.

title: Physicists Find a Way to See the ‘Grin’ of Quantum Gravity
description: A recently proposed experiment would confirm that gravity is a quantum force.

title: New Giant Viruses Further Blur the Definition of Life
description: A newfound pair of giant viruses have massive genomes and the most complete resources for building proteins ever seen in the viral world. They have refreshed the debate about the origins of these cellular parasites.

title: Solution: ‘When Probability Meets Real Life’
description: When our brains don't have a good intuition for reasoning with numbers, explicit probabilistic thinking can lead to improved decision-making.

title: Why Don’t Patients Get Sick in Sync? Modelers Find Statistical Clues.
description: The long, variable times that some diseases incubate after infection defies simple explanation. An idealized model of tumor growth offers a statistical solution.

title: Elusive Higgs-Like State Created in Exotic Materials
description: Two teams of physicists have created the "Higgs mode" – a link between particle physics and the physics of matter. The work could help researchers understand the strange behavior of deeply quantum systems.

title: A Statistical Search for Genomic Truths
description: The computer scientist Barbara Engelhardt develops machine-learning models and methods to scour human genomes for the elusive causes and mechanisms of disease.

title: The Simple Algorithm That Ants Use to Build Bridges
description: Even with no one in charge, army ants work collectively to build bridges out of their bodies. New research reveals the simple rules that lead to such complex group behavior.

title: How Cells Pack Tangled DNA Into Neat Chromosomes
description: For the first time, researchers see how proteins grab loops of DNA and bundle them for cell division. The discovery also hints at how the genome folds to regulate gene expression.

title: Why Artificial Intelligence Like AlphaZero Has Trouble With the Real World
description: The latest artificial intelligence systems start from zero knowledge of a game and grow to world-beating in a matter of hours. But researchers are struggling to apply these systems beyond the arcade.

title: Physicists Mourn Joe Polchinski, Developer of Deep Ideas and Paradoxes
description: The theoretical physicist Joe Polchinski, who died February 2, left a tremendous professional and personal legacy, says a friend and collaborator.

title: Scant Evidence of Power Laws Found in Real-World Networks
description: A new study challenges one of the most celebrated and controversial ideas in network science.

title: Smart Swarms Seek New Ways to Cooperate
description: New algorithms show how swarms of very simple robots can be made to work together as a group.

title: Neutron Lifetime Puzzle Deepens, but No Dark Matter Seen
description: Two methods of measuring the neutron's longevity give different answers, creating uncertainty in cosmological models. But no one has a clue what the problem is.

title: Evolution Saves Species From ‘Kill the Winner’ Disasters
description: Modelers find evidence that a combination of competition, predation and evolution will push ecosystems toward species diversity anywhere in the universe.

title: When Probability Meets Real Life
description: When faced with a difficult decision, should you go with your gut or carefully calculate the attendant risks?

title: The Argument Against Quantum Computers
description: The mathematician Gil Kalai believes that quantum computers can't possibly work, even in principle.

title: With Strategic Zaps to the Brain, Scientists Boost Memory
description: Stimulating part of the cortex as needed during learning tasks improves later recall. The finding reveals more about the brain's memory network and points toward possible therapies.

title: How Math (and Vaccines) Keep You Safe From the Flu
description: Simple math shows how widespread vaccination can disrupt the exponential spread of disease and prevent epidemics.

title: Quantum Algorithms Struggle Against Old Foe: Clever Computers
description: The quest for "quantum supremacy" – unambiguous proof that a quantum computer does something faster than an ordinary computer – has paradoxically led to a boom in quasi-quantum classical algorithms.

title: How the Universe Got Its Bounce Back
description: Cosmologists have shown that it’s theoretically possible for a contracting universe to bounce and expand. The new work resuscitates an old idea that directly challenges the Big Bang theory of cosmic origins.

title: Solution: ‘Triangulation and Motion Sickness’
description: A method for estimating distances in sailing and astrophysics helps explain why riding on buses and boats can make us nauseous.

title: In Birds’ Songs, Brains and Genes, He Finds Clues to Speech
description: The neuroscientist Erich Jarvis found that songbirds' vocal skills and humans' spoken language are both rooted in neural pathways for controlling learned movements.

title: Job One for Quantum Computers: Boost Artificial Intelligence
description: The fusion of quantum computing and machine learning has become a booming research area. Can it possibly live up to its high expectations?

title: Tissue Engineers Hack Life’s Code for 3-D Folded Shapes
description: Mechanical tension between tethered cells cues developing tissues to fold. Researchers can now program synthetic tissue to make coils, cubes and rippling plates.

title: The Era of Quantum Computing Is Here. Outlook: Cloudy
description: Quantum computers should soon be able to beat classical computers at certain basic tasks. But before they’re truly powerful, researchers have to overcome a number of fundamental roadblocks.

title: A Domesticated Dingo? No, but Some Are Getting Less Wild
description: Near an Australian desert mining camp, wild dingoes are losing their fear of humans. Their genetic and behavioral changes may echo those from the domestication of dogs.

title: Fossil Discoveries Challenge Ideas About Earth’s Start
description: A series of fossil finds suggests that life on Earth started earlier than anyone thought, calling into question a widely held theory of the solar system’s beginnings.

title: Simpler Math Tames the Complexity of Microbe Networks
description: The dizzying network of interactions within microbe communities can defy analysis. But a new approach simplifies the math and makes progress possible.

title: A Neurobiologist Thinks Big — and Small
description: By developing new tools for visualizing subcellular structure and activity in molecular detail, Ed Boyden advances on his goal of understanding how the brain works.

title: What Makes the Hardest Equations in Physics So Difficult?
description: The Navier-Stokes equations describe simple, everyday phenomena, like water flowing from a garden hose, yet they provide a million-dollar mathematical challenge.

title: With ‘Downsized’ DNA, Flowering Plants Took Over the World
description: Compact genomes and tiny cells gave flowering plants an edge over competing flora. This discovery hints at a broader evolutionary principle.

title: Astronomers Trace Radio Burst to Extreme Cosmic Neighborhood
description: A mysterious object that repeatedly bursts with ultra-powerful radio waves must live in an extreme environment — something like the one around a supermassive black hole.

title: In Praise of Simple Problems
description: The mathematician Richard Schwartz finds the hidden depth lurking in simple mathematical puzzles.

title: Why an Old Theory of Everything Is Gaining New Life
description: For decades, physicists have struggled to create a quantum theory of gravity. Now an approach that dates to the 1970s is attracting newfound attention.

title: How Triangulation Leads to Knowledge
description: What does measuring distances in sailing and astrophysics have to with motion sickness?

title: Physicists Aim to Classify All Possible Phases of Matter
description: A complete classification could lead to a wealth of new materials and technologies. But some exotic phases continue to resist understanding.

title: Is a Bigger Genetic Code Better? Get Ready to Find Out
description: Evolution settled on a genetic code that uses four letters to name 20 amino acids. Synthetic biologists adding new bases to DNA will be free to improve on nature — if they can.

title: Quanta’s Science and Math Crossword Puzzle
description: This holiday season, catch up on science and math news while solving our year-end crossword.

title: Mathematicians Find Wrinkle in Famed Fluid Equations
description: Two mathematicians prove that under certain extreme conditions, the Navier-Stokes equations output nonsense.

title: A Mathematician Who Decodes the Patterns Stamped Out by Life
description: Corina Tarnita deciphers bizarre patterns in the soil created by competing life-forms.

title: The End of the RNA World Is Near, Biochemists Argue
description: For decades, an origin-of-life story starring RNA has prevailed. New research may be shaking that theory’s hold on our understanding of life’s beginnings.

title: Why Is M-Theory the Leading Candidate for Theory of Everything?
description: The mother of all string theories passes a litmus test that, so far, no other candidate theory of quantum gravity has been able to match.

title: Light-Triggered Genes Reveal the Hidden Workings of Memory
description: Nobel laureate Susumu Tonegawa’s lab is overturning old assumptions about how memories form, how recall works and whether lost memories might be restored from "silent engrams."

title: New Bird Species Arises From Hybrids, as Scientists Watch
description: The rapid, unorthodox emergence of a new finch in the Galápagos hints that speciation isn’t rare. New hybrid species may quietly appear and disappear without anyone noticing.

title: Neutrinos Suggest Solution to Mystery of Universe’s Existence
description: Updated results from a Japanese neutrino experiment continue to reveal an inconsistency in the way that matter and antimatter behave.

title: The (Math) Problem With Pentagons
description: Triangles fit effortlessly together, as do squares. When it comes to pentagons, what gives?

title: Solution: ‘Triumph or Cooperation in Game Theory and Evolution’
description: How well does the Nash equilibrium concept from game theory map to the real world?

title: Mathematicians Crack the Cursed Curve
description: A famously difficult mathematical problem resisted solution for over 40 years. Mathematicians have finally resolved it by following an intuition that links number theory to physics.

title: Earliest Black Hole Gives Rare Glimpse of Ancient Universe
description: It weighs as much as 780 million suns and helped to cast off the cosmic Dark Ages. But now that astronomers have found the earliest known black hole, they wonder: How could this giant have grown so big, so fast?

title: What Bacteria Can Tell Us About Human Evolution
description: To discover our species’ deep history and to shape its future health, we should learn from the microbes that accompanied us on our evolutionary journey.

title: Plunge Into a (Virtual Reality) Black Hole
description: Join a fleet of robotic probes on a one-way virtual-reality trip into the abyss of a massive black hole.

title: Secret Link Uncovered Between Pure Math and Physics
description: An eminent mathematician reveals that his advances in the study of millennia-old mathematical questions owe to concepts derived from physics.

title: How Bacteria Help Regulate Blood Pressure
description: Kidneys sniff out signals from gut bacteria for cues to lower blood pressure after meals. Our understanding of how the symbiotic microbes affect health is becoming much more molecular.

title: A Physicist’s Physicist Ponders the Nature of Reality
description: Edward Witten reflects on the meaning of dualities in physics and math, emergent space-time, and the pursuit of a complete description of nature.

title: The Overlooked Link Between Two of This Year’s Nobel Prizes
description: To better understand the molecules described by the latest prize in medicine, we will need the technique recognized by the latest prize in chemistry.

title: Bacteria Sacrifice DNA Repair for Better RNA
description: Preserving its DNA ought to be a cell’s top priority. But bacteria slow their DNA repair to a crawl in favor of proofreading gene transcripts.

title: Hidden Supercluster Could Solve Milky Way Mystery
description: Astronomers generally stay away from the “Zone of Avoidance.” When one astronomer didn’t, she found a giant cosmic structure that could help explain why our galaxy moves so fast.

title: A Mathematician Who Dances to the Joys and Sorrows of Discovery
description: Federico Ardila opens up about his journey as a mathematician, teacher, Colombian transplant, DJ and creator of mathematical spaces.

title: Deathblow Dealt to Dark Matter Disks
description: New data tracking the movements of millions of Milky Way stars have effectively ruled out the presence of a “dark disk” that could have offered important clues to the mystery of dark matter.

title: New Model Warns About CRISPR Gene Drives in the Wild
description: Two new papers urge caution in using powerful genome-editing technology against invasive species: Models show that aggressive gene drives can’t be contained in the wild.

title: Choosy Eggs May Pick Sperm for Their Genes, Defying Mendel’s Law
description: The oldest law of genetics says that gametes combine randomly, but experiments hint that sometimes eggs select sperm actively for their genetic assets.

title: Galactic Glow, Thought to Be Dark Matter, Now Hints at Hidden Pulsars
description: A number of high-energy anomalies raised hopes that astrophysicists had seen their first direct glimpses of dark matter. New studies suggest a different source may be responsible.

title: Seeing the Beautiful Intelligence of Microbes
description: Bacterial biofilms and slime molds are more than crude patches of goo. Detailed time-lapse microscopy reveals how they sense and explore their surroundings, communicate with their neighbors and adaptively reshape themselves.

title: How to Triumph and Cooperate in Game Theory and Evolution
description: In applying game theory to biology and human behavior, have scientists focused too much on competition over cooperation?

title: ‘Crazy’ Supernova Looks Like a New Kind of Star Death
description: Astronomers are mystified by a strange star explosion in a distant galaxy that might be a relic from an earlier cosmological era.

title: A Zombie Gene Protects Elephants From Cancer
description: Elephants did not evolve to become huge animals until after they turned a bit of genetic junk into a unique defense against inevitable tumors.

title: From the Edge of the Universe to the Inside of a Proton
description: The Zoomable Universe, a new book by the astrobiologist Caleb Scharf, the illustrator Ron Miller and 5W Infographics, tours the universe’s 62 orders of magnitude.

title: Solution: ‘How to Win at Deep Learning’
description: When equipped with hidden layers, deep neural networks can accomplish nonlinear feats that are difficult even with sophisticated mathematics.

title: Life’s First Molecule Was Protein, Not RNA, New Model Suggests
description: Which mattered first at the dawn of life: proteins or nucleic acids? Proteins may have had the edge if a theorized process let them grow long enough to become self-replicating catalysts.

title: How to Build a Robot That Wants to Change the World
description: And not destroy humanity in the process.

description: Imagine the fabric of space-time peeled back layer by layer.

title: How Quantum Pairs Stitch Space-Time
description: New tools may reveal how quantum information builds the structure of space.

title: Wormholes Untangle a Black Hole Paradox
description: A bold new idea aims to link two famously discordant descriptions of nature. In doing so, it may also reveal how space-time owes its existence to the spooky connections of quantum information.

title: Concerns of an Artificial Intelligence Pioneer
description: Computer scientist Stuart Russell wants to ensure that our increasingly intelligent machines remain aligned with human values.

title: How Structure Arose in the Primordial Soup
description: Life’s first epoch saw incredible advances — cells, metabolism and DNA, to name a few. Researchers are resurrecting ancient proteins to illuminate the biological dark ages.

title: For Persi Diaconis’ Next Magic Trick …
description: A mathematician who has analyzed card shuffling for decades is tackling one final nemesis: “smooshing.”

title: A Grand Theory of Wrinkles
description: A collaboration between mechanical engineers and mathematicians has revealed universal rules for how wrinkles form.

title: After Prime Proof, an Unlikely Star Rises
description: Two years ago, Yitang Zhang was virtually unknown. Now his surprise solution to a major problem in number theory has catapulted him to mathematical stardom. Where does he go from here?

title: Dark Energy Tested on a Tabletop
description: Is dark energy a cosmic chameleon that can fade into its surroundings? A recent test brings the mysterious anti-gravitational force down to earth.

title: Did Neurons Evolve Twice?
description: The comb jelly, a primitive marine creature, is forcing scientists to rethink how animals got their start.

title: ‘Penguin’ Anomaly Hints at Missing Particles
description: A statistical anomaly in the signal from rare particle decays at the Large Hadron Collider offers hope that new discoveries might be around the corner.

title: Science’s Path From Myth to Multiverse
description: In his latest book, the Nobel Prize winner Steven Weinberg explores how science made the modern world, and where it might take us from here.

title: Mathematicians Chase Moonshine’s Shadow
description: Researchers are on the trail of a mysterious connection between number theory, algebra and string theory.

title: Strange Stars Pulse to the Golden Mean
description: Nature has revealed peculiar mathematical objects that connect order and chaos.

title: In LHC’s Shadow, America’s Collider Awakens
description: The Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider fired up for its 15th run to take a deeper look at the building blocks of atoms.

title: Killer Virus Is Invading Koala DNA
description: An infection sweeping through Australia’s struggling koala population provides an unprecedented opportunity to explore how retroviruses insert themselves into the genome.

title: Genetic Geometry Takes Shape
description: Inside the cell’s nucleus, the double helix folds up in myriad loops and twists. The quest to unravel this structure is revealing the subtle genetic orchestration of all life on Earth.

title: In Fake Universes, Evidence for String Theory
description: If string theorists can show that their framework is the only consistent theory of quantum gravity, does that make it true even without tangible evidence?

title: Game Theory Calls Cooperation Into Question
description: A new solution to the prisoner’s dilemma, a classic game theory scenario, has created new puzzles in evolutionary biology.

title: Breakthrough DNA Editor Born of Bacteria
description: Interest in a powerful DNA editing tool called CRISPR has revealed that bacteria are far more sophisticated than anyone imagined.

title: Joint Dust Analysis Deflates Big Bang Signal
description: No definitive evidence for cosmic inflation is found, but support remains strong for the theory even as critics highlight its shortcomings as an explanation for how and why the universe began.

title: Networks Reveal the Connections of Disease
description: Disease is the result of failure somewhere along the line in a complex dance of biological components. Now statistical physicists are using enormous databases of medical records to study connections between illnesses.

title: Quantum Computing Without Qubits
description: A quantum computing pioneer explains why the near future of quantum computation may lie in simulators, not general-purpose quantum machines.

title: A Proof That Some Spaces Can’t Be Cut
description: Mathematicians have solved the century-old triangulation conjecture, a major problem in topology that asks whether all spaces can be subdivided into smaller units.

title: Scientists Conjure Curves From Flatness
description: Researchers have found a set of rules for imbuing flat surfaces with curvature, enabling them to form a virtually unlimited range of three-dimensional structures.

title: Machine Intelligence Cracks Genetic Controls
description: Scientists have begun to decipher the most difficult-to-read parts of the genome — the parts that don’t code for proteins. The new work reveals how errors in these genetic instructions can lead to disease.

title: Prime Gap Grows After Decades-Long Lull
description: A year after tackling how close together prime number pairs can stay, mathematicians have now made the first major advance in 76 years in understanding how far apart primes can be.

title: A Common Logic to Seeing Cats and Cosmos
description: New research suggests physicists, computers and brains employ the same procedure to tease out important features from among other irrelevant bits of data.

title: New Twist Found in the Story of Life’s Start
description: All life on Earth is made of molecules that twist in the same direction. New research reveals that this may not always have been so.

title: Ancient Survivors Could Redefine Sex
description: Microscopic creatures called bdelloid rotifers have thrived without mating for millions of years. How they did it could reveal why sex is so essential for almost everyone else.

title: Multiverse Collisions May Dot the Sky
kicker: Infinity and Beyond: The Ultimate Test
description: Early in cosmic history, our universe may have bumped into another — a primordial clash that could have left traces in the Big Bang’s afterglow.

title: In a Multiverse, What Are the Odds?
kicker: Infinity and Beyond: The Ultimate Test
description: Testing the multiverse hypothesis requires measuring whether our universe is statistically typical among the infinite variety of universes. But infinity does a number on statistics.

title: Dwarf Galaxies Dim Hopes of Dark Matter
description: For five years physicists have been tantalized by possible evidence of dark matter in the Milky Way’s center. But new results from small satellite galaxies have complicated the story.

title: Mental Leaps Cued by Memory’s Ripples
description: The same mental processes that organize memories may also coordinate how we make decisions.

title: At the Far Ends of a New Universal Law
description: A potent theory has emerged explaining a mysterious statistical law that arises throughout physics and mathematics.

title: Brain’s Positioning System Linked to Memory
description: The 2014 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded to three researchers who discovered how the brain navigates the world. Their work may also help illuminate how the mind stores memories.

title: Elusive Form of Evolution Seen in Spiders
description: A study of diverse colonies of spiders supports a controversial idea in evolution — that natural selection can act on communities as well as on individuals.

title: Lizard Stowaways Revise Principle of Ecology
description: The movement of lizards around the Caribbean is forcing researchers to account for human activity in even their most basic ecological models.

title: ‘Big Bang Signal’ Could All Be Dust
description: Cosmic dust in the high latitudes of the Milky Way could account for the entire swirl pattern that had been presented as proof of a leading Big Bang theory, according to a new data analysis from the Planck satellite.

title: Finding Dark Energy in the Details
description: The astrophysicist Joshua Frieman seeks to pinpoint the mysterious substance driving the accelerating expansion of the universe.

title: Evolution’s Random Paths Lead to One Place
description: A massive statistical study suggests that even though genetic changes happen at random, the final evolutionary outcome — fitness — is predictable.

title: The Thermodynamic Theory of Ecology
description: Nature’s large-scale patterns emerge from incomplete surveys that borrow ideas from information theory.

title: Quark Quartet Fuels Quantum Feud
description: Newly discovered particles are forcing physicists to extend their simple picture of subatomic interactions or replace it with a more nuanced understanding.

title: I Contain Multitudes
description: Our bodies are a genetic patchwork, possessing variation from cell to cell. Is that a good thing?

title: At Multiverse Impasse, a New Theory of Scale
description: Physicists have begun to explore the idea that mass and length may not be fundamental properties of nature. The hypothesis could help to avoid the conclusion that our world is just a weird bubble in an endlessly foaming multiverse.

title: A Grand Vision for the Impossible
description: Subhash Khot’s bold conjecture is helping mathematicians explore the precise limits of computation.

title: In Noisy Equations, One Who Heard Music
description: Martin Hairer was named a 2014 Fields medalist for an epic masterpiece in stochastic analysis that colleagues say “created a whole world.”

title: A Tenacious Explorer of Abstract Surfaces
description: Maryam Mirzakhani, who became the first woman Fields medalist for drawing deep connections between topology, geometry and dynamical systems, has died of cancer at the age of 40. This is our 2014 profile of her life and work.

title: A Brazilian Wunderkind Who Calms Chaos
description: Artur Avila’s solutions to ubiquitous problems in chaos theory have “changed the face of the field,” earning him Brazil’s first Fields Medal.

title: The Musical, Magical Number Theorist
description: The search for artistic truth and beauty has led Manjul Bhargava to some of the most profound recent discoveries in number theory, which have helped earn him the Fields Medal.

title: As Animals Mingle, a Baffling Genetic Barrier
description: Despite swapping DNA through interbreeding, butterflies and other animals can maintain distinct species.

title: Where Animals Come From
description: Bacteria may have helped single-celled organisms make the leap to multicellular animals.

title: In Search of Dark Stars
description: Katherine Freese, a physicist who will soon lead the Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics, reflects on the hunt for dark matter and how dark matter heating may have produced the first stars.

title: The New Science of Evolutionary Forecasting
description: Newly discovered patterns in evolution may help scientists make accurate short-term predictions.

title: Hints of Life’s Start Found in a Giant Virus
description: Newly discovered specimens support a more ancient origin for viruses, perhaps all the way back to the origins of life.

title: A Bold Critic of the Big Bang’s ‘Smoking Gun’
description: The cosmologist David Spergel explains why a widely publicized gravitational-wave discovery could be wrong, and how the “overreaching” study could affect the public’s perception of science.

title: Early-Universe Explorer Looks for Answers
description: Chao-Lin Kuo, who helped design the experiment that claimed to have found evidence of gravitational waves from the Big Bang, isn’t bothered by criticism that cosmic dust may account for his results.

title: Fluid Tests Hint at Concrete Quantum Reality
description: Surprising oil drop experiments suggest that the quantum world may not be as strange as advertised.

title: The Game Theory of Life
description: An insight borrowed from computer science suggests that evolution values both fitness and diversity.

title: In a Grain, a Glimpse of the Cosmos
description: When scientists traced a museum rock back to its origins, they uncovered mysteries about the early solar system.

title: Evolving With a Little Help From Our Friends
description: A new theory suggests that cooperation between a host and its microbes may be a significant evolutionary force.

title: Physicists Prove Surprising Rule of Threes
description: Three groups of experimentalists have independently observed a strange state of matter that forms from three particles of any type and at any scale, from practically infinitesimal to infinite.

title: Inside the Din, Cells Fight Noise With Noise
description: Is the random noise inside a cell a nuisance, or have cells evolved ways to put it to work?

title: Forging a Qubit to Rule Them All
description: A scientist at Bell Labs has started construction of a topological qubit, which could be the building block of a robust, scalable quantum computer.

title: In Bees, a Hunt for Roots of Social Behavior
description: By comparing the genomes of social and solitary bees, scientists hope to uncover the basis for communal behavior.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Superconductivity
description: Experimentalists have pinpointed the microscopic structure of waves inside high-temperature superconductors, which could be the key to understanding the complex materials.

title: Early Life in Death Valley
description: Evidence from Southwestern deserts suggests that oxygen-breathing organisms arose on land rather than in the seas.

title: Time’s Arrow Traced to Quantum Source
description: A new theory explains the seemingly irreversible arrow of time while yielding insights into entropy, quantum computers, black holes, and the past-future divide.

title: The Remarkable Self-Organization of Ants
description: Knowing the rules behind ant-made structures could help scientists understand how other complex systems emerge in nature.

title: A Fundamental Theory to Model the Mind
description: Support is growing for a decades-old physics idea suggesting that localized episodes of disordered brain activity help keep the overall system in healthy balance.

title: A ‘Rebel’ Without a Ph.D.
description: A conversation with the mathematical physicist Freeman Dyson on quantum electrodynamics, climate change and his latest pet project.

title: Possible Echo of Big Bang Detected
description: Scientists report the possible discovery of primordial gravitational waves, ripples in space-time that carry a record of how the universe began.

title: Betting on the Future of Quantum Gravity
description: New calculations suggest physicists may someday discover a fundamental theory of gravity, but it could require a radical new perspective on the universe.

title: Does Competition Drive Diversity of Species?
description: A large new study of ovenbird lineages questions the extent to which competing species push each other to evolve.

title: Case for Dark Matter Signal Strengthens
description: A new analysis strengthens the case that gamma rays emanating from the center of the Milky Way come from dark matter particles known as WIMPs.

title: A Fluid New Path in Grand Math Challenge
description: A daring speculation offers a potential way forward in one of the great unsolved problems of mathematics: the behavior of the Navier-Stokes equations for fluid flow.

title: Scientists Reveal Structure of Pain Sensor
description: Scientists have finally resolved the structure of the molecule that responds to chili peppers, high temperatures and spider toxins.

title: Big Bang Secrets Swirling in a Fluid Universe
description: With a new approach that treats the universe as a fluid, cosmologists plan to tease out the fine details of the Big Bang from its behavior and evolution.

title: Chemists Seek Possible Precursor to RNA
description: Scientists have discovered building blocks similar to those in modern RNA that can effortlessly assemble when mixed in water and heated.

title: Perfecting the Art of Sensible Nonsense
description: In a watershed moment for cryptography, computer scientists have proposed a solution to a fundamental problem called “program obfuscation.”

title: A New Physics Theory of Life
description: An MIT physicist has proposed the provocative idea that life exists because the law of increasing entropy drives matter to acquire lifelike physical properties.

title: Under Pressure, Does Evolution Evolve?
description: Some organisms respond to stress by driving up their mutation rate. Are they evolving specific mechanisms to enhance evolution in times of crisis?

title: A Missing Genetic Link in Human Evolution
description: Mysterious episodes of genetic duplication in our great ape ancestors may have paved the way for human evolution.

title: A New Tool to Help Mathematicians Pack
description: Improvements in how densely spheres and other shapes can be packed together could lead to advances in materials science, deep space communication and theoretical physics.

title: The Secret Language of Plants
description: Striking evidence that plants warn each other of environmental dangers is reviving a once ridiculed field.

title: Could Knots Unravel Mysteries of Fluid Flow?
description: By investigating the central role played by knots in fluids and fields, physicists hope to unravel long-standing mysteries of turbulence.

title: Inside a Brain Circuit, the Will to Press On
description: A rare brain stimulation study suggests that a brain circuit known as the “salience network” contributes to differences in our ability to overcome challenges and cope with stress.

title: To Settle Infinity Dispute, a New Law of Logic
description: To determine the nature of infinity, mathematicians face a choice between two new logical axioms. What they decide could help shape the future of mathematical truth.

title: Together and Alone, Closing the Prime Gap
description: Working on the centuries-old twin primes conjecture, two solitary researchers and a massive collaboration have made enormous advances over the last six months.

title: Tracking the Evolution of Cancer, Cell by Cell
description: Analyzing individual cancer cells could reveal the answer to some of the disease’s most enduring mysteries.

title: RNA’s Secret Life Outside the Cell
description: Circulating RNAs carry messages for plants and invertebrates. Do they do the same for us?

title: Physicists Eye Quantum-Gravity Interface
description: Physicists have devised experiments that can probe the interface between quantum mechanics and general relativity.

title: In Brain’s ‘Rich Club,’ Meetings of the Mind
description: Neuroscientists have identified a network of highly linked brain regions that could prove essential in integrating information and facilitating higher-order cognitive tasks.

title: Search Escalates for Key to Why Matter Exists
description: Physicists have completed a new round of searches for the answer to why matter dominates over antimatter. But the radioactive decay that would solve the puzzle is evading them.

title: The Future Fabric of Data Analysis
kicker: Data Driven: The New Big Science
description: The nature of computing has changed dramatically over the last decade, and more innovation is needed to weather the gathering data storm.

title: Our Bodies, Our Data
kicker: Data Driven: The New Big Science
description: New technologies have launched the life sciences into the age of big data. Biologists must now make sense of their windfall.

title: The Mathematical Shape of Things to Come
kicker: Data Driven: The New Big Science
description: Scientific data sets are becoming more dynamic, requiring new mathematical techniques on par with the invention of calculus.

title: A Digital Copy of the Universe, Encrypted
kicker: Data Driven: The New Big Science
description: As physics prepares for ambitious projects like the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope, the field is seeking new methods of data-driven discovery.

title: Imagining Data Without Division
kicker: Data Driven: The New Big Science
description: As science dives headlong into an ocean of data, the demands of large-scale interdisciplinary collaborations are growing increasingly acute.

title: Debating the Evolution of Multicellularity
description: An interview with the developmental biologist Cassandra Extavour on the origins of multicellular organisms and the evolution of cooperation.

title: A Jewel at the Heart of Quantum Physics
description: Physicists have discovered a jewel-shaped geometric object that challenges the notion that space and time are fundamental constituents of nature.

title: Evolution as Opportunist
description: A computational study reveals surprising flexibility hidden within metabolic networks, providing new evidence for an evolutionary concept called exaptation.

title: Decoding Flu Viruses Before an Outbreak
description: Machine learning techniques are helping scientists pinpoint the mutations that allow bird and pig viruses to infect humans.

title: The Proof in the Quantum Pudding
description: How do you know if a quantum computer is doing what it claims? A new protocol offers a possible solution and a boost to quantum cryptography.

title: In Natural Networks, Strength in Loops
description: In the complex architecture that ferries fluids in plants and brains, scientists are finding a model of resilience.

title: Physicists Close In on ‘Perfect’ Optical Lens
description: Researchers are making progress toward a “perfect lens” that will be able to resolve an organelle assembling a protein or a virus attacking a cell.

title: On the Microbial Frontier, Cooperation Thrives
description: Population expansion may be a major driver in the evolution of cooperation, with implications for new antibiotics, cancer treatments and perhaps even human behavior.

title: In Pursuit of Quantum Biology With Birgitta Whaley
description: An interview with the Berkeley chemist K. Birgitta Whaley on the promise and challenge of translating quantum biology into practical quantum devices.

title: As Machines Get Smarter, Evidence They Learn Like Us
description: Studies show that computer models called "neural networks" behave strikingly similar to actual brains when performing certain tasks, suggesting the two may learn in the same way.

title: In the Hunt for Dark Matter, Promises to Keep?
description: Whispers of the elusive particles are becoming stronger with a series of signals that appear to be zeroing in on a leading contender.

title: The Surprising Origins of Life’s Complexity
description: Scientists are exploring how organisms can evolve elaborate structures without Darwinian selection.

title: Mathematicians Shed Light on Minimalist Conjecture
description: Two young mathematicians are illuminating a frontier in the study of rational solutions to polynomial equations: the cubics.

title: Signs of a Stranger, Deeper Side to Nature’s Building Blocks
description: New findings suggest that beneath the surface of quantum theory lies a vibrant string theory world where some matter corresponds to black holes in higher dimensions.

title: In Lopsided Map of the Cosmos, a Glimmer of Its Origins
description: Theoretical cosmologists are piecing together a cosmic origin story from a surprising anomaly in the recently released Planck satellite image.

title: Tiny Genomes May Offer Clues to First Plants and Animals
description: Symbiotic bacteria that dwell within insect cells are intricately intertwined with their hosts, prompting scientists to question when these bacteria stop being bona fide organisms and become part of the cell.

title: A New Approach to Building the Tree of Life
description: More genetic data is available than ever before to help build evolutionary trees, but scientists are finding that different genes even in the same organism can tell conflicting stories.

title: Is Nature Unnatural?
description: Decades of confounding experiments have physicists considering a startling possibility: The universe might not make sense.

title: Waiting for the Revolution
description: An interview with the Nobel Prize-winner David J. Gross on the confusing state of theoretical physics.

title: Unheralded Mathematician Bridges the Prime Gap
description: A virtually unknown researcher has made a great advance in one of mathematics’ oldest problems, the twin primes conjecture.

title: Perpetual Motion Test Could Amend Theory of Time
description: A radical theory predicting the existence of “time crystals” — perpetual motion objects that break the symmetry of time — is being put to the test.

title: Scientists Parse Ocean’s Dynamic Role in Climate Change
description: New data collected by mathematicians and oceanographers in the frigid waters of the Southern Ocean could dramatically improve climate models.

title: Solid or Liquid? Physicists Redefine States of Matter
description: Glass and other strange materials have long confounded textbook definitions of what it means to be solid. Now, two groups of physicists propose a new solution to the riddle.

title: Biologists Home In on Turing Patterns
description: New research has prompted a resurgence of interest in the patterning mechanisms Alan Turing proposed 60 years ago.

title: Treading Softly in a Connected World
description: In an increasingly interconnected world, scientists are seeking safeguards against catastrophic cascades of failure like stock market crashes and widespread blackouts.

title: Peering Into the Early Universe
description: Three “extremely large telescopes” poised to begin observations within a decade could help answer some of the universe’s oldest and best-kept secrets.

title: How to Make Impossible Wallpaper
description: A new collection of arresting wallpaper designs seems to defy the crystallographic restriction.

title: In Computers We Trust?
description: As the role of computers in pure mathematics grows, researchers debate their reliability.

title: In Mysterious Pattern, Math and Nature Converge
description: All complex correlated systems, from Arctic melt ponds to the Internet, appear to be governed by the same math as a random matrix.

title: Computer Scientists Take Road Less Traveled
description: An infinitesimal advance in the traveling salesman problem breathes new life into the search for improved approximate solutions.

title: Hunger Game: Is Honesty Between Animals Always the Best Policy?
description: Game theorists have developed a new model of communication among animals. It suggests evolution will produce a situation in which members of a species are honest most of the time, but not always.

title: Alice and Bob Meet the Wall of Fire
description: If a new hypothesis about black hole firewalls proves correct, at least one of three cherished notions in theoretical physics must be wrong.

title: Classical Computing Embraces Quantum Ideas
description: Computer scientists are finding that “thinking quantumly” can lead to new insights into long-standing problems in classical computer science, mathematics and cryptography, regardless of whether quantum computers ever materialize.

title: Privacy by the Numbers: A New Approach to Safeguarding Data
description: A mathematical technique called “differential privacy” gives researchers access to vast repositories of personal data while meeting a high standard for privacy protection.

title: A Primordial Nucleus Behind the Elements of Life
description: Using supercomputers and new mathematical techniques, physicists are working to reveal how the Hoyle state atomic nucleus gives rise to the light elements that enable life, and how it drives the evolution of stars.

title: As Supersymmetry Fails Tests, Physicists Seek New Ideas
description: As the elegant theory of supersymmetry continues to fail experimental tests, physicists debate whether to change course and what the future holds for particle physics.

title: Getting Into Shapes: From Hyperbolic Geometry to Cube Complexes and Back
description: Thirty years after William Thurston articulated a grand mathematical vision, a proof by Ian Agol marks the end of an era in the study of three-dimensional shapes.
